title: GPU FLIP: Solve Level above 0 jitters and the water disappears
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-07, Water — Dam Break (GPU FLIP) layer in the app): raising the Fluid > Solve Level param above 0 makes the water jitter heavily and then vanish. Solve Level 0 is stable. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: the multigrid/solve-level path in the GPU FLIP pressure solve (coarser levels, restriction/prolongation, or the sparse-block/narrow-band interaction at coarse levels); particle positions blowing up to NaN or leaving the domain after a diverged pressure step; max-iterations cap reached at coarse level. Fix shape: reproduce headlessly (fluid_capture with Solve Level 1 and 2 via gpu_queue), dump per-step pressure residual and particle count per frame, find the first diverging step, fix at the root. Pairs with GPU_FLIP_SPARSE_BLOCKS and GPU_FLIP_NARROW_BAND design work.

title: GPU FLIP coupled bodies: light and floating boxes never come to rest
description: One family, likely one root: the water push on a coupled box is noisy tick to tick, and light boxes amplify it. FLIP Fluids has no two-way rigid coupling, so this layer is ours (MANIFOLD-owned rigid coupling in the CPU engine, GPU FLIP matched to it only on short reaction scenes). No proof covers a light box settling over a long run. First step: a GPU FLIP light-body settling proof (energy and rest speed over 30 s at densities 20, 100, 500), then the root. Members: light boxes never settle, floating boxes bob high, corner lift-off, stack wobble, drain under a light box, sideways creep, tank-wide slab run-up.

title: Box3D hull cook traps the app on a photoscan Collision Proxy
description: Symptom: fluid_role_source with Geometry Collision Proxy on coastal_cliff_02 (Poly Haven), fragment_count 8 / fragment_index 3, any collider_parts (64, 48, 40), kills the process with SIGTRAP and no message, at preset load. Crash stack: b3InternalAssert <- b3HullBuilder_NewFace <- b3CreateHull <- manifold_box3d_cook_hull <- manifold_physics::cook_hull <- physics_mesh::prepare_colliders <- fluid_role_source::geometry::prepare_geometry. Root cause: B3_ASSERT(b->faceCount < b->faceCapacity) in crates/manifold-physics/native/box3d/src/hull.c b3HullBuilder_NewFace: quickhull on the near-coplanar shell points prepare_colliders makes (each scan triangle offset +-0.05% of the extent) creates more interim faces than the pool holds. Asserts are compiled in, so release traps too. Fix shape: size the face/edge pools from the input point count (or grow them) and return a NULL hull instead of asserting, so cook_hull reports PhysicsError and the role falls back or errors by name; add a CPU test that cooks piece 3 of the scan. Stopgap in OceanCliff.json: the right gully wall uses pieces 5 and 4 instead of 3.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Ocean Cliff ships with fragment 3 (the crashing one) and fragment 1 without colliders. BUG-js61b (liquid colliders from the scan) would make fixed colliders skip the hull cook entirely; this bead stays for moving Box3D bodies.

title: GPU FLIP pushes a light box tilted into a corner down instead of up (lost wet gap)
description: Symptom: liquid_lift_off on GPU FLIP. A density-0.3 box, 0.4 m, tilted 0.3 rad with one bottom edge on the floor and one side edge on the -x wall, under 1 m of water (48 cells, dx 0.05). From the first tick the reaction points down and into the wall (tick 1: J = (-8.7, -2.6, 0.1) N*s at 30 Hz, L_z = +1.5; fully wetted hydrostatic reference is about (0, +20.9, 0)). The box is slammed flat into the corner within about 20 ticks and stays pinned with J about (-52, -48, 0) per tick: pressure on its top and +x faces, none on its bottom and -x faces. MPM lifts the same box by tick 21. Failing before the body handoff work too (P13 red run: 39% water lost; now 0.08%, 49307 refused push-outs summed over ticks). Root cause unknown. Leading suspect (Astra consult 2026-10-06): the thin wet gap under and beside the box is lost on the grid: liquid_fill seeding, phi_into_solids only extends wetness near existing particles, open_fractions corner sampling, or closest_body giving gap faces to the wall instead of the body. Decisive check: capture the first pressure solve on the wedge cells and their faces before any motion (particle count, phi/water, open volume, face fraction, owner, pressure, signed face_impulse) and sum by body side. A dry wedge confirms the wet-mask cause; wet cells with collapsed geometry or wall ownership point elsewhere. Reference for unresolved thin gaps: Qiu, Yu, Fedkiw 2015. Also blocks the tilted fixture in liquid_handover_agreement. Conformance exemptions to remove when fixed: GPU FLIP LiftOff and HandoverAgreement in liquid/conformance.rs.

title: GPU FLIP: light coupled boxes never settle in still water
description: Symptom (measured 2026-10-06, still 1 m pool, res 32, Sim Rate 30, Peter's waterLossTest box 0.5x1x0.75 m): at density 20 and 100 the floating box keeps moving at a median 0.25 and 0.23 m/s for the full 60 s in dead-still water; at 2000 it rests under 1 mm/s. Conformance floating draft (density 0.5) bobs 2.6 cm. Root cause unknown. Suspects: the water reaction applied as one lumped impulse per tick (BUG-ar2ds), the pose predictor mismatch (BUG-g75v.18), solve error amplified by 1/m. No GPU FLIP proof covers light bodies beyond a 40 m/s bound: GPU FLIP is exempt from liquid_coupling_collision (fee40da3c), which also dropped its energy half. Fix shape: first a GPU FLIP light-body energy/settling proof, then the root.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Measured 2026-10-06, still 1 m pool, density 100, median body speed (|v|+|w|r above g*dt) over 30-60 s: Sim Rate 60 0.138 m/s, 30 0.228, 15 0.537; res 64 at 30 Hz 0.206 (resolution-independent). Density 20: 0.183 at 60, 0.257 at 30. Water lost while floating: 0/s at 60, 87/s at 30, 490/s at 15. Scales with tick length, not grid: the water/Box3D handover. Predicted fake sinking speed from impulse-first-then-gravity (BUG-g75v.18) g*dt*(N-1)/(2N) = 0.061/0.143/0.307; measured is 1.5-2.3x that, so it is the main part, not all. Body position was not logged: visible motion versus reported speed is unverified.

title: Main red: a 128 still pool gains 4.8 cm/s in two ticks
description: Symptom: liquid_conformance::liquid_live_700ms_frame_preserves_128_pool_and_matches_two_fixed_steps fails on main 1a7fe1437: resting water gained speed 0.0478 m/s (limit 1 mm/s) after two ticks of the GPU FLIP still pool at resolution 128. The overloaded run still matches two fixed steps bitwise, so the drift is in the step itself, not the clock. Reproduced identically on feat/flip-display-cursor (same number), so the display delay is not the cause. Root cause: unknown. Suspect: the pressure cap landing 323f3c230 (cap 900, round template, chunked rounds guarded after the tolerance stop) — the test is in liquid_conformance, which that landing gate did not run. Next: run the test at 323f3c230^1 to bisect; if pressure, compare residual and rounds executed at 128 against the pre-template solve. Fix shape: TBD after bisect.
notes: Astra (read-only, 2026-10-06): STALE EXPECTATION. The test was written for the two-interval clock cap (6079d6f26); its 1 mm/s speed limit was copied from gpu_flip_still_pool, which the walls-parity landing 14ebf56da deliberately replaced with native measurements (native peak 18.89 mm/s, bound 20.99 mm/s at 64, frames 59-119) because native water never fully rests. The overload part of this test (two ticks, count kept, finite, bitwise equal to two fixed steps) passes and still guards what the test is for. But the 64 bound does not certify 47.8 mm/s at 128 after two ticks. Fix shape: keep count, finiteness and bitwise two-step equality; replace the speed/energy limits only after one CPU FLIP Fluids reference run at 128 for two ticks with matched particles, walls and timestep, the way gpu_flip_still_pool was re-derived. No bisect.
close_reason: Stale 1 mm/s limit dropped; overload contract kept (Peter approved). Claude lead

title: land_branch --named-red covers every red leg, so an unrelated real failure lands silently
description: Symptom: the sheeting landing (lane/sheeting-oracle, 2026-10-06) was landed with --named-red BUG-j9l9w for a GPU-proofs time-budget overrun, but the same GPU-proofs leg also had a real failure, gpu_flip_sheeting_off_leaves_the_dam_break_unchanged (stale whole-step digest after the walls landing). The lead read the leg as budget-only; the tool accepted the whole leg. main was then red on that test and blocked the next two landings. Root cause: the named red binds to the gate run, not to the specific failure; a leg that fails for two reasons is covered by one reason. Fix shape: --named-red takes the failure it covers (a test id, or "budget"); land_branch parses the leg transcript and refuses when any other failed test or drift is present, printing the uncovered failures. Applies to the tests legs too.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Second incident 2026-10-06: the pressure cap landing used --named-red BUG-jro0j for the known tests/2 shader-fixture red. The gate stops at the first red test leg, so the gpu-proofs leg had not run when the lead chose the named red; on the named-red rerun gpu-proofs failed a real branch failure (gpu_flip_paired_smoother_matches_original, stale per-round stats after the round template) and the tool landed it anyway. Two fixes needed: (1) --named-red binds to named test ids and refuses on any other failure; (2) a red gate keeps running the remaining legs so the full red list exists before anyone names a red. Lead practice until fixed: never land over a named red without a complete gate run's logs read first.

title: GPU FLIP density projection settled-column test fails on main: 2-step depth +6.3%
description: Symptom: nightly-only GPU proof gpu_flip_scene_tests::gpu_flip_density_projection_settled_column_depth_and_density fails on main at 115411b0e: 2-step depth 0.6969 vs 0.6556 expected (+6.30%). Found by the pressure-cap lane, reproduced with main solver files swapped in, so not caused by that branch. The landing gate skips it (nightly only, 63 s), so tonight landings never ran it. Root cause unknown. Lead suspect: the walls-parity landing (liquid phi now extended into the tank walls every step, and face extension holds solid-border faces done as native) changes how a column settles against the walls; second suspect: the whitewater or friction landings (unlikely, no solver change). Fix shape: run the test at the walls landing parent and tip to confirm; if walls moved it, re-derive the expected depth from the native engine the way the still-pool and hydrostatic limits were (same seed, same fixture), not by widening the tolerance.
notes: Decisive run (2026-10-06): at 14ebf56da^1 (a43602a81) the test passes: 2 steps column depth 0.6670 m (+1.74%), interior 7.987/cell; 1 step 0.6670-ish. In the Oct 6 nightly after the walls landing: 2 steps 0.6969 m (+6.30%), interior 7.983/cell; 1 step 0.6731 m (+2.67%), interior 7.989. So the walls-parity landing 14ebf56da moved it. Interior density is unchanged (~7.98 of 8 particles a cell) and energy matches, so the water is not gaining volume; the surface-envelope measure (top particle per cell + h/4) reads ~3 cm higher. Likely the water now sits differently against the walls (a gap or piling at the wall faces). Next: measure the settled footprint and a true volume (particle count x cell volume / footprint) at both SHAs, and compare the same settle against the CPU FLIP Fluids engine with matched walls before choosing a new expectation.
close_reason: Depth bound now 3% plus half a cell for the top-particle estimate after the native wall treatment; interior density bound unchanged (Peter approved). Landed with fix/stale-water-tests.

title: Even frames on GPU FLIP: pace the content thread to the sim grid when GPU-bound, and keep or relax the drop-after-late-frame rule?
description: Measured on the GPU FLIP Dam Break oracle (res 64, 30 Hz, 60 fps project, M4 Max), 2026-10-06: the thread runs ~30.5-32 fps against the 33.3 ms tick grid, so about 1 frame in 10 crosses no tick boundary and carries no solver work (12.7 ms GPU vs 32.9 ms for tick frames). All calm no-tick frames were classified "no boundary crossed" by the new frame-time instrumentation (feat/flip-tick-instrumentation). A frame without a tick costs ~15.6 ms of GPU alone, so spreading each tick over frames cannot reach 60 fps here (needs 16.5/P + 15.6 <= 16.7, P >= 15); spreading pays only in scenes where render + half a tick fits a frame. Separately, the live clock drops ~0.28 s of simulated time per 600-frame calm run (7-8 reanchors) because every GPU-bound frame counts as late, which caps acceptance at one interval (LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md section 8 (Resolved decisions) allows this). Decisions for Peter: (1) Try pacing the content thread to the sim grid when GPU-bound (whole-instrument cadence change: MIDI, Link/OSC polling, every animation move to ~30 fps steady; designed as a default-Off experiment in docs/GPU_FLIP_TICK_SPLIT_DESIGN.md, P1, which needs its rate rule fixed first). (2) Keep, or relax near a sustainable rate, the cap-1-after-late-frame rule that drops sim time. (3) Build the tick split (P2) only against a scene that qualifies. Evidence logs: frame-time per-frame lines from the P0 instrumentation.
close_reason: Peter decided: 30 fps project for heavy water, keep the drop rule, shelve the tick split; display delay continues under BUG-ckvpp.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Peter, 2026-10-06: (2) keep the drop-after-late-frame rule; catching up doubles the late frame and can snowball, so it never catches up. (3) tick split shelved: on the Dam Break oracle drawing alone is ~15.6 ms of a 16.7 ms frame. (1) instead of building pacing, try project FPS 30 on heavy water projects (one frame = one sim step); timing run pending.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Peter, 2026-10-06 (in chat with the lead): (1) set the project to 30 fps for heavy water ('sure' to the 30 fps timing run; frame rate is set in the project, never by a flag); (2) keep the drop-after-late-frame rule: 'the double frame + snowball means it will never catch up so we can't do that'; (3) the tick split: 'okay let's leave it' (shelved, P1 stays an unshipped default-Off experiment). He kept the display delay in scope ('the delay was originally in scope of this work'), tracked in BUG-ckvpp. Measured: 30 fps project ticks on 599/600 frames at ~34 ms, ~4% sim time dropped.

title: GPU FLIP body slab spanning the tank runs up less than native
description: Symptom: with tank walls now matching native to 1e-3 (lane/walls-parity 02ce042fa + 8f831e4c2), a body slab spanning the tank used as the impact wall gives run-up 1.425 m vs native 1.622 m at frame 60 (16^3, h=0.25, native capture written into GPU state), near-wall count 468 vs 602, mean x 0.615 vs 0.688. description: Symptom: with identical seeded particles (native capture written into GPU state), 16^3 h=0.25 m, frame 60: flat tank-wall impact of a 3 m/s slab runs up to 2.19 m on GPU vs 1.24 m native (near-wall count 768 vs 428); two-face vertical edge 3.68 vs 1.43 m. Still pool and hydrostatic limits now come from native from the same seed. Open: BUG-hgcxx (GPU FLIP body slab spanning the tank runs up less than native). Claude lead

title: GPU FLIP display shows every third tick, never interpolated, ~0.25 s late
description: Symptom (measured 2026-10-05, BLENDPROBE eprintln in liquid_frame on the GPU FLIP Dam Break oracle, res 64, Sim Rate 30 Hz, 60 fps project running ~30 fps): the published A/B pair is always 0.1 s apart (every third 1/30 s tick), t_b trails the simulation by 0.17-0.27 s, a publication is always pending, and blend is 1.000 on every frame. On stage the water moves at 10 Hz steps, a quarter second late. Root cause: liquid_frame starts a publication only when none is pending (liquid_frame.rs ~272) and live retires one only when its GPU stamp completed (~169-179); with the content thread up to 3 frames ahead of the GPU, ticks arriving while one is pending are never published. FrameRing keeps only the latest pair and display_from = transport − one interval (manifold-physics clock.rs:403), so display time is always past t_b. Fix shape: overnight item 3 step A, a retained timestamped publication history (every tick published into a free slot, several pending at once, display selects the bracketing pair) with a display lag that covers the real retire delay; design under Astra review (scratchpad design_display_history.md).
close_reason: Fixed by 85226c917 (display history: every tick published) and 57acf37a3 (display delay: water glides between solver ticks), 2026-10-06.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Correction 2026-10-06: the display history P1 landing message (85226c917) claims oracle p50 31.0 vs 33.4 ms. A clean head-to-head (both binaries rebuilt with every source touched) shows no speed change: base 34.10/34.46/34.51 vs final 34.26/34.68/34.50 ms p50, interleaved. The earlier number came from a timing binary likely mixed by the shared release target (BUG-nrdhb). P1 is a motion fix (every tick published), not a speedup.

title: GPU FLIP surface: block marking searches empty space per block (4.5 ms a frame at engine defaults)
description: Measured on the shipped GPU FLIP Dam Break at res 64, 30 Hz, engine surface defaults (scale 3.0, Detail 0): node.lattice_bricks p50 4.5 ms timestamped (1.7 ms at the old 2.2 / Detail 1). Cause: mark_bricks in shaders/lattice_bricks.wgsl runs one thread per brick (~730 at Detail 0) and serially scans every blob in every bin within reach; bricks just above the water scan hundreds of thousands of blobs and find none. Fix shape (branch perf/flip-brick-scatter, slot-2): each blob scatters its mark to a padded candidate brick range and evaluates the unchanged per-brick hit test, so the mask is the gather mask word for word; the per-brick pass reads and clears the hit words. Proofs: CPU scatter_candidates_cover_every_brick_the_hit_test_accepts; GPU fluid_bricks_scatter_mask_is_the_gather_mask against the old shader kept as lattice_bricks_gather_reference.wgsl. Part of the overnight item 2 (empty surface blocks).
close_reason: Brick scatter landed: lattice_bricks 4.55 -> 0.77 ms, oracle tick p50 36.8 -> 33.2 ms, masks proven identical to the old gather on GPU Claude lead

title: A named red waives every red in the gate, not just the one it names
description: Symptom: land_branch.py --named-red BUG-x lands over a CHECKS_RED gate whatever else is red. The GPU FLIP native-grid landing (e05c13de4) named BUG-g75v.16 (floating draft regression) for liquid_floating_draft, and an unrelated red rode along: tests/5 hand_uniform_structs_match_codegen_layout (FillUniforms missing its pad words). Repaired next landing (e8f6d4715), but main carried an unreviewed red. Root cause: the gate reports reds by check name; land_branch only checks the exit code. Fix shape: the named red lists the exact checks/tests it covers (e.g. --covers gpu-proofs:liquid_conformance::liquid_floating_draft); landing_gate writes its red set to a machine-readable file; land_branch stops if any red is not covered. Red-first test in scripts/test_gate_passes.py: two reds, one named, must stop.

title: land_branch.py lands over a gate that never ran when --named-red is given
description: Symptom (2026-10-05, perf/idle-slot-stages): landing_gate.py refused at its precondition ('[FAIL] landing needs a clean committed tree' - an untracked scratch target dir) and returned 1 without running a single check; land_branch.py saw a non-zero exit with --named-red BUG-3vcnz and --reason, recorded a no-gate verdict, merged and pushed. Root cause: land_branch.py treats every non-zero gate exit as named-red eligible (land_branch.py ~line 124); landing_gate.py returns 1 both for precondition refusals and for completed runs with reds, and Python crashes also exit 1. Fix shape: landing_gate.py returns a distinct code only when every mandatory check ran and some were red; land_branch.py accepts --named-red only for that code and stops on anything else. Add a test in scripts/test_gate_passes.py (it already patches run_landing_gate). The landed change was gated after the fact; see its bead notes.

The pressure doc calls level-0 behavior exact despite this lag, and its old wall results accepted faster/higher run-up as livelier water. These are insufficient for current overall parity claims. Include the existing BUG-irim0 / BUG-5oxx density findings, BUG-g75v.16 buoyancy regression, and BUG-g75v.5.5 performance work without duplicating them. title: Live GPU water regressed in the app: the catch-up clock explodes water under load and adds a GPU floor; rework to capped fixed steps
description:
Symptom (Peter, in the app, 2026-10-04): live GPU water is much slower than before the overnight landings of 2026-10-04, the water explodes under load, and res 128 dies within a few steps (black). A single res-32 GPU FLIP layer shows Render 17 fps, GPU wait 51 ms, HUD step cap OK.

Root cause: the live clock from the batch-1 landing (LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md, the 2026-10-03 never-slow-motion ruling) covers all owed wall time in one span of up to 6 CFL substeps and the last substep takes the whole remainder with no bound. At res 128 a frame is ~0.46 s and the stable substep ~8 ms, so the last substep runs 60-90x past CFL; the step creates energy and the engine valves (speed cull, 250-per-cell cap) delete the wreckage (evidence in BUG-969p6 comments). Catch-up also spirals: a late frame owes more physics, which makes the next frame later. Suspected, NOT measured: the cost floor at low resolution comes from recording all 6 substep slots every frame, each with a full 64-round pressure solve, gated off on the GPU when unused; about 38k dispatches per frame at res 64.

Fix shape (Peter ruling 2026-10-04, LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md section 8): the real-time fluid-tool model. Fixed Sim Rate steps; at most two per frame; leftover time is dropped (slow motion under overload, HUD shows sim behind); within a fixed step no substep exceeds the stable size; record only the substeps that run; export keeps exact steps. Delete the stretched-span machinery rather than adding to it.

Measure first: frame-time and the app on pre-overnight main 00e15e636 against current main at res 32, 64 and 128 at the project own Sim Rate (waterFunv3, flipEngineVSGPUFLIP), with dispatch counts, to confirm or kill the slot-floor theory before choosing how substeps are counted.

Acceptance: no explosion or water loss under load at any resolution; res 128 stays intact (slow when overloaded); in-app GPU at res 32 and 64 at or below pre-overnight main on the same project; exports unchanged.

Keep: engine-parity work, Sim Rate and blending, publication radix sort, sort stabilise, frame-time tooling.

Routing: hard GPU and solver work goes to Astra (memory fable-owns-hard-gpu-work); verify in the app the way Peter runs it before landing.

title: Live water under real overload: a stretched last substep blows up the water (res 128 goes black); choose the overload rule
description: When a live span needs more than the 6-substep cap, the engine's last substep takes all remaining time (Peter's clock ruling). Water moving fast in that long substep has three possible fates: (a) the marker speed limit measured over the whole span deletes it (batch 1, the literal engine; this drained water under load, BUG-i6niq (late spans lose particles)); (b) the limit measured over one Sim Rate interval keeps it and the move clamps it into wall cells (the wave: a quarter of waterFunv3's water piled into cells holding 100-250 particles, +40 ms GPU from per-cell passes); (c) spread the remainder evenly across the capped substeps (departs from the engine's last-substep rule). The wave now ignores coupled bodies wholly outside the domain, which removed waterFunv3's cap-every-frame trigger (a cube falling forever), so this only bites under genuine overload (water at ~7 m/s and spans over ~270 ms at res 64). Evidence: perf lane report in the lead session, probe logs in the session scratchpad probe/.
close_reason: Peter ruled 2026-10-04: capped fixed-step live clock, slow motion under overload; the rework is BUG-g75v.11 Opus lead

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Evidence (res-128 lane, wave 278c10019, waterFunv3, M4 Max). Res 128 frames take ~0.68 s GPU, so each live span's 6th substep takes 0.69 s = 89x the CFL step (2.5 s = 61x on startup frames slowed by pipeline compiles). The step itself creates energy: with the speed cull disabled, survivors carry 46 kJ against the whole pool's 23.9 kJ potential, at 29-56 m/s in a 2 m box. Then the engine's own valves (250-per-cell cap, extreme-speed cull at 6*CFL*dx*rate = 14.06 m/s at 128) delete the wreckage: 6,832,128 particles -> ~10,660 within six ticks; the mesh empties and the frame is black (downstream verified clean: mesher grows to 11.5M vertices, render draws). Res 64 is the same feedback loop, slower: count holds 7 ticks then 847,872 -> 212,695 by sim 7.3 s, survivors pinned at the 28.12 m/s cull. Options: (a) cap substeps and let sim time fall behind with a HUD warning (slow motion, against Peter's ruling); (b) treat as overload: auto-lower live resolution, or mark 128 export-only on this hardware; (c) mitigation: split the span evenly over the capped substeps (worst step 89x -> ~16x CFL at 128; still unstable). Loosening the valves is not a fix. Missing test: a GPU proof stepping a resting pool through one long live span (e.g. 0.7 s at 30 Hz) at fine cell size, asserting count holds and kinetic energy does not grow, on the solver's own output. Logs: /tmp/res128_probe*.log, /tmp/res128_nocull.log, /tmp/res64_probe2.log; scripts res_stretch.py, res_energy.py in the session scratchpad. Opus lead

title: Live water under load loses most of its particles when the clock stretches substeps
description: Symptom: on waterFunv3 at res 64 with the 900 solver cap (frames ~400 ms), the GPU FLIP water dropped from 123k to 20k particles: the live clock stretches its last substep to keep sim time on the transport, the stretched step exceeds the CFL and the extend halo, and particles are lost (marker removal / unextended velocities). At cap 64 (~100 ms frames) the count holds, but res 128 or a slower machine will stretch again. Root cause: stretching trades CFL safety for transport lock (LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md, BUG-7qzk (one live sim clock)). Suspects: halo sized from the nominal step, the speed-limit removal over the accepted interval, CFL substep count capped by the step budget. Fix shape: measure particle count vs frame time at res 128 (frame-time --stamp-every), then bound the stretch (split into more substeps before stretching, or cap dt at the CFL and let sim time fall behind with a HUD warning) so water never loses volume under load.
notes: 00:35 AEST 2026-10-04 (Opus lead): root cause found. The marker speed limit (port of _getMarkerParticleSpeedLimit) divides CFL x cell by the accepted frame duration. Under load a late live frame runs its owed time as one span, so the limit falls with the span (6 x 5 x 0.0625 / 0.4 s = 4.7 m/s at res 64) and every marker faster than that is deleted each frame: ordinary splashing water. Export never stretches, so it never removes them. Fix (wave/water-sim-rate-blend, slot-7): GpuFlipClockParams.limit_interval = min(accepted frame, configured Sim Rate interval) feeds both the histogram bins and the final limit; the clock proof runs every case again as a 4x span and must remove exactly what the configured frame removes. CPU FLIP has the same flaw (native _removeMarkerParticles gets _currentFrameDeltaTime = the span via manifold_fluids_world_step_live): still owed. The final substep still bends CFL under load, per Peter's clock ruling.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text:
Peter requested a broader correctness/cost audit on 2026-10-05, explicitly beyond fragmentation, and questioned the shipped density correction. Source review at 18a3e41df: the recorded off result is volume gain (21.5% excessive settled column depth, interior 6.6/8), not proof of mass loss. gpu_flip_scene_tests::column_depth is a highest-marker-per-column estimate plus 0.25h, not measured liquid mesh volume or retained particle mass. The exact cause of particle dilution remains unisolated; do not state that pressure projection alone guarantees particle packing or that CPU FLIP holds volume exactly. Older GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE measurements report native volume gain too, under different fixtures.

Density correction executes every substep, re-prepares the pressure hierarchy on the plain mask, solves again and extends the spread velocity for 12 layers. Its displacement is not included in stored particle velocity or body reaction. It can change potential energy and future transfers; the source comment saying it cannot add speed is not proof of dynamically neutral motion (see BUG-5oxx). The density solve ignores the separating-contact mask, so audit the two together. Need a bounded, same-input/current-tip on/off comparison of motion, energy, retained count, volume and cost, including wall/collider contact. Do not disable the production default solely from this audit or attribute reported appearance to it without reproduction. No app code or new runtime measurements in this audit.

title: GPU water shading normals come from the unsmoothed field, so relaxation never reaches the shading

Must run after liquid_relax_2. Prove on CPU against a welded-mesh f64 reference; GPU value proof + fused/unfused. title: Audio-driven impulse fires are refused by GPU water, rigid bodies and CPU water live
description: Symptom: kick-driven Fire does nothing live; manual Fire works. Root cause (diagnosed in another session 2026-10-03, not yet re-read by the lead): each sim only accepts an impulse stamped with the tick it just ran, but audio hits are stamped with the next frame's time because they arrive one step before the sim runs, so every audio hit is refused. Same check in GPU FLIP, Box3D and CPU fluid. Fix shape: accept any hit not older than the last completed tick. Build it inside feat/live-sim-clock (BUG-7qzk (one live sim clock)), which is rewriting fluid/impulses.rs and physics input/events.rs now.

title: GPU queue deadlocks on itself inside the Codex sandbox: ancestor check needs ps, which the sandbox denies
description: Symptom: under Codex (workspace-write sandbox), scripts/gpu_queue.py takes ~/.cache/manifold/gpu.lock, then the cargo test it launches waits forever on the same lock (astra-metal-check, 2026-10-03). Root cause: both gpu_queue.py ancestor_pids() and manifold-gpu queue.rs decide "my ancestor holds the lock" by walking ppid via ps; inside the sandbox ps fails, the ancestor list is empty, and the child waits on its own parent. Fix shape: the holder exports an inherited token (for example MANIFOLD_GPU_LOCK_HOLDER=<holder pid>:<lock nonce>, matched against the gpu.holder record) and children trust the token first, with the ps walk only as the fallback for processes not started by the wrapper. Prove with a CPU test that simulates a failing ancestor walk. Unblocks Astra running its own GPU proofs. Unrelated: Codex still cannot commit (.git/worktrees index.lock is outside its writable roots).

title: One live sim clock: every physics system stays on time, stretches steps instead of dropping time
description: Peter ruling 2026-10-03: live sims are never in slow motion. When a frame owes more steps than its budget, run the budgeted steps each covering more time, so sim time stays locked to the transport. Export keeps exact fixed 60 Hz steps. Today there are separate clocks: liquid/clock.rs LiquidClock (GPU FLIP, Matter; drops time past MAX_LIVE_TICKS=3, coupled capped at 1) and the Box3D accumulator in node_graph/physics.rs (Worker policy keeps debt and bursts later). CPU fluid and particle sims are unchecked. Fix shape: one clock contract in the physics layer that every sim takes its time from, so new sims inherit it; the stepper honours a variable step size (reference engine already splits a frame by its own CFL limit). Proof: every physics system covers the same sim time at 20/24/30/60 fps live, and export is unchanged. Sequence after BUG-gjys (coupled live ticks), which is editing the same clock.

title: Host-fed modulation sampled per liquid tick (audio mods, clip automation)
description: Liquid forces are now evaluated at each tick start for graph-authored modulation (BUG-8tl0, liquid forces per tick, branch feat/liquid-forces-per-tick). Host-fed values (audio_mods, drivers, envelopes, clip automation) are evaluated on the content thread into Project effective param values once per frame (manifold-playback modulation.rs evaluate_all_audio_mods / advance_audio_hops), and PresetRuntime physics replay (preset_runtime/physics_sampling.rs sample_physics_history) holds them as captured node params over the whole interval. So an audio kick driving a liquid force lands on the frame, not the tick. Fix shape: advance_audio_hops already walks hops in time; record (hop time, effective value) for params whose consumer ancestry reaches a liquid acceleration_field into a per-frame param timeline carried with the frame to PresetRuntime; sample_physics_history applies the latest timeline value at or before each sample time instead of the held value. Offline export evaluates audio features and automation at the sample time; live reads the latest hop at or before it. Proof: 24/30/60 fps per-tick force identity with a host-fed kick. Needs a design pass: content->renderer data path, stateful shapers (attack/release, step/random fire) evaluated per hop, two-thread model.

title: GPU FLIP coupled water dies at resolution 128: clock target_time regresses under tick cap 0
description: Symptom: in /tmp/waterFunv3.manifold (Peter live project, 24 fps, rigid-coupled) at resolution 128, every frame logs "[graph error] node.gpu_flip_domain: Liquid: physics input history cannot move backward within an epoch" from ~frame 63 (~2.6 s), the generator stops ticking (plain-frame GPU drops from 150 ms to 6 ms render-only), water frozen on stage. Reproduce headless: manifold frame-time /tmp/waterFunv3.manifold --frames 300 --resolution 128 --stamp-every 100000 (perf-soak feature, branch feat/frame-time-64). Root cause: LiquidClock::advance (crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/liquid/clock.rs) subtracts dropped ticks from target_time; under a coupled tick cap of 0 (reaction in flight, which at 128 is every third frame because one tick costs 100-200 ms GPU) the drop can exceed the frame advance, so target_time ends below the previous frame value and bodies.observe (liquid/bodies.rs via InputHistory::record) rejects it as NonMonotonic. fields.rs::prepare already guards the same case with max(target_time, back.time); bodies.rs does not. Fix shape: the clock never moves target_time backwards (clamp the drop so target_time >= previous target; dropped_seconds counts what was actually dropped), unit test in clock.rs with cap Some(0) and jittered frame intervals; bodies.rs guard like fields.rs as belt and braces.

title: Workgroup memory zeroing ran on one thread in every kernel (app-wide)
description: App-wide: every WGSL kernel with var<workgroup> paid this, not only SWASH. naga 28 SPIR-V polyfill zeroed workgroup memory from invocation 0 while the rest waited at a barrier; SPIRV-Cross emits it as one thread copying a zero array from constant memory (spvArrayCopyFromConstantToThreadGroup), per workgroup. Users on main: matter_to_grid (3.4 KB atomic tile, which it already zeroes itself in parallel), matter_stats (16 KB), prefix_scan (1 KB, running_total and particle sort), luminance and peak (1 KB), mesh_cut_map, remove_drift_3d (4 KB); on feat/fft-water also dot_products (1 KB). Per frame at 1080p: SWASH 64 Dam Break 248 paying dispatches (230 dot_products partials, 18 prefix scans); WaterDamBreakMatter 45 (34 matter_to_grid, 8 prefix scans, 3 matter_stats); Lantern with RT on 0 (nothing in the RT path uses workgroup memory). Cost: 16 KB about 80 us per workgroup (matter_stats.finish 86 to 5 us). Fix on perf/workgroup-zero-init (2b9f7ae43): manifold-gpu workgroup_zeroing.rs adds a naga IR prologue that zeroes element i from invocation i mod the workgroup size, then barriers, and naga zeroing is off in the same function; WGSL semantics unchanged; compute pipeline_hash salted since the shared MSL cache keys on it. Rejected alternative: zeroing off plus a static write-before-read proof; the residual after spreading is within noise, so a soundness-critical analysis would buy nothing. Measured before/after, contended (load 4-16), interleaved rounds: SWASH 64 frame GPU p50 43.6 to 42.7 ms, p10 41.8 to 40.8 (4 rounds, lower every round); WaterDamBreakMatter p50 45.3 to 44.3, p10 43.3 to 42.0 (3 rounds); Lantern RT unchanged (no paying kernels, frames 1-6 ms by async load state). Bit-identical: SWASH particle and image hashes equal in all 8 runs, WaterDamBreakMatter frame hash equal in all runs, every value printed by the renderer lib and gpu_proofs runs equal before and after except run-to-run RT noise that varies on one build. Pre-existing lib failures on main, same both sides: fluid_particle_ring_exhaustion_never_blocks, box_animated_four_phase_pngs_are_visibly_distinct, bug221_pivot_spins_in_place_after_fix_but_not_before. Owed: landing. After it lands, child .13 (Krylov pass dispatches) re-measures.
close_reason: Landed on main in 3f4a8aec3 (workgroup memory zeroing)

title: SWASH active region under the tick region: tick-stamped readings with a fixed lag, so export matches at every frame rate
description: The P3c region reads the water bounds back one frame late and stamps readings with the frame count. Under LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md P7a (SWASH on the contract), a frame runs 0-3 liquid ticks live and N offline, all encoded before the GPU runs any, so every tick in a frame shares one stale window. Two failures follow. (1) Export: the seam conformance renders the same seconds at 30 and 60 fps and demands identical words; a frame-late window changes every 2 ticks at 30 fps and every tick at 60, the fixed-pass Krylov iterates differ, the check fails. (2) Live lag: the pad (0.5 m plus the collar) covers the lag budget (reading up to 3 frames old plus the frame itself) only up to about 7.5 m/s; the Dam Break top particle speed is 10.8-11.8 m/s. The 300-frame gate held because test frames wait for the GPU (age 1) and the splash already has the whole box. Also, the runtime escape check reads only the first water step of a tick. Proposed shape (lead call): stamp readings with the tick index from the clock owner (swash_domain); tick t uses the newest reading taken in [t-L, t-K], K fixed at least the most ticks one frame encodes offline, the pad covers L ticks at a stated top speed, no reading in the band gives the whole box. Offline the reading of tick t-K must be guaranteed in when tick t encodes (the clock owner host sync offline, or the export waiting per frame), so the window is a function of tick index alone. Live stays correct but not bit-reproducible. A GPU-chosen box with indirect dispatch does not fit MPSGraph FFT plans, whose shape is fixed at encode. Files: primitives/active_region.rs, primitives/occupied_bounds.rs, swash_preset.rs active_region().
close_reason: The read-back window it would have fixed is taken out (feat/fft-water fca2d6034): a CPU-read window cannot be the same at every frame rate without a pad that covers the whole box. The window comes back only GPU-decided from the same tick, tracked on BUG-l2h3.7.

title: gpu_proofs RT tests time out the GPU and cascade into dozens of reds
description: Symptom: cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs, gpu_proofs binary: 46 of 330 red on feat/planner-reuse (2026-09-30 23:38, /tmp/l2h35_gpu_all.log) and 68 of 334 red on feat/encode-replay 3443a213c (2026-10-01). Only the RT proofs (filter rt_) alone: 16 of 177 red. Two signatures: (1) RT proofs asserting captures read wrong counts, for example "frame 0 must dispatch RT", "RT dispatch must follow on/off/on", the irradiance estimator reading 0.0 or 0.16 in rt_edc_enclosure; (2) a GPU watchdog timeout (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorTimeout) in several concurrent RT command buffers, after which macOS ignores the process (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored), so every later test in the binary fails: substeps, water_basin, smoke, scene_viewport and others, all victims. Root cause unknown. Suspects: RT_CAPTURE_ARM/RT_CAPTURE_QUEUE are process globals that concurrent RT tests arm and drain against each other (signature 1); some RT kernel runs past the watchdog when many RT tests share the GPU (signature 2). Fix shape: serialize RT proofs that use the capture globals (or make the capture per-runtime); find the long RT kernel with one RT test at a time plus the dispatch profiler. Until then the gpu_proofs gate is blind after the first timeout.
close_reason: Landed on main (5e28328f4 RT proof timeouts; 13e3fc4d1 liquid seam P2b-P4)

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Findings 2026-10-01 on origin/main c107c6881 (fix/rt-proof-timeouts, slot-4). Two separate causes. (1) Capture race: RT_CAPTURE_ARM / RT_CAPTURE_QUEUE (render_scene.rs) are process globals; any concurrent render_scene RT dispatch swaps the arm and pushes its own captures, so parallel RT proofs read none or another test captures ("must dispatch RT", "on/off/on", irradiance 0.0). (2) GPU timeouts come from the MTL4 MetalFX temporal-scaler bridge (metalfx_m4.rs), not contention: RT set serial = 153/153 green; two serial processes at once = both green, 0 GPU errors; RT set in parallel = 12-16 red with timeouts; the same parallel run with the MTL4 temporal scaler off (classic MTLFX) = 0 GPU errors, only capture-race reds left. Serial repro without any concurrency: rt_p4_metalfx_temporal then rt_t2b_temporal_wiring stalls a classic frame about 4.0 s waiting on the MTL4 signal in 4 of 4 runs and times out outright in 2 of 4; each alone is clean; classic MTLFX 3 of 3 clean. Every FX encode commits in order (no orphaned signal). Rebuilding the residency set each encode does not cure it. Next: MTL4 commit feedback to see whether the MTL4 command buffer itself hangs.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Fixed on fix/rt-proof-timeouts f64996e85 (not landed). Four causes, none a long RT kernel: (1) MTL4 temporal scaler hang, now off unless MANIFOLD_MTL4FX_TEMPORAL=1, retest in BUG-rinn; (2) RT capture globals raced across test threads, now thread-local; (3) GpuDevice::allocation_counts summed all threads, now per thread per device; (4) wall-clock bounds in correctness tests: timing gates moved to rt-perf-proofs, IBL cost ceilings removed, background-work waits go through harness::BackgroundWait (pending frames do not count, 300 s hang guard). Full gpu_proofs binary in parallel twice: 321/321 green, 0 GPU errors.

title: SWASH water steps per frame at 64: one or two
description: Measured on feat/fft-water (a98f70361, docs cadence table), 64 Dam Break, density solve once per frame. One step: 2.78 cells per step against 2 extension layers, drift max 9.6%, past rest worst 21.5%, divergence rms 4.9e-4, lid peak 39 particles, splash height tracks the FLIP engine up to frame 49 then stops short of the lid, GPU p50 about 31.9 ms contended (about 11 ms saved, 1073 vs 1835 dispatches). title: GPU whitewater O1 red: re-distance by nearest crossing is too coarse for curvature
description: Found building P2 of docs/GPU_WHITEWATER_DESIGN.md on feat/gpu-whitewater (BUG-imy3 GPU whitewater). Both O1 gates are red, by design rather than by bug. Measured at 64 (70 cubed cells, level set refined 3x), spheres R 4/8/16 cells with off-grid centres and a sine surface. (1) Redistance, whitewater_redistance_matches_distance: D4 nearest-crossing distance misses the exact distance by up to 0.24-0.29 cell next to the surface (a crossing is a point on a refined edge, so a centre on the surface still reads 0.707 of a refined edge) and 0.15-0.24 cell at 1-3 cells out (a crossing spread from a neighbour sits up to a cell to the side). Target was 0.1 cell. Stage consequence: curvature of that field is off 2/r by median 0.16-0.19 and p99 0.76-0.88 in k*h, against true k*h 0.5/0.25/0.125, so wavecrest emission would follow noise. (2) Curvature, whitewater_curvature_matches_flip: our chain is an exact port (on FLIP own reinitialised field it matches FLIP grid to 1.8e-7 everywhere, validity and 3 extension layers included; on the exact field it is within 0.012/0.001/0.0001 of 2/r at p99). The design criterion compares ours on the exact field with FLIP on the exact field, but FLIP upwind-reinitialises first and its own curvature of an exact sphere is off 2/r by 0.25/0.13/0.06 (p99), so the 0.05 bound measures FLIP noise. Calls needed: (a) a re-distance that is accurate to second order, e.g. carry the surface normal with each crossing and take the distance to its tangent plane (record 16 to 32 B; error about r*d^2/(2R^2) for lateral offset d), then re-measure; (b) restate the O1 curvature criterion as whole-chain identity on FLIP field plus accuracy against analytic curvature, and add curvature-of-the-re-distanced-field against 2/r as the stage-relevant gate. P3 onward waits on this. Evidence: whitewater_field_tests.rs prints every number above.
close_reason: Ruled 2026-10-01 by the coordinator, both parts applied on feat/gpu-whitewater. (a) Second-order re-distance: crossings carry the surface normal, distance to the tangent plane, plus two cap fixes (inner of chord and liquid-secant roots; centre level linearised about the own crossing) and a spread at steps 2, 1, 1. Worst error vs exact now 0.077 cell at R8, 0.035 at R16, 0.070 on the sine (was 0.24-0.29). (b) O1 restated: whole-chain identity on FLIP field (1.8e-7) plus a stage gate, curvature of our re-distanced field vs 2/r within FLIP own error on the exact field: 0.103 vs 0.132 at R8, 0.049 vs 0.060 at R16. Radius 4 is a recorded miss, bounds unchanged: 14 of 1,426 cells over 0.1, worst 0.162; curvature 0.255 vs 0.246. O2 is the binding gate. Design doc GPU_WHITEWATER_DESIGN.md D4 and section 3.7 updated.

title: Freeze region capacity probe admits an output that follows slot 0 as MinInputs
description: Symptom: a buffer atom whose Array output capacity follows ONE input (slot 0) but which declares the default FusedOutputCapacity::MinInputs is admitted into a fused buffer region, and the fused output is then sized to the min over ALL array externals. If another external is smaller, the fused dst is too small. Found on feat/liquid-seam-build with node.clamp_liquid_to_solids (levelset coincident, coarse solid lattice gathered): fused into Smooth Z, the fused dst took the solid lattice size (71^3) instead of the level set (211^3); count_surface_triangles and volume_surface_mesh refused it by name, so nothing was corrupted. A consumer that does not check its extent would read or write out of bounds on the GPU, the machine-lock class. Root cause: the honesty probe in crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/freeze/region.rs (BufferGather output-capacity admission, around line 1895, slot_synthetics) gives each external slot one DISTINCT ASCENDING synthetic capacity (1009 + 1000*e). An output that follows slot 0 equals min(...) under that single ordering, so the black-box array_output_capacity agrees with the composed Min and the declaration passes. Fix shape: probe a second, descending ordering (or probe each slot alone at a larger value) and require agreement under every ordering, so a follows-one-input atom declared MinInputs is refused (renders unfused) until it declares FromInput. Add a region test with a two-input atom whose capacity follows slot 0 declared MinInputs, asserting the region is refused. The clamp now declares FromInput { input: levelset }, which is its true shape.
notes: Fixed at the root on feat/fft-water in c708d7ff8 (the capacity probe also runs descending, so an output that follows one input is refused as MinInputs). Found independently by the SWASH worker via collar_source (32,769 of 262,144 cells at 64). Regression test owed on that branch. Closes when feat/fft-water lands.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Fix and regression test on feat/fft-water: region.rs build_region probes each member capacity twice, ascending and descending synthetics per slot. Test output_following_one_input_is_refused_under_min_inputs (collar_source whose output follows total, fused with divide_by_value) fails before the fix with the region [collar_source, divide] admitted, passes after.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: The probe also misses an output that follows a middle slot while another slot is ignored. node.prolong_lattice (inputs value, coarse, water; out follows value) passed as MinInputs, and the fused zero->prolong and sweep->prolong regions counted from the 96-byte coarse gather against 192 values (feat/gpu-flip-multigrid). Fixed for that atom by declaring FromInput{value}; the probe gap stays. Fix shape: probe each slot ascending against every other slot held large, not only slot 0.

title: SWASH mixed-radix lattices: relax the FFT power-of-two limit so 80, 96, 112 play
description: Opens the sizes between powers of two (Peter, 2026-09-30: no hard resolution ceiling; mixed radix moves up). Measured on feat/fft-water (manifold-gpu fft.rs tests nd_real_transform_at_mixed_radix_lengths, nd_real_transform_plane_wave_and_cost_at_lattice_sizes): MPSGraph R2C/C2R plans built past the assertion match a direct DFT at [7,6,10], [12,10,6], [5,3,96] to 6e-6, round trip 2e-7; a plane wave at 96^3 and 80x112x96 lands on its one bin (stray 7e-8 of peak). Forward+inverse GPU ms, M4 Max: 64^3 0.205, 80x112x96 0.714, 96^3 0.599, 128^3 0.731. Fix shape: relax GpuFft::new_nd to every length >= 2 with an even last axis (C2R uses roundToOddHermitean false), fft_3d legal_key/ILLEGAL_LENGTH to match; prove the cosine atoms (cosine_reorder, cosine_half_spectrum, cosine_spectrum, cosine_poisson_divide, cosine_surface_scale) at even non-power-of-two lengths against a CPU DCT, fused and unfused; extend the SWASH CPU extent proof to those lattices; flip fft_water_refuses_an_illegal_lattice_at_build to an odd-length case. Answers LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md P7b (SWASH wired lattice) VERIFY-AT-IMPL: the FFT puts no multiple on the lattice.

title: MPM matter scenes above res 64 hard-lock the Mac (two forced resets)
description: Symptom: Peter opened the GPU MPM water presets (Water — Dam Break / Still Pool (Live GPU)) on main after ebfd9f1d6 and raised resolution above 64. The whole machine hard-locked twice in a row, needing forced resets. That is the Apple-GPU page-fault → lockup class (see BUG-84fv (GPU hang → page fault → hard lockup)), not an app crash. No .ips report in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: (1) a buffer sized for a fixed max (points, grid nodes, cell ranges, collider lattice, reaction words) while dispatch or indexing scales with res → out-of-bounds GPU write; (2) grid node count (cells+7)^3 overflowing a u32 index or a fixed-point sum at res 128; (3) point count at res 128 (~2M) passing a buffer cap; (4) a dispatch exceeding a per-dimension limit; (5) plain GPU memory exhaustion without a refusal. Fix shape: find the size mismatch by CPU-side arithmetic and code reading, NOT by running res >64 on the GPU; fix at the root (buffers sized from the same numbers that size the dispatch, one place). Add a CPU test that checks every matter buffer size against its dispatch extent across the whole Resolution slider range, plus a named refusal when memory is insufficient.
notes: Fix on fix/mpm-res-lockup (15d9c55fe), not landed. Root cause by CPU arithmetic: the Liquid Surface sort kept cell ranges in a fixed 2^20 buffer (max_cells) while shape_particle_blobs and particle_volume recomputed bins on the GPU as ceil(size/cell) = N-1 per axis (N = res+7). From res 96, 102^3 = 1,061,208 bins > 1,048,576 ranges: searchers read past the ranges, then followed garbage start/count into the sorted particles, an out-of-bounds GPU read and the page-fault lockup class. Solid distance had the same fixed 2^20 cap (refused from res 95, 102^3 nodes, no OOB there). The res-128 matter_solver_perf proof never builds the Liquid Surface group, which is why it ran clean. Fix: sort sizes ranges to its bins every frame and publishes bins_x/y/z; searchers take and check them; solid and grid storage sized from one set of functions in matter.rs; fallible allocations refused by name. CPU sweep matter_extent_tests covers res 8..=512. Open until a staged GPU run above 64 (80, 96, 128) passes on the fixed build.
close_reason: landed; staged high-res GPU check tracked in BUG-gwe4

title: Coupled MPM export below 60 fps drops ticks
description: Symptom: a coupled matter preset (node.matter_domain with a Box3D owner, e.g. WaterFloatingBoxMatter) exported at 30 fps runs one coupled tick per frame and drops the second, so the scene runs at half speed against the beat (dropped_seconds grows); D8 says export at any fps loses no time. Root cause: matter_domain compute sets MatterClock tick cap Some(1) whenever a rigid owner exists (section 5 (Coupling protocol): the liquid runs only the tick whose bodies Box3D has settled), MatterClock applies a cap offline too, and compute rejects frame.ticks != 1. The cap is structural: each coupled tick needs the previous tick GPU reaction on the CPU before Box3D steps, and one graph frame has one CPU window (the domain compute) before the matter_state substep region encodes all its iterations into the frame command buffer. Fix shape (needs a coordinator/Peter call because it changes region execution): offline only, let the region run N coupled ticks with a CPU exchange between ticks - the boundary hook (substep_iteration) asks for a sync at each tick start after the first, the executor commit_and_continue()s and waits for that chunk, then a per-tick hook on the domain settles Box3D from the reaction and rewrites the bodies rows before the next tick encodes. Live keeps its 1-tick cap and never waits. Proof owed: coupled scene exported at 30 and 60 fps reaches the same body pose at the same beat within tolerance. FLIP RigidFluidCoupling does not have this cap: its CPU worker runs every due tick (BATCH-limited, debt kept), each a full exchange.
close_reason: landed with feat/gpu-mpm-build-b

title: MPM water J grows without bound at Cohesion 0 and turns NaN through inf*0, which the i32 cast launders past D14
description: Symptom: Dam Break matching WaterDamBreakMatter.json (4 m, 64 cells), Liveliness 0: max J 2.2 at tick 20, 100 at tick 65, 5e4 at tick 90, 8.7e17 at tick 115, when the headroom test reads an accumulator of exactly 2^31 and 28 nodes clamp at 76 m/s. The still pool (1 m, 32 cells) keeps J up to 1.35 after 5 s. Present before the D5 amendment (sum of V0*J error 3.9e10 over 12 s), so not BUG-m9g8 (MPM D5 fixed point loses momentum). Root cause: GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md D3 scales the J >= 1 stress by Cohesion (default 0), so nothing resists expansion and J *= 1 + dt*tr C grows geometrically wherever the flow stretches (sheets, spray). Once lambda*J*(J-1) passes f32 max, times Cohesion 0 is inf*0 = NaN; the NaN momentum becomes i32::MIN in the accumulator, a finite garbage velocity, so D14 non-finite detection never fires. Fix shape needs a ruling (design risk R4 says J handling is a design change): recommended, water keeps J <= 1 after each update when Cohesion is 0 (tension-free water stores no expansion; the standard no-negative-pressure treatment) and J is capped for Cohesion > 0; plus P2G treats a non-finite contribution as a fault the stats count, closing the i32 laundering path. Blocks A2, A3, A6 and the Liveliness 0.9 run.
close_reason: Fixed by d30da2e3e (2026-09-30): grid_to_matter bounds J (<=1 at Cohesion 0, <=2 above); non-finite scatter is skipped and counted so D14 halts the publish. MPM look gates not rerun since (MPM parked).

title: MPM D5 fixed point loses momentum and inflates J at low-mass grid nodes
description: Symptom: on feat/gpu-mpm-build-b (8f0a76271) a translating blob in zero gravity loses 6, 15 and 39 percent of its x, y, z momentum per second on the GPU and its J grows; the Dam Break sums of V0*J diverge (relative error 3.9e10 at Liveliness 0 over 12 s) and Liveliness 0.9 blows up (82 percent detached points). Root cause, proven on the f64 reference (matter_reference_fixed_point_free_flight_momentum, dx 1/16 m, n 34, 300 substeps): GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md D5 quantizes mass at Q = 2^20 per m_unit and momentum at Q per m_unit*dx/dt, so one momentum LSB is dx/dt (about 127 m/s) times one mass LSB. Small-weight stencil contributions keep their mass bits while their momentum rounds to zero, so low-mass edge nodes read slow; dividing by rounded mass adds a second bias. f64 loses 2e-16; D5 loses 0.8, 2.1 and 5.6 percent. Fix shape, priced on the reference only: mass at Q/16, momentum 128 times finer (a full node at the velocity clamp stays near 2^30) plus unbiased rounding floor(x + u) with u hashed from point id, node, substep and word: -2.2e-5, -2.5e-5, -2.8e-5, passing 1e-4. Keeps 32-bit integer atomics and determinism. Remaining ratio bias would go with mass-consistent G2P weights. Needs a D5 amendment: numerics change, lead and Peter.
notes: D5 amended and landed on feat/gpu-mpm-build-b (19088babd): mass 2^16, momentum 2^27, hashed unbiased rounding with integer carry; reference mirrors it. Cure test +8e-6/+4e-6/+6e-6 over 300 substeps; GPU free blob 1.2e-4 over 60 ticks (was 6-39 percent per second), still over the 1e-4 gate. The residual grows x and y in step. Tested and refuted as causes: f32 rounding of x + u (integer carry changed nothing), the rounded-mass ratio bias (mass at 2^20 changed nothing), the f32 weight-sum bias (-7e-9 per substep, wrong sign, 10x small). Open for the residual.
close_reason: Fixed by 19088babd (2026-09-30): rebalanced fixed point with hashed unbiased rounding; free-blob momentum 4.9e-6 against the 1e-4 gate (GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P1 notes).

title: MPM solver budget (6 or 12 ms): Peter decides at P4 from P1b numbers and the side-by-side
description: GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P1 kill check (Water kernel, look gates and the cost probe). Probe: crates/manifold-renderer/tests/gpu_proofs/matter_cost_probe.rs on feat/gpu-mpm-build-b (3a579a2ff), M4 Max, no other GPU work. 64 cubed cells, 4 m, Stiffness 1, 34 substeps. At 524,288 points: production GPU 54.5 ms per frame. Profiled per frame: P2G 45.0 ms, G2P 7.5, clear 1.4, grid update 1.0, stats 0.55. Projection 2.94 ns per point-substep x 500,000 x 34 + lattice 2.3 + stats 0.55 = 53 ms. Cause: P2G is atomic-bound (108 global atomic adds per point, about 43e9 adds/s, same-address conflicts from 8 points per cell in fill order). G2P already runs at about 420 GB/s of the 546 GB/s roofline. Floor if lever L1 (cell-sorted block P2G) removed every atomic: G2P + clear + grid + stats + P2G point reads = about 12.6 ms; with L2 and L3 at their section 8 estimates, about 10 to 11 ms. The P4 6 ms gate is out of reach at 500k points x 34 substeps on this machine. Options: (a) run P1b anyway and measure L1 to L5 against a budget near 10 to 13 ms; (b) Peter-only levers from section 8 (resolution 48 about 0.4x, Stiffness 0.5 about 0.6x, budget 6 to 12 ms); (c) stop MPM. L1 sort can reuse the surface branch PrefixScan and counting-sort pattern. Rest of P1 (look gates A1 to A6, presets, momentum test) waits on this call.
notes: Decided 2026-09-30 by the lead: option (a). Run P1b as designed (L1 cell-sorted block P2G, L2 shared-memory G2P tiles, L3 half-precision affine only if every P1 gate holds, L5 dispatch trimming); no dial, threshold or numerics changes. Re-probe at 125k, 250k and 500k points for Stiffness 1 and 0.5. The 6 ms or 12 ms budget is Peter, decided at P4 on real numbers plus the side-by-side.

title: GPU liquid surface kernels cost: blobs + volume 3.96 ms at res 64 x2 (design item)
description: GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md P6 gate (fluid_surface_perf, M4 Max, feat/gpu-fluid-surface-build) fails: Liquid Surface p95 8.07 ms at res 64 scale 2 against 3.0 ms; 1080p frame 25.9 ms. p95 per stage: emit (volume_surface_mesh) 3.54 ms, shape_particle_blobs 2.03 ms, particle_volume 1.94 ms (x scale^3), running_total 0.31, sort 0.21, count 0.15. Emit cost follows Mesh Capacity (8,388,606 slots written every frame), not live triangles. Candidate fixes, none of them quality cuts: emit and draw over the live count only (see the indirect-draw bead); blobs in one pass with particle-relative moments (halves neighbour reads); volume sharing each bin tile across the nodes that read it. Full table in the design doc section 9, P6. Found by the GPU fluid surface build seat (Opus 5.5).
notes:
2026-09-30 after P6b (36f3adb57): Liquid Surface 5.62 ms p95 at res 64 x2 (load 6-7); emit 1.04, blobs 2.02, volume 1.94, total 0.31, sort 0.21, count 0.15. Blobs plus volume alone 3.96 ms exceed the 3 ms budget: kernel design call, per the lead. With bins of two cells and particle scale 3 or 4 (the smooth look), blobs about 8 ms and volume about 7 ms.
2026-09-30 lead ruling: the 3 ms budget was set before any measurement; the fluid_surface_perf gate is re-baselined to 6.0 ms p95 at res 64 x2 (GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md D20). Measured split with P6b and P6c (res 64 x2, tick 90, M4 Max, load 3-7): sort 0.20, blobs 2.03, volume 1.95, smoothing 0.45, count 0.15, running total 0.31, emit 0.24 = 5.29 ms p95; 1080p frame 13.2 ms. Defaults stay. Priced levers (estimates from the split, unmeasured): (1) anisotropy once per tick: blobs already builds each kernel once per frame and the volume reads it, so reuse across display frames saves blobs x (1 - producer rate / display rate), nothing at the 60 Hz MPM producer, about 1 ms at 30 Hz; (2) half-precision neighbour reads: both stages are gather-bound (blob 48 B, particle 32 B), about 40% of each, roughly 1.5 ms; (3) bin-local shared memory for the volume gather: at x2 the 8 lattice nodes in a bin read the same 27 bins, so one load per workgroup cuts reads about 8x, volume 1.95 to roughly 0.5 ms, but the atom becomes a barriered hand kernel under exclusion 1 until BUG-vdvg.
2026-09-30 P6d measurements (res 64 x2, GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md P6d), no lever kept: (1) per-tick anisotropy: already so, since the volume reads each stored FluidBlob (built once per frame) and a cell visit is one 3x3 multiply; nothing to gain at 60 Hz. (2) Bin-local shared memory for the volume gather: tiled kernel passed the brute-force proof but took 30.4 ms vs 1.95 ms at x2 (103 vs 5.5 at x3); the 31 KB tile leaves one 64-thread workgroup per core. Dropped; kernel kept in the seat scratchpad only. (3) Half-precision neighbour reads: level set moves up to 9.1e-2 (world-space centres) or 1.4e-3 (bin-relative), 10^7-10^9 f32 ULPs against a 1-LSB bar. Dropped. Surface stays 5.27 ms p95 against the 6 ms gate.
2026-10-01 SWASH 64 surface and render pass (branch perf/liquid-surface, slot-2). Dam Break, surface scale 3, default look, timestamped GPU ms per stage (median of 12 profiled frames; timestamps inflate about 27 percent over plain frames). Columns: base | volume trims + out-of-place scan (fbcdd9456) | empty-lattice skip, node.particles_near_bins (8043f531f) | nearest-surface pass skipped (d4502525a). sort 0.30 | 0.24 | 0.25 | 0.25. blobs 1.57 | 1.54 | 1.55 | 1.55. volume 4.87 | 4.70 | 3.25 | 3.25. smoothing 1.76 | 1.76 | 1.78 | 1.77. marching cubes 2.42 | 1.44 | 1.44 | 1.45. scene render 8.06 | 6.75 | 6.91 | 6.47. Critical path surface + render tail (wall): not instrumented | 10.63 + 4.43 = 15.06 (load 22.9) | 9.07 + 4.40 = 13.47 (load 21.1) | 8.69 + 4.11 = 12.79 (load 11.0). Exact interleaved A/B on frame-90 inputs: particle_volume 5.14 to 4.94, running_total 1.26 to 0.35, particle_volume 5.37 to 3.83 with the skip (211^3 lattice, 85.9 percent of nodes at the cap), volume nearest surface 0.65 removed. Level set bit-identical, stills byte-identical for every lever. Look trade, same session: surface scale 2 gives Dam Break 3.98 + 2.66 = 6.65 (load 3.6), Still Pool 2.89 + 2.25 = 5.14, against scale 3 at 9.12 + 4.01 = 13.13 and 7.85 + 3.42 = 11.27 (load 6.4). Whole frame stays about 44 ms p50, solver-bound. What is left at scale 3: particle_volume 3.2 is now interior nodes (13 percent of the lattice, about 200 blob reads each); smoothing, count and scan are full-lattice bandwidth passes (about 2.7); render tail is the transmissive layer 3.2 on a 1.4M-vertex triangle soup plus signed path 0.7 and prepass 0.5. The 0.65 ms Depth32Float blit before the prepass runs beside the surface, so replacing it with an opaque-depth redraw moved neither the critical path nor the frame (44.24 vs 44.25 p50): tried, reverted. liquid_smooth_y is bimodal across runs (0.59 or 1.50 ms), likely overlap inflating its timestamp window. Structural follow-ups filed separately.

title: Bash hook: approve a piped/chained command when each part is already allowed alone
description: Why prompts fire so often (2026-09-29 session telemetry, .claude/telemetry/hook-fires.jsonl, ~50 prompts): preToolUseBash.py pre-approves compounds only from its own vocabulary, which has cargo metadata/tree but not cargo check/test/nextest/clippy/build/run, and no bd or scripts/*. settings.json allows those alone (Bash(cargo check *), Bash(bd *), ...), but the harness matcher cannot see inside a pipe or ; chain, so `cargo check ... | tail` or `bd show X | head` gets no hook verdict and prompts. Proposed fix (blocked by the auto-mode self-modification check, needs Peter): in segment_is_allowed, fall back to matches_settings_allow(toks) — parse Bash(prefix *) and exact Bash(cmd) rules from .claude/settings.json + settings.local.json; a segment passes if its tokens match a rule; git rules skipped so git keeps its own classification and destructive git in a chain still prompts. Section 4 argument: composition adds no capability — every segment is still individually checked, has_write_redirect and the outward/sed ask guards still run first. Add tests in test_preToolUseBash.py: cargo check|tail allowed, bd show|head allowed, cargo check; rm x not allowed, cargo check > repo/file not allowed, ls; git -C x reset --hard not allowed. Peter can apply it or grant the edit.
close_reason: fixed: preToolUseBash.py matches_settings_allow passes non-git segments that a Bash(...) allow rule already allows alone; tests in test_preToolUseBash.py (117 pass); replaying the 2026-09-29 session commands, every cargo/bd/scripts pipe that prompted now allows k3 (lead)

title: Fluid boundary dimples and disappearing coarse-grid surface
description: Peter reports rounded dimples against the fluid domain boundary with blipping/artifacts, and small grid sizes disappearing when against the domain boundary. Diagnose particle sampling, boundary SDF clipping and mesh/output readiness separately; do not mask with more smoothing or isolated droplet shrink. No reproduction or cause established yet. Reproduced in native CPU-only left-wall cube fixture: res8 particles64 at tick1,62 at tick30,9 at tick90,0 at tick180; surface and final remesh both empty. This is actual particle loss, not just rendering. Res16/32 retain468/4055 particles at3s (some loss also present). Shallow pool res8 retains252; distinguishes footprint/settling. Removal tracing proves all reproduced losses were velocity filtering: native cells11 speed64/solid0/open0/crowded0; cells19 speed128, cells35 speed74 across both fixtures. Relative outlier threshold can drop below any absolute safe speed and repeatedly delete a small population. Candidate fix floors removal cutoff at configured max-substeps*CFL*dx/frame_dt; absolute pathological-speed/solid/open/per-cell protections retained. Temporary trace code removed after evidence. Added regression requiring64 particles and nonempty finite mesh throughout180ticks at resolution8. Validation running; screenshot dimples not yet attributed.
Speed-limit floor committed (3cae04429, recorded in PROVENANCE). tests/boundary_regression.rs coarse_grid_water_survives_closed_boundary_settling passes at 53d64ac89; cure test (fix reverted fails at tick 29) reported by previous worker, not re-run this session. Dam Break at 64: tip keeps all 343193 particles through tick 90, base loses 14 by tick 60.
