title: glTF-imported material params silently dropped in instantiate_def (blocks BUG-pt6g end-to-end)
description: Symptom: glTF-imported materials (via assemble_import_graph -> flatten_groups -> PresetRuntime::from_def_with_device) do not respond to param overrides applied post-import to the flattened def -- confirmed on node.pbr_material ambient and node.bake_environment intensity on tests/fixtures/gltf/the_rosetta_stone.glb: mutating def.nodes params after flatten_groups() correctly changes the def (verified via print), but the rendered output is byte-identical across a 0.05->0.9 ambient sweep and a 0.2->3.0 env intensity sweep. Root cause: unknown, suspects narrowed via source instrumentation earlier this session -- graph_loader.rs instantiate_def (or one of its 4 migration passes: migrate_def_type_ids, migrate_scene_object_wires, migrate_gltf_anim_v2, flatten_groups) silently drops SOME node params (confirmed: bake_equirect_envmap intensity reads its primitive-declared default 1.0 regardless of the def override) while others survive fine (mode param on the same node persists correctly) -- the override loop in graph_loader.rs:679-704 looks structurally correct/unconditional on read, so the drop happens somewhere between a correct-looking write and the primitive run() read. Fix shape: instrument/bisect instantiate_def one migration stage at a time (print node.params before/after each) to find which stage clobbers which params. This blocks real-world verification of BUG-pt6g (lighting macros dead on photoscan imports) -- the unlit-routing fix (this session, lane/unlit-default-lit) is structurally correct and unit-tested, but end-to-end on a real GLB is still dark because of this separate bug. Likely the same mechanism as "the binding-replant bug" the team lead flagged as split into its own bead -- confirm and dedupe before starting new work on it.
close_reason: Duplicate of BUG-ji6q (binding default_value replant) — same mechanism, confirmed by the same instrumentation trail. Root-fix slice tracked there.

title: Binding default_value replant clobbers live node.params on every graph rebuild (BUG-303 relapse class)
description: Mechanism (lane-confirmed with instrumentation, 2026-07-30): card-stamped defs (GLB imports via stamp_scene_node_exposures_into, scene_exposure.rs:166-255) give EVERY node param a BindingDef whose default_value is a frozen snapshot of node.params at stamp time. On every graph build, instantiate_def (graph_loader.rs:679-704) correctly writes def node.params onto the live node, then BoundGraph::new -> apply_binding_defaults (param_binding.rs:629-648) unconditionally replants every binding default_value over it. Two copies of one fact, nothing keeps them in sync — any writer touching node.params for a bound target (def edits, migrations, direct macro/mapping writes) is silently reverted at next rebuild. This is the BUG-303 (import values clobbered to primitive defaults) class relapsed; the old fix only synced the copies at stamp time. Fix direction chosen by lead: ROOT (option B) — remove the duplicate source of truth: seed the binding skip-cache from the live graph value instead of replanting default_value. CAUTION: bound_graph.rs binding lifecycle is load-bearing (OilyFluid Speed regression 903deaa8; apply_inner_overrides cache-clear contract) — own slice with full-context review, not a quick lane. Also: dropped/reverted param writes must become loud. Regression test shape: import fixture, mutate a bound param post-stamp, assert it survives a rebuild.
notes: Bisect result (2026-07-30, CPU-only repro: post-assembly def mutation of bake_environment intensity, survives-rebuild check): BROKEN at every testable commit back to 6b02cba0 (2026-07-12, the commit that ADDED the intensity param + card binding) — no introducing commit; defect born with the param. Mechanism older still: bound_graph.rs traces to 652486d9 (shared BoundGraph unification). BUG-303 (import transforms clobbered, fixed 66772e69/995006eb 2026-07-22) diagnosed the same mechanism against a different symptom — confirmed recurring class. Note: the ParamManifest per-frame path (bound.apply) is IMMUNE — live macro sliders are unaffected by this bug; it bites def edits, migrations, and any direct node.params writer.
close_reason: Closed

title: RT shadows collapse to one caster — moving a zero-intensity sun re-shadows all live lights
description: render_scene.wgsl shadow_factor (RT branch, ~line 611) returns the single RT mask (traced along casters[0] dir, render_scene.rs:4062) for EVERY light — so moving a zero-intensity sun re-shadows all live lights (repro: RtLightTestingV2.manifold, RT on, sun intensity 0). Root cause: RT shadow pass supports exactly one caster, applied globally. Fix shape: per-caster traced visibility (up to MAX_SHADOW_CASTING_LIGHTS=4), per-pixel ray direction + max_distance for point/spot casters, shadow_factor indexes the mask by slot like the raster path.
close_reason: Fixed on main (merge b1fbc9e2): per-caster traced visibility, one channel per shadow slot; point casters per-pixel dir + distance cap; shadow_factor indexes by slot; GI/reflection sun terms sum over sun casters. Proof rt_multi_caster_shadow: zero-intensity sun move byte-identical; casters independent.

comments.author: glm-4.7 (dispatcher)
comments.text:
Dispatcher read-only mechanism findings (no probes, no code changes). Companion to /tmp/manifold_seam_review.md (K3's dispatch-gate review). Fable to review.

== The discriminator ==

Shadow/AO/GI/reflection are ONE kernel, ONE dispatch, ONE accel binding (render_scene.rs:4240 calls dispatch_shadow_rays once per RT-ready frame; kernel at raytrace.rs ~L840 casts all four ray types from the same origin, same accel, same walk_with_alpha_test). Therefore any dispatch-level failure theory (encoder cache, command-queue ordering, accel coherence) predicts shadow rays die too. They survive. The failure is DOWNSTREAM of accel traversal, INSIDE the kernel — something GI+reflection read that shadow does not.

That thing is `n` — the interpolated vertex normal at the primary-ray hit (raytrace.rs:885):
- GI: cosine_hemisphere(n, ...) (L1007). Bad n -> rays miss upward -> emissive-hit term -> 0. Matches symptom.
- Reflection: reflect(-V, n) (L1078). Bad n -> rays all-miss. Matches symptom.
- Shadow: biases along p.sun_dir, NEVER n (comment L921 "bias along sun_dir ONLY, not n"). Unaffected. Matches symptom.
- AO: also uses n (L969). Bug says AO survives — OPEN THREAD (Peter suggests this may be observation-level: AO is the subtle channel, a uniform darkening reads as "still working" if not specifically probed).

`n` is read via the bindless normal_sources buffer (RtNormalSource.vertex_base_addr = vertex_buffer.gpu_address() + vertex_offset, raytrace.rs:1981).

== Mechanism candidates, ranked ==

M1 (FAVORED) — normal_sources stale/invalid read under no-refit. ensure_normal_sources (raytrace.rs:1925) rewrites the CPU-mapped rt_normal_sources buffer every RT-ready frame (render_scene.rs:3976). No useResource: for this buffer (the comment at types.rs:238 argues the bound accel transitively makes BLAS vertex buffers resident — true for vertex/index data referenced by the accel geometry, but normal_sources is a SEPARATE kernel-read buffer, not referenced by the accel structure itself). The STOPGAP's refit opens its own device.raw_queue().commandBuffer() (raytrace.rs:406) — a fresh command buffer that may act as an implicit ordering/coherence point on the queue. Static scene, no refit, no ordering point, CPU-mapped writes become unreliable to the trace dispatch.

M2 — general per-dispatch useResource: absence. dispatch_compute_with_accel (encoder.rs:521) never calls useResource: or useHeap: anywhere in manifold-gpu (verified: only two hits, both comments). The "no separate useResource needed" comment at raytrace.rs:1844 is correct ONLY for resources referenced by the accel geometry, not for gi_materials/normal_sources/params_buffer/obj_motion/material textures. M1 may be a specific instance of M2.

M3 — material_textures table staleness via encoder-bind-cache-invalidation bug class. Plausible per-channel split but symptom is "refls all-miss" (walk_with_alpha_test returns false), not "wrong-colored" — texture staleness produces wrong colors not traversal miss. Less favored.

REJECTED — dispatch-level / queue-ordering theories. Cannot explain why shadow+AO survive in a shared dispatch.

== Why the STOPGAP works under M1/M2 ==

Not because the refit fixes the accel (accel was fine — shadow rays prove it) but because the refit's fresh command buffer is an implicit ordering/coherence point on the queue. Static scene, no refit, no ordering point, CPU-mapped writes unreliable. The STOPGAP's correctness depends on a side effect, not the documented refit contract — why it's a stopgap not a fix.

== Fix shape (lead to steer) ==

1. Declare kernel-read buffers on the trace dispatch via useResource: in dispatch_compute_with_accel (encoder.rs:521) — root fix, removes the dependence on the refit's side-effect ordering. Usage: .read for inputs, .write for the four output textures.
2. CHEAPER EXPERIMENT FIRST: the encoder already has compute_memory_barrier_buffers() (encoder.rs:635). Try one line — encoder.compute_memory_barrier_buffers() before tracer.dispatch_shadow_rays at render_scene.rs:4240, remove the stopgap, run the static-scene harness. If RT stays alive, the root cause was coherence not resource declaration — smaller fix. If only useResource fixes it, it was declaration. Both valid, different layers.
3. Delete STOPGAP (render_scene.rs:4058-4073 + rt_frames_since_refit field).
4. Stale-comment cleanup: "no separate useResource needed" comments at raytrace.rs:1844 and types.rs:238 must be removed/rewritten — they are now wrong.

== Cheapest confirmation experiment ==

3-action decomposition already in BUG-jddy: if M1/M2 is right, the "GPU refit command" action ALONE (enqueue an empty/no-op command buffer on device.raw_queue() between CPU writes and trace dispatch, no instance-buffer rewrite, no flag flip) should keep RT alive. If it does -> M1/M2 confirmed.

== File:line anchors ==

- render_scene.rs:3976 — ensure_normal_sources call (CPU writes normal_sources incl vertex_base_addr, no barrier)
- render_scene.rs:4190 — CPU writes gi_materials via mapped pointer, no barrier
- render_scene.rs:4058-4073 — STOPGAP forced-refit block
- render_scene.rs:4240 — single dispatch_shadow_rays call (shared dispatch)
- raytrace.rs:375-425 — refit_accel opens its own commandBuffer() (suspected implicit ordering point)
- raytrace.rs:885 — n = fetch_interpolated_normal(normal_sources, ...) [GI/refl depend, shadow does not]
- raytrace.rs:921-931 — shadow bias along sun_dir NOT n [the asymmetry]
- raytrace.rs:1007 — GI uses cosine_hemisphere(n, ...)
- raytrace.rs:1078 — Reflection uses reflect(-V, n)
- raytrace.rs:1844 / types.rs:238 — the now-wrong "no separate useResource needed" comments
- encoder.rs:521-626 — dispatch_compute_with_accel never calls useResource:/useHeap:
- encoder.rs:625 — compute_cache.clear() after accel dispatch [encoder-bind-cache-invalidation neighborhood]
- encoder.rs:635 — existing compute_memory_barrier_buffers() [the cheaper-fix primitive]

== Open threads for Fable ==

1. AO-discrepancy — bug says AO survives but AO uses n. Likely observation-level (Peter: "not knowing what I am looking at — potentially"). One targeted probe settles it.
2. M1 (normal_sources-specific) vs M2 (general missing-useResource) — predict same symptom, M2 is the more general hazard M1 sits inside.
3. useResource vs memoryBarrierWithScope — different layers, both valid; cheaper experiment (barrier first) bisects.

title: BUG-326 — rt-depth-snapshot-wrong-on-imported-glb-scenes
description:
### BUG-326 (rt-depth-snapshot-wrong-on-imported-glb-scenes) — RT primary rays miss on imported glb scenes: the depth snapshot holds near-zero values at object pixels, wp reconstruction is garbage, reflections black, AO/shadow degraded
**Status:** OPEN
**Severity:** HIGH — RT reflections unusable on imported hero assets (AMG GT3 renders black with `rt_reflections` on); RT AO/shadows subtly wrong on the same scenes (Peter 2026-07-25: "shadows look odd at times where I would expect AO"). Hand-authored probe scenes pass, which masked this.
**Symptom:** AMG GT3 (`tests/fixtures/gltf/mercedes-amg_gt3__www.vecarz.com.glb`) with RT on + `rt_reflections` on renders black/textureless (non-black fraction 0.024 vs 0.096 baseline). Originally read as Base traced reflections (R1)'s v1 shading gap; the Raster-parity reflections build landed (`7ad9bd36`) and the render stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL, proving the shading change never reached the image.
**Root cause (proven 2026-07-25, K3 kernel-probe chain):** the reflection block is gated on `obj_id >= 0` from the PRIMARY visibility ray (`crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace.rs` `trace_shadow_rays`). On imported glb scenes that ray misses at (almost) every shaded pixel: `opaque_depth_snapshot` holds near-zero values at object pixels (AMG ≈ 0.0003–0.005, DamagedHelmet ≈ 0.009–0.04 — measured via temporary kernel debug writing `depth_tex.read(gpix,0)` into `out_refl`), while the hand-authored R1 grid scene holds proper standard-z ≈ 0.995 at its probe pixel (verified numerically: on=1.1 = depth 0.995 × LUT weight ≈ 1.1). `world_pos_from_depth` (standard-z inverse, far = `>= 1.0-1e-6`) reconstructs near-plane garbage, the `dist*1e-3`-bounded primary ray stops centimetres out and misses, the block's else writes zeros, and the WGSL substitution (`rt_flags.x`) replaces the specular env with those zeros → black. Every shading-path debug variant (albedo-only, env-only, constant env sample) left the render byte-identical, confining the fault to the depth/wp/primary-ray path, NOT the reflection shading (Raster-parity's env-at-hit term is proven live by `rt_r1_reflection::raster_parity_env_at_hit_adds_env_term` on the hand-authored fixture).
**Unknown (next oracle):** WHY imported scenes write tiny depth while hand-authored scenes write standard-z. Suspects, ranked: (a) the import graph's `camera_lens` node (probes lack it) alters the projection the E2a prepass uses vs what `world_pos_from_depth` assumes; (b) the E2a prepass (`render_scene.rs:3762`, `shadow_pipeline` + camera `view_proj`) emits a different z convention for these scenes; (c) synthesized import camera near/far defaults. Cheapest discriminator: add a `camera_lens` node to the R1 grid scene and re-measure probe-pixel depth — a flip to tiny values convicts the lens.
**Fix shape:** depends on (a)/(b)/(c): honour the actual z convention in `world_pos_from_depth` (if scene-variant-but-legitimate), or make the prepass write standard-z (if the convention is a bug). Plus a gpu-proof that renders an IMPORTED glb through the RT path asserting primary-hit coverage above a threshold, so this class can't hide behind hand-authored fixtures again.
**Exonerated (2026-07-25, Flash-lane experiment matrix on the R1 grid fixture, debug-kernel depth readout):** `camera_lens` (depth identical with/without: on=1.1002 both) and import camera params (tilt 0.3/fov 0.9: on=0.7965 = different geometry at the probe pixel, not corrupted depth). Remaining suspects: an untested split between the gpu-test harness path (works) and the render-import/in-app runtime path (broken) — same scene through both paths is the next discriminator — or import-graph content beyond the camera (env nodes, transmission, object count).
**Lead seam review (2026-07-25, k3 — full text `/tmp/manifold_seam_review.md`):** the ENTIRE static write/read path is exonerated element-by-element: one `view_proj` local feeds prepass (3769), raster (3264), and `inv_view_proj` (3979); prepass consumes the SAME `ObjectDraw.uniforms.model` as the raster (3635 shares by reference); `shadow_depth.wgsl` writes plain `clip.z/clip.w` (no remap); the batch CLEARS to 1.0 (encoder.rs:1326 — stale-texture theory dead); snapshot is single-sample Depth32Float with correct usage; RT dispatch binds it at texture(0) with no slot collision; gltf meshes are 48-byte `MeshVertex` soup so `vcount`/stride match. **Geometric contradiction:** tiny standard-z ⟺ object pixels at z ∈ [1.0003·n, 1.04·n] — a mm-thin shell at the near plane, geometrically incompatible with a correctly-framed raster image of a 4.5 m car under ANY single-view perspective; the import auto-frame near (`min(0.05, front_margin·0.5)`, scene.rs:171) analytically yields d ∈ [0.5, 0.98]. So either (A) the GPU prepass draw diverges from the CPU matrix math at draw time (bindings/pipeline/vertex-pull level), (B) runtime `view_proj`/`model` VALUES are degenerate (invisible statically), or (C) texture identity at dispatch ≠ texture written (no static evidence). **Next oracle (lane-delegated one-shot probe):** CPU-project known points with the runtime matrices AND read back the GPU snapshot at the same pixels in ONE render_import run on DamagedHelmet — CPU≈0.98/GPU≈0.003 convicts the draw level (A); CPU≈GPU≈0.003 moves the bug to import scene assembly (B).
**Edge note:** probes can pass for the wrong reason — a far-garbage wp still lets the primary ray cross real geometry because `max_distance` scales with wp distance. Probe fixtures should assert wp sanity (probe-pixel depth in a stated standard-z band), not only final image values.
**Probe round 2 (2026-07-25 PM, Flash lane `bug326-depth-probe`, env-gated `MANIFOLD_BUG326_PROBE` raw readback, commit `a2373535`):** the tiny-depth measurement DOES NOT REPRODUCE with a trustworthy oracle. Raw `copy_texture_to_buffer` readback of `opaque_depth_snapshot` (no PNG/LUT in the path): DamagedHelmet GPU 0.983 vs CPU-expected 0.986; AMG GT3 GPU 0.765 vs CPU 0.741; temporal_upscale on/off identical; global min/max/mean healthy (AMG 0.606/1.0/0.936). Git history shows NO renderer code landed between the morning's tiny-depth measurement and this probe — so the morning's numbers were almost certainly an ARTIFACT of its readout path (depth written into `out_refl`, read back through the tonemapped PNG LUT — scene-exposure-dependent, and the import scenes carry IBL/env the grid scene lacks). The depth-corruption theory of the black render is thereby DEMOTED; the live question is whether the black-render symptom itself (non-black 0.024 vs 0.096, byte-identical across shading variants) still reproduces — round 3 measures that matrix. If it does, the next instrument is a RAW primary-hit/obj_id coverage counter in `trace_shadow_rays` (never a PNG readout).
notes: EVIDENCE CHALLENGED 2026-07-25 (Opus code review, opposite-space pass). The "near-zero depth on imported scenes" number is a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not a depth reading. out_refl is only observable through the shaded image (gpu_proofs/rt_r1_reflection.rs reads final-target luminance), and fs_pbr consumes the substituted value as `specular_ibl = prefiltered * (F0*env_brdf.x + env_brdf.y)` (render_scene.wgsl:1541). Every debug value written into out_refl is therefore scaled by that per-pixel split-sum weight. The R1 grid probes weight ~1.1 (ground material metallic 1.0 / roughness 0.01 / albedo 0.8 — the "LUT weight ~1.1" already noted in the R1 handoff); imported dielectric/dark-metal materials weight 0.001-0.05. 0.995 x 1.1 = 1.1 (grid), 0.99 x 0.04 = 0.04 (DamagedHelmet), 0.995 x 0.003 = 0.003 (AMG). The whole 300-3000x "wrong depth" spread is the material weight. Suspects (a) camera_lens, (b) prepass z convention, (c) near/far defaults are aimed at an artifact — do not spend the morning there without first reading the depth snapshot DIRECTLY (readback of opaque_depth_snapshot, or a full-frame constant write into out_refl) rather than through fs_pbr. ALSO: the "raster-parity build left the render BYTE-IDENTICAL" evidence is weak, not proof the change never reached the image. Asset facts (read from tests/fixtures/gltf/mercedes-amg_gt3__www.vecarz.com.glb, 78 materials, NO metallicRoughness textures — all factors): the largest group is roughness 0.958, and ~half the materials sit above the refl cutoff+band (0.6+0.1), so those pixels take the no-ray above-cutoff branch (raytrace.rs:1067-1070) and never cast a reflection ray at all; the raster-parity change only touched the reflection-ray HIT branch, and on a hero car over a void background most rays that DO cast escape to the env miss branch. Byte-identity is expected either way. THIRD: metallicFactor is 1.0 on ~90% of the AMG materials, so the car is a full metal in fs_pbr — no diffuse term, its entire appearance IS the specular-env fetch RT substitutes. That is why a zero from RT paints this asset literally black while a dielectric test scene would only look dull; it is an amplifier of the fault, not the fault. Related new bug: BUG-88m (substitution domain wider than trace domain — Blend/Mask objects get out_refl=0 by construction).

title: BUG-156 — fluidsim3d-4k-perf-regression-suspect-bug066-fix
description:
### BUG-156 (fluidsim3d-4k-perf-regression-suspect-bug066-fix) — FluidSim3D no longer holds smooth 60FPS at 4K — HIGH, reported by Peter 2026-07-14
**Status:** OPEN — found not fixed 2026-07-14, reported by Peter during live-rig use.

**Symptom** — FluidSim3D used to run smoothly at 60FPS at 4K output resolution; it no longer does. Peter suspects this is a regression from the BUG-066 fix.

**Root cause** — unknown, not investigated this session, but the suspected culprit is well-formed: BUG-066's fix (`eebac94d`, see the closed entry in `docs/archive/BUG_BACKLOG_CLOSED.md`) resized `edge_slope_3d`/`swirl_force_3d`'s (and the other volume nodes') dispatch grids from `div_ceil(8)` (legacy 8×8×8 workgroup) to `div_ceil(4)` against the freeze codegen's actual `@workgroup_size(4,4,4)` for 3D-volume kernels. Correcting the grid size to match the real workgroup was necessary for correctness (forces were only landing in 1/8th of the volume before), but going from an 8³ to a 4³ workgroup at the same volume resolution means 8x more dispatched workgroups per volume kernel — a real, expected throughput cost of the fix, not an incidental one. Whether that 8x is actually what's landing on the frame budget (vs. some other change since, or the 4³ workgroup being genuinely suboptimal occupancy for this GPU) is unverified.

**Fix shape** — profile FluidSim3D at 4K with the profiler (`manifold-profiler`) to confirm the volume-node dispatches (`edge_slope_3d`, `swirl_force_3d`, and any other 3D-volume kernel sized off `VOLUME_WORKGROUP_3D`) are where the frame time went, comparing against a pre-`eebac94d` build if needed to isolate it from unrelated changes since. If confirmed, the fix is not "revert BUG-066" (that reintroduces the top-right-quadrant forces bug) — it's making the corrected dispatch cheap again: a larger workgroup size for the 3D volume kernels (if occupancy/shared-memory allows), or reducing per-workgroup overhead, while keeping the grid sized correctly against whatever workgroup size is actually emitted.

title: BUG-297 — multi-session-memory-exhaustion-freezes-machine
description:
### BUG-297 (multi-session-memory-exhaustion-freezes-machine) — concurrent Claude Code sessions jetsam the machine; indistinguishable from BUG-290's GPU freeze from the user's seat
**Status:** PARTIAL (logged 2026-07-21; worktree Spotlight exclusion landed 2026-07-21, Opus Workstream 1). Mitigated earlier same session: two stale rust-analyzer instances flagged for kill; analyzer LRU caps landed.

**Worktree Spotlight exclusion — DONE + VERIFIED (2026-07-21, Opus WS1):** the entry's fix-shape (d) is now implemented durably for the worktree vector. `scripts/agent-worktree.py::ensure_spotlight_exclusion()` drops `.metadata_never_index` at the pool root (`.claude/worktrees/`) on every `acquire`, excluding the entire subtree — all six slots, their `target/` dirs, and checkouts — from Spotlight (Apple-documented per-directory-tree exclusion, no sudo). It sits ABOVE `target/` so `cargo clean` never removes it, and is recreated on acquire so it survives the pool dir being deleted/recreated; the marker lives in gitignored space, so the script IS its version-controlled source of truth (no reliance on a manual System-Settings privacy entry that a fresh clone or a forgetful setup would miss). Chosen over the `.cargo/config.toml` `target-dir = "target.noindex"` rename because that needs a repo-wide audit of hardcoded `target/` paths (a Peter decision) and doesn't cover checkouts. **Verification (no sudo):** before the marker, a worktree `target/` `.rlib` resolved content attributes; after dropping it, the whole `.claude/worktrees` tree returns nothing from `mdfind`, and `mds_stores` — which spiked to ~80% CPU / 500MB RSS while it pruned the newly-excluded ~114GB subtree — fell to **0.0% CPU / 157MB RSS** within 30s and stayed there; `memory_pressure` held ~85% free throughout. That mds spike-then-idle is the exclusion being honored (mds did the pruning work, then stopped touching the tree).

**Remains (honest):** (1) the brief's end-to-end proof — memory_pressure logged during a REAL concurrent gate wave — was deliberately NOT manufactured this session: Peter is actively on the machine and it hard-locks under load, so fabricating a heavy wave purely to observe pressure is the wrong risk. The imminent Workstream-2 bug-debt wave (real gates under the serialize constraint) is the natural place to capture it. (2) The Spotlight vector is now fully closed: **Peter confirmed (2026-07-21) the whole repo is already in the System-Settings Spotlight privacy list** — which is why mdfind returned no repo file. That manual entry covers the immediate churn (worktrees AND main-checkout `target/`); the landed `.metadata_never_index` script fix is the durable/portable layer on top — it survives a fresh clone or another machine and doesn't depend on the per-machine privacy entry being re-added. No sudo attribution or fix-shape (d) `.cargo/config.toml` rename is needed while the privacy entry stands; if Peter ever removes it, the worktree pool stays excluded (script) but the main-checkout `target/` would reindex (that vector would then want a durable lever of its own).
**Recurrence 2026-07-21 (evening, Opus-orchestration session):** repeated HARD lockups while an Opus mid-orchestrator ran landing-review loads (full-workspace nextest + repeated `ui-snap` flow runs = Metal GPU renders) concurrently with Peter using the machine. Peter: "has been investigated and attempted to be fixed a few times" — the mitigations to date have NOT held. NEEDS A DEDICATED INVESTIGATION SESSION with the machine instrumented (memory_pressure log + gpuEve/JetsamEvent correlation DURING an orchestration wave, per this entry's and BUG-290's separation protocol) rather than another post-hoc guess. Until fixed, orchestration sessions should treat "Peter is actively using this machine" as a reason to serialize heavy gates (one workspace nextest at a time, no parallel flow sweeps).
**Severity:** HIGH — same "whole macbook locks up" symptom as BUG-290, and it MASKS BUG-290's conviction: a freeze during a test run proves nothing until the two mechanisms are separated.
**Symptom:** `JetsamEvent-2026-07-21-100109.ips` — machine froze while another agent session ran the full landing gate (workspace clippy + deny + nextest) with NO gpu-proofs involved and NO new gpuEvent. Top consumers at jetsam: FOUR rust-analyzer instances (4.56 + 4.09 + 4.04 + 3.08 GB ≈ 16 GB — one per live Claude Code session on this workspace) plus rustc + nextest process trees. Prior art: `JetsamEvent-2026-07-17-184945.ips` fired 9 min after that day's gpuEvent — both mechanisms were live that evening.
**Root cause:** each session's LSP plugin spawns a private rust-analyzer (~3–4.5 GB warm on this workspace); N sessions + one workspace-scale build/test run exceeds RAM, and macOS thrash + jetsam reads as a total lockup. Stale sessions (12–14 h old tmux panes) keep their analyzers resident.

**Instrumented-session findings (2026-07-21, Fable, morning after the 2026-07-20-evening lockups):**
- **The evening lockups left NO JetsamEvent and NO gpuEvent.** Neither convicted mechanism fingerprinted. The kernel DID enter memory pressure 20:46–20:55 (unified log: `killing_idle_process` osr_code 9 × 4, plus `knowledgeconstructiond` per-process kill) — but desktop macOS does not jetsam regular apps; it **thrashes** (compressor + swap saturation), which presents as a total hard lockup with no diagnostic report. That is the working mechanism for the "indistinguishable from BUG-290" freezes. GPU saturation from concurrent `ui-snap` Metal renders stalling WindowServer remains a possible co-mechanism (also reportless when no fault fires).
- **NEW convicted contributor: Spotlight.** `mds_stores_2026-07-21-000154.diag`: mds_stores dirtied **8.6 GB of file-backed writes over 20:57→00:00** — exactly the orchestration-gate window. Spotlight indexing is fully enabled with zero exclusions, and the repo has SIX worktrees each with its own `target/`; every gate build makes Spotlight re-index gigabytes of artifacts (CPU + IO + page-cache pressure on top of the build itself). `rustc` itself held a CPU-resource violation 20:23–21:31.
- The 10:01 JetsamEvent (morning) was `knowledgeconstructiond` hitting its own per-process limit with ~4 GB still free — pressure, not exhaustion; the four rust-analyzers (4.6/4.1/4.0/3.1 GB) are confirmed in its process table.
- `rust-analyzer-2026-07-21-102454.ips` is a codesigning **Launch Constraint Violation** SIGKILL (binary launched from `/private/tmp/*/rust-analyzer`) — unrelated to memory; note 0 analyzers were alive at 11:45 with 8 claude sessions open, so analyzers respawn on demand only.
- **Instrumentation:** an always-on 10 s sampler was installed then REMOVED same day at Peter's request (too intrusive). If a future wave needs the second-by-second record, run it wave-scoped only: the orchestrator starts a loop logging `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` + `vm.swapusage` + top-12 RSS every 10 s at wave start and kills it at wave end. Nothing is running now.
**Fix shape:** (a) protocol — only the landing session runs `--workspace` gates (already the rule; today's run by a second agent violated it); (b) hygiene — kill rust-analyzer in idle/stale sessions (respawns on demand); (c) structural — investigate capping rust-analyzer memory (`lru.capacity` / `RA_LRU_CAP` env, cache priming off) or sharing/disabling analyzers in worker sessions; (d) **exclude build dirs from Spotlight** — root option: `build.target-dir = "target.noindex"` in the workspace `.cargo/config.toml` (`.noindex` suffix is the reliable modern exclusion; needs a repo-wide audit for hardcoded `target/` paths first — Peter decision), quick option: Peter adds both repo roots to System Settings → Spotlight → Search Privacy; (e) when a freeze occurs, check `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` for gpuEvent vs JetsamEvent AND the unified log for `memorystatus` kernel lines around the freeze time — thrash leaves NO diagnostic report, so no-report + kernel pressure lines = this bug, not BUG-290.

title: BUG-290 — gpu-proofs-test-binary-faults-gpu-firmware
description:
### BUG-290 (gpu-proofs-test-binary-faults-gpu-firmware) — a `manifold_renderer` test binary triggered an AGX GPU fault/restart; whole-display freezes on Peter's machine correlate with GPU test runs
**Status:** OPEN, hardening LANDED 2026-07-21 @ `7cacb965` (cross-process flock in `test_device()` kills the concurrent-process trigger class; `sg_blur_dynamic` radius clamped at 2048 kills the wired-garbage watchdog class). Remaining to close: the conviction run — ONE isolated `cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs smoke -- --test-threads=1` with Peter present (freezes-alone ⇒ single bad kernel still live; clean ⇒ concurrency was the trigger, downgrade + monitor).
**Severity:** HIGH — stage risk by class: a compute dispatch that can fault GPU firmware in a test could do the same from the live app mid-show. Also the likely cause of Peter's "whole screen freezes, machine still alive" reports.
**Symptom:** whole machine (all displays, WindowServer, ghostty/tmux) freezes during GPU test runs, recovers after seconds. Two distinct firmware fault classes on record (both bug_type 284):
- `gpuEvent-manifold_rendere-2026-07-17-184055.ips` — restart_reason 3 **"BIF0 page fault"**, `is_read=true`, address 4398052055936, guilty_dm 3: a kernel READ an unmapped GPU address (OOB read or GPU-side use-after-free). Directly attributed to a `manifold_renderer` test binary.
- `gpuEvent-<unknown>-2026-07-18-133620.ips` — restart_reason 2 **"progress timeout"**, command_buffer_trace_id -1: a dispatch outran the firmware watchdog (runaway/unbounded loop). Process unattributed.
**Root cause:** unknown; two independent classes to convict. Facts established 2026-07-21: `GPU_TEST_LOCK` (`manifold-renderer/src/lib.rs:87` `test_device()`) is a `static` in-process ReentrantMutex — **zero cross-process serialization**, so nextest (process-per-test) or two concurrent agent sessions running GPU work defeat it entirely; concurrent-dispatch pressure is a live trigger hypothesis (Peter observed another agent running nextest around freeze times). Readback paths use `commit_and_wait_completed` (no test callers of `commit_and_wait_scheduled`), so simple drop-before-complete on the readback path is NOT confirmed. Static audit (Codex gpt-5.4-mini pass + Fable verification, 2026-07-21): `wgsl_compute.rs` `evaluate()` (~:2324) dispatches user-supplied WGSL with no host-side bounds guard — the widest OOB surface by class; `separable_gaussian_body.wgsl:94` `sg_blur_dynamic` derives its loop bound from `i32(radius)` **unclamped** (linear branch clamps to 32 at :133) — verified real, but current gpu-proofs exercise only the clamped linear mode; Plasma's `octaves = 3u + u32(cx*2.0)` loop was flagged but is 3–5 iterations for in-range complexity (saturating cast) — weak. No specific kernel convicted yet. Prior art: `agx-0x78-crash` memory, `ui-present-content-gpu-contention`.
**Fix shape:** (1) enforce cross-process GPU test exclusion — OS-level file lock inside `test_device()` alongside `GPU_TEST_LOCK`, and/or hook-deny `nextest` with `gpu-proofs` — kills the concurrency trigger class regardless of which kernel faulted; (2) clamp `sg_blur_dynamic`'s radius like the linear branch; (3) convict with ONE isolated run (`cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs smoke -- --test-threads=1`, nothing else touching the GPU): freezes-alone ⇒ single bad kernel, clean-alone ⇒ concurrency trigger. Requires Peter present — a successful repro freezes the machine. Until fixed: never run gpu-proofs while performing/recording or while another session may touch the GPU.

title: App startup pipeline warmup takes ~3 min every launch despite the on-disk pipeline archive
description:
Symptom: every manifold launch spends 160-181s in the startup warmup pass, and it hits its time limit before finishing (rt-capture logs: "warmup pass took 168294ms (completed=false)", 181330ms, 159945ms, on three back-to-back runs of the same binary, 2026-10-07). The RT noise gate launches the app once per capture, so a 6-capture re-baseline costs ~20 min of warmup alone; Peter pays it on every app launch too.

Root cause: unknown. crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/archive.rs already wraps MTLBinaryArchive to cache compiled pipelines on disk, so the second launch should be near-free. Suspects: (1) the archive is not saved, or is saved to a path that is not reloaded; (2) the archive only covers the Metal compile step, and the real cost is our WGSL->MSL translation and codegen, which nothing caches; (3) pipeline descriptors differ run to run (for example codegen output not deterministic), so archive lookups miss.

Fix shape: time one launch with a warm archive and split the warmup into translate vs Metal compile to pick the suspect. Then cache whichever step is uncached, keyed by shader source hash, so only the first launch after a shader change pays. Verify: second rt-capture launch logs warmup well under 10s with completed=true.

title: Whitewater floats above the water surface when surface shaping params are pushed
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-07, Water — Dam Break (GPU FLIP), screenshot: Surface Particle Scale 1.2, Stretch 8.13, Centre Smoothing 0.45, Smoothing Iterations 2): foam and other whitewater particles hover above the rendered water mesh instead of sitting on it. Root cause: unknown, not reproduced. Leading suspect: two different surfaces. whitewater_step classifies and places foam against the solver level and solid grids, while the rendered mesh comes from liquid_blobs (particle_scale, stretch, smoothing) then liquid_smooth_mesh and liquid_mesh_relaxation. Stretch, centre smoothing and Laplacian smoothing all pull the displayed surface inward, so foam that is correctly on the simulated surface ends up above the visible one. Check first how FLIP Fluids keeps foam on its smoothed mesh (whether it accepts the gap at default settings or offsets foam), per follow-industry-standards. Fix shape candidates: keep foam on the displayed surface (project or offset foam against the display mesh level), or bound the display surface drift from the sim surface. Oracle: fluid_capture renders at default vs these settings, measure foam height above the display mesh.

title: Whitewater: lowering Whitewater Budget mid-run leaves existing whitewater stuck
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-07, Water — Dam Break (GPU FLIP)): once whitewater exists, lowering the Whitewater Budget does not remove it. The existing foam/spray/bubbles stay stuck in the scene. Only Reset then lowering the budget clears it. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: the budget only caps new emission (spawn_whitewater_body.wgsl reads capacity), so the live population above the new cap is never trimmed; the lifecycle storage (whitewater_lifecycle.rs) grows in 4,096 steps but may never shrink, and the age/keep passes may stop touching particles whose index is past the new capacity, so they neither move nor die. Check what FLIP Fluids does when its max whitewater particle limit drops mid-sim before choosing the fix. Fix shape: a budget change trims or retires the population above the new cap in one defined operation, never leaves particles outside the stepped range; a CPU reference test that lowers capacity mid-run and asserts the population falls to the cap and every survivor still advects.

title: GPU FLIP water with no air: sealed tanks and pressed lids
description: One family: water fully enclosed with no air anywhere. FLIP Fluids gives sealed water no push from a solid (pressuresolver.cpp:214); we pin one cell per sealed pocket instead. Constraint: water is never deleted at a solid (D19), so the engine rule of deleting what a lid sweeps does not port. First step: compare the engine sealed-pocket handling with ours on the full sealed tank, then port. Members: dry patch in a full tank, lid churn, pressed-lid solve cap, one-cell pin.

title: Liquid colliders sample a fixed 32-node distance field and hull pieces, so FLIP water misses photoscan rock
description: Symptom: in Ocean Cliff the GPU FLIP water reads as clipping into or stopping short of the cliff scan. Root cause (read, not yet confirmed by a still): fluid_role_source builds each collider as convex hull pieces (Collider Detail, up to 64), and fluid_role.rs build_distance samples their union on DISTANCE_NODES_ALONG_LONGEST = 32 nodes along the longest side, whatever the water grid (about 7 cm at Res 128). Hulls bridge every hollow and the field blurs the rock. Also, in OceanCliff.json the back cliff is drawn whole but only fragments 0 and 2 have colliders; 3 crashes the hull cook (BUG-ra759, hull assert) and 1 is missing for unknown reasons, so water can pass through those parts. Fix shape: for fixed colliders skip hulls and build the signed distance straight from the scan triangles (the builder already signs by generalized winding number, which tolerates open meshes; relax validate_closed_mesh for this path), at a spacing tied to the liquid cell size. Hulls stay for moving Box3D bodies. Oracle: a still of the solid field drawn over the scan, before and after.

title: Delete key on one part of an imported model deletes the whole model; the part's ✕ button deletes only that part
description: Symptom: selecting one part (submesh row) of an imported glTF compound and pressing Delete, or choosing Delete from the context menu, removes the entire model. The part's ✕ button removes just that part. Root cause: keyboard and menu Delete go through remove_selection_action -> RemoveSceneObjectCommand, whose group branch removes every slot of the group, while the ✕ button routes to RemoveSceneSubmesh. Fix shape: remove_selection_action routes a compound part to the same submesh removal as its ✕ button, with a test covering button, keyboard and context menu agreeing for a part row. Found during the water family F1b review.

title: Camera Sky: visible seam where the HDRI wraps (looking along -x)
description: Symptom: Camera Sky draws a thin vertical seam in the sky when the camera looks along -x. Root cause: the equirect lookup u = atan2(d.z, d.x)/2pi + 0.5 wraps at u=0/1, but the sampler is GpuSamplerDesc::default() (ClampToEdge on U), so bilinear filtering at the seam clamps instead of wrapping. Found by Astra review of feat/ocean-cliff. Fix shape: repeat on U, clamp on V for the standalone pipeline (camera_sky.rs run) and the fused path (the sampler the freeze codegen binds for this input), plus a GPU proof that renders a ray straddling the seam and checks it against a wrapped CPU bilinear reference. None of the Ocean Cliff hero cameras sees -x, so the shipped renders are unaffected.

title: GPU FLIP light box: accept the engine trim under a bobbing box, or let particles slide along solids
description: Residual of BUG-beblk (water drains under a light Moving box). title: Handover bound for ticks where the body touches a support
description: D18 bounds every tick at 0.5 mm, 5 mm/s, 0.1 deg. The law is exact for free bodies but a rigid-contact predictor when touching: Box3D soft contacts slip about 1.3 cm/s further on the first tick of a slide from rest, and a contact Box3D finds inside the step is unknown at the tick start (measured 0.6-0.8 mm, 2-5 cm/s on MPM lift-off ticks). Astra (2026-10-06) and the lead recommend: keep the strict bound for contact-free ticks; for contact ticks bound the boundary displacement |dx| + R|dtheta| and dt x boundary velocity error |dv| + R|domega| against a declared fraction of the water cell; report contacts found inside the step separately. Peter to choose.

title: Body handoff: supports between two coupled bodies (box on box)
description: Deferred by Peter 2026-10-06 until after the body handoff lands. liquid_submerged_stack on GPU FLIP: three boxes at 1.5x water density stacked under 1 m, 2.40% of the water lost (was 10% before the handoff work), top box still moving 1.33 cm/s over the last 2 s. support_points skips dynamic supports, so an upper box is free in the pressure solve and sinks into the box below the way a lone box sank into the floor before D16. Shape: a joint prediction with linked mobility across touching coupled bodies (the constrained mobility over the stack as one block), proven against Box3D on a two-box stack in coupled_motion tests, then the GPU twin. docs/LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md D16 "Not yet". Conformance exemption to remove when done: GPU FLIP SubmergedStack in liquid/conformance.rs.

title: MPM floats boxes about 3.5 cm low and drifts at rest
description: Symptom: liquid_floating_draft on MPM (node.matter_domain): centre 0.4846 m against waterline 0.5246, draft error -0.640 cells (bound half a cell). liquid_floating_rest on MPM: density 0.5 box centre 0.969 / 0.965 / 0.965 m against 1.000 at 15 / 30 / 60 Hz, RMS motion about 0.05 m/s, drift 3.5 cm in 3 s; density 0.05 box drifts 9-10 cm. Pre-existing but hidden on main: the old impulse-before-the-step handoff pushed floating bodies up by an amount growing with the tick (MPM half-density centre 1.067 / 1.042 / 1.017 at 15 / 30 / 60 Hz), which put the draft inside the bound (+0.208 cells). D17 (reaction as a steady force over the step) removed that; heights are now the same at every rate, about 3.5 cm low. Root cause unknown. Suspects: the waterline read for MPM (the test takes the particle top plus a quarter cell) against the true free surface of a weakly compressible pool; buoyancy near a surface-piercing body short of the fully submerged case (liquid_hydrostatic_lift passes within 5%); the per-substep body move (matter_move_bodies_body.wgsl) against Box3D now integrating the reaction as a steady force. Conformance exemptions to remove when fixed: MPM FloatingDraft and FloatingRest in liquid/conformance.rs.

title: GPU FLIP floating boxes keep bobbing at rest and float about a cell high
description: Symptom: liquid_floating_rest on GPU FLIP (REST tank, dx 0.05). Density 0.05 box: RMS motion 0.166 / 0.024 / 0.013 m/s at 15 / 30 / 60 Hz over the rest window, centre 1.2355 / 1.2285 / 1.2257 m against 1.1800. Density 0.5 box: RMS 0.036 / 0.014 / 0.005 m/s, centre 1.048 / 1.031 / 1.027 against 1.000. Bound: 1 cm/s RMS and centre within a cell. Pre-existing: the P13 red run had RMS 0.45 / 0.18 / 0.09 and the same heights (1.225-1.235, 1.024-1.030). The body handoff is exact on these boxes (D18 handover error 1e-7 m, 3e-8 m/s), so the cause is in the liquid. Root cause unknown. Suspects: buoyancy measured against a surface standing 0.54-0.62 cells above the top particle (gpu_flip_step.wgsl particle_distance, union of balls of radius sqrt(3)*dx/2) so a box rides high; the bob at 15 Hz is one coupling exchange per 66 ms tick for a very light body (added-mass instability of explicit exchange, worst at low mass ratio). Also makes the FloatingAt fixtures start near rest so liquid_handover_agreement reads under 1 cm of travel. Conformance exemption to remove when fixed: GPU FLIP FloatingRest in liquid/conformance.rs.

title: GPU FLIP: water volume drains while a light Moving box sits on the floor
description: Symptom (Peter, 2026-10-06, res 32, /Users/peterkiemann/Downloads/waterLossTest.manifold): with a box3d physics object on Moving (density 20, friction 0.5, bounce 0.15), the water volume drops over time; the box feels stuck to the floor and jittery. Root cause unknown; nothing has been run yet. Suspects, read from code only: (1) faces_to_particles in gpu_flip_step.wgsl removes any particle still inside a solid after resolve_solid. In the wedge between a box resting on the floor and the floor, the push out of the box lands in the floor or wall, is refused, and the particle is deleted. Each twitch of the box sweeps fresh water into that wedge. (2) Density 20 (2% of water) is the unstable light-body case for two-way coupling: added-mass buzz, plus noisy lift in shallow res-32 water, plus stick-slip on Coulomb friction. First oracle: run the file headless and log the live particle count per tick, box Moving vs Static, then again at density 500. Fix shape depends on which of these it is.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text:
Measured 2026-10-06 (headless `manifold frame-time <file> --frames 1800 --frame-clock`, RUST_LOG=gpu_flip::schedule=debug, live count per retired tick; Sim Rate 30 Hz, one liquid step per tick). Live particles after ~30 s, from 42,524:
- Moving, density 20: 8,402 (80% gone, steady drain)
- Fixed, density 20: 42,524 (no loss)
- Moving, density 500: 27,723 (35% gone; still draining ~22/tick after the box comes to rest on the floor)
- Fill height 1.0 m so the box floats (from 82,668): density 500 lost 8; density 20 lost 2,054 (box pressed against the back wall)
Every other removal path is ruled out for this scene: all walls closed, no outflow regions, push_refused 0, speed limit far above the water's speed, crowding cap 250/cell.
Verdict: suspect (1) confirmed in refined form: water is deleted only where a dynamic box touches the floor or a wall (the inside-solid rule), not in open water. Suspect (2) killed as the cause, kept as an amplifier: density 20 drains 2.3x faster and never settles (body speed 0.3-0.7 m/s above the gravity term for the whole run), density 500 settles.
Unproven: which resolve_solid branch deletes (push lands in floor/wall and is clamped back into the box, vs the box twitching over water). Next oracle: a temporary per-branch deletion counter, plus the same scene in CPU FLIP to see whether the engine drains too.
Code-read suspects for the root, unmeasured: the liquid predicts each body as v + external accel * t + its own reaction, so Box3D floor/wall contacts are invisible within a tick (a resting box is told to the water as falling at up to g/30 = 0.33 m/s); a box flush on the floor has no water cell beneath it at 12.5 cm cells, so it gets no lift however light (stuck to the floor). Fix shape is pending a talk with Peter.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Still pool, 1 m deep, no dam: a density-2000 box resting dead still on the floor (motion under 1 mm/s) drains 717 particles/s at Sim Rate 30, 429/s at 60, 904/s at 15; 66% of the water in 60 s at 30 Hz. Density 500 ends on the floor and drains the same. So the drain needs no body motion. It grows with tick length, which fits the water predicting a resting body as falling at g*dt (contacts invisible), but it is not proportional and 60 Hz still drains, so that is probably not the whole cause. A Fixed box (no prediction) drains nothing.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Measured 2026-10-06 on feat/liquid-body-handoff with the v1.20.0 contacts-wire upgrade (saved projects had no domain.contacts to step.contacts wire, so the support fix never reached them; the upgrade adds it on load). Headless frame-time, live particles: still2000 65532 to 65532 (was 22061 on main), still500 65532 to 65532 (was 22611), moving20 (light density-20 box on Moving, 30 Hz, 1800 frames) 42524 to 36186 (was 7585 on main, 16185 on the branch without the wire). Still boxes: fixed. Light moving box: 15% still lost, mostly 2.7 s to 8 s while the dam wave throws the box, then about 1 particle a tick. push_refused 0 throughout, all faces closed, max particle speed under 5 m/s (speed removal needs about 9 m/s), so the remaining path is unknown: suspects are crowded-marker removal (over 250 per cell where push-out stacks water against the box) or the narrow-band delete. Next oracle: a per-path removal counter in the tick stats.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Landed on main 4e26ff403 (body handoff P13-P16 plus the v1.20.0 contacts-wire rung). Still boxes hold all their water; the light moving box residual (15%) stays open here.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Measured 2026-10-06 on main 4e26ff403 (temporary probes, reverted): all of the light moving box's residual loss is the engine's crowding trim (remove_crowded_markers, over 250 particles a cell); with the trim off, moving20 keeps 42524 of 42524. 98% of the trimmed cells sit directly under the box (combined solid gradient pointing down), within 2 cells; the water in this scene is only about 2.5 cells deep. Not the cause: the collision shape posed without this step's reaction (re-posing it changed nothing: 36147 vs 36186 left), nor the solve's shape posed without the water's support (8205 trimmed vs 6363). title: Mesh relaxation on packed positions inside smooth_surface_mesh
description: smooth_surface_mesh + surface_mesh_normals + volume_surface_mesh cost about 2.6 ms of a 33 ms frame at res 64 and 12.4 ms at 128 (stamp ratios, 2026-10-06). Each Jacobi pass reads and writes the 80-byte MeshVertex. Idea from the parked surface stage design (docs/archive/LIQUID_SURFACE_STAGE_DESIGN.md D6, with Astra review corrections in section 10 (Measured, parked)): relax over a packed 16-byte position buffer and write MeshVertex once with normals. Treat as a numerical rewrite: same neighbour order, attributes, index tails, iteration-zero and overflow semantics; f64 references and frame-hash comparison; Peter approves any changed output. Measure first: split stamps for relax vs normals vs emit.

title: physics_boxes proof switches offline to live mid-run; its retained-backlog check is obsolete
description: Symptom: tests/gpu_proofs/physics_boxes.rs:160 physics_boxes_render_motion_and_latch_count_until_reset gets 0 bodies instead of 4003, with graph error "physics input history cannot move backward within an epoch" (Oct 6 nightly). Root cause (Astra, read-only): the test renders to frame 185 offline, then adds a live zero-budget scope around frame 215 without a reset, and its backlog_seconds > 0.45 checks contradict the adopted dropped-time rule (from eaa16ecf3/8c73d108b). Fix shape: make the overload fixture live from frame one; assert retained bodies plus bounded accepted steps and dropped time. The backward-history error it exposes is a separate defect, logged on its own bead; never accept zero bodies as the result.

title: node_error_fails_the_frame relies on a resolution refusal that no longer exists
description: Symptom: tests/gpu_proofs/node_error_status.rs:69 node_error_fails_the_frame gets Complete instead of Failed(NodeError) on main (Oct 6 nightly). Root cause (Astra, read-only): the test triggers its node error by asking GPU FLIP for a resolution the solver was not built for, but 8286d25c3 deliberately removed that refusal (runtime-resizable storage; resolution 32 is supported, gpu_flip_preset.rs:1318-1329). The real contract, a node reporting ctx.error fails the frame so export never accepts fallback output, is still in execution.rs:2565-2569 and is now untested. Fix shape: use a deterministic node that reports ctx.error on purpose; keep the Failed(NodeError) expectation. Test-only change.

title: GPU FLIP over-noding: fold surface mesh, whitewater internals and no-op passes into optimised stage kernels
description: Astra audit 2026-10-06 (read-only, Peter asked: "find if we are over noding ... instead of writing sensible optimised compute kernels. Users won't touch these GPU FLIP nodes"). Solver stage boundary (gpu_flip_step) is right; render is not over-noded. All savings unmeasured; bit-identical targets unless noted. Ranked after the approved particle_volume gather: (1) mesh rebuild as one stage (count/edge-count/offsets/volume_surface_mesh/smooth_surface_mesh/surface_mesh_normals): mesher computes gradient normals that the final normals pass replaces; relaxation moves 80-byte vertices when only positions change; keep positions packed, assemble once, keep separate Jacobi iterations and final normals; preserve original UVs. (2) whitewater_step runs ~15 internal standalone atoms: emitter chain 7->1, spawn+classify 2->1, advect+retype+age 3->1 (nine dispatches per tick), keep RNG streams and order. (3) surface no-op passes: with Fill Pits 0 and Smoothing 0, grow/redistance/shrink/smooth x,y,z pass through, and the final clamp repeats particle_volume's own solid clamp; a surface stage bypasses them (replaces the parked array-passthrough P3 of PARTICLE_VOLUME_BRICK_GATHER_DESIGN.md). (4) unused copies: liquid_frame publishes face components nobody reads (3 dispatches + 3 history blits per publication); whitewater reads 3 face_sample_component arrays it could sample packed; two zero-padding pad_distance_lattice copies and an influence ping-pong copy in whitewater. (5) solver: particle_distance -> phi_into_solids -> water_from_phi as one cell kernel on the normal path (2 dispatches per substep). (6) spherical-blob fast path: build blobs in the sort's final pass (1 dispatch, 64 B/particle). Unified grid: share solid distance with nearest-object metadata (static scenes now; moving bodies need timestamped fields); do NOT replace whitewater liquid_cells with solver water (the engine also keeps its own diffuse material grid; replacing changes typing, away from parity). Other presets with the same surface chain: WaterDamBreakGpu, WaterStillPoolMatter, WaterDamBreakMatter, WaterFloatingBoxMatter; WaterDamBreakParticles has the whitewater pattern. Next: a design doc per stage (mesh stage, whitewater fusion, surface bypass + unused copies), Astra review, measured A/B per landing.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Progress: item (2) and the whitewater parts of (4) shipped with the whitewater stage fusion (docs/WHITEWATER_STAGE_FUSION_DESIGN.md (whitewater stage fusion) P1-P5): emitter chain, spawn and lifecycle fused, face adapters and pad/influence copies gone. Open: (1) mesh rebuild stage, (3) surface no-op passes, (5) solver cell kernel, (6) blob fast path.

title: GPU FLIP pressure cap 900: slowest-frame (p95) tick interval rose 2.4 ms on the Dam Break oracle
description: Symptom: interleaved bundled A/B on gpu_flip_dam_break.manifold (3 pairs, GPU lock), main 5a1218c89 vs lane/pressure-cap-template b9489677d: tick interval p50 30.46 vs 30.49 ms (same), p95 38.8 vs 41.2 ms in every pair. Root cause unknown. Suspects: (a) hard frames now run rounds past the old cap of 64 (accuracy cost, accepted by the cap-900 decision); (b) chunked template overhead (guarded tail past the stop, geometric chunks up to 32); (c) direct-path frames. Earlier C4/C5 measurement at chunk 32 showed only +0.8 ms p95. Fix shape: one node-granularity stamped run on both sides, split tick frames by solve iteration count; if (a), document as the cost of the cap; if (b), tune the chunk ladder (design doc section 11 (Deferred), chunk maximum tuning). Logs: scratchpad bb6z42ag4 output in session d130fcf5.

title: GPU FLIP oracle: ~9 ms GPU stall spikes land on whatever node runs (p95)
description: Symptom: on the Dam Break oracle the calm-phase p95 of render_scene (8.96), project_extend (8.83) and liquid_frame (8.67) are all ~9 ms while their p50s are 0.7-1.5 ms; Fable (2026-10-06 audit) reads it as a per-frame GPU stall landing on whichever node is running, not node work. Root cause unknown; suspects: GPU timestamp clock pause (profiling.rs:378-386 note), memory pressure from the 16-slot display history, an occasional large buffer upload. Oracle: print per-stamped-frame per-node spans and check the spikes share a frame; then a Metal capture of a spike frame.

title: GPU FLIP Dam Break: drawing-side GPU cost targets (whitewater liquid cells, particle volume, transparent render)
description: Measured 2026-10-06 on the Dam Break oracle (res 64, 30 Hz, node-stamped frames; stamps inflate ~1.4x, so real ms ~ value/1.4). Besides the solver step (~30 ms stamped, sim frames only), the per-frame drawing side is about 15.6 ms GPU on a frame with no sim step: whitewater_step.liquid_cells 8.4 ms stamped (~6 real) - whitewater rebuilds its own liquid-cell mask; the solver already owns one, so reusing it may be one wire away; first check whether it runs per frame or per tick. particle_volume 7.9 stamped (~5.5) - particles splatted into the surface volume; particle scale 3.0 (item 1 look) widens each splat ~27x vs scale 1, candidates: splat only into surface bricks, or a coarser volume. render_scene 5.0 stamped (~3.5), of which transparent depth prepass 1.9 and transparent layer 1.1. Surface mesh chain ~2.5 stamped. Each needs a section 2.5 audit and an identical-output proof before any change. Source: scratchpad t7/n-c3.1.txt (node breakdown).

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Corrected 2026-10-06 on current main (node-stamped, ratios; cost_node.log): the earlier whitewater 8.4 ms was the whole whitewater group on an older binary; today whitewater_step is 1.6 ms. Real targets: particle_volume 7.5 every frame; render_scene 4.7 (transmissive depth prepass 1.9, transmissive layer 1.1); surface mesh chain ~2.7; liquid_frame p50 1.6 but p95 10.1 (spikes). Solver side on tick frames: gpu_flip.stage.pockets 12.5 ms next to pressure 13.7 and prepare 4.7. No-tick frames 14.5 ms GPU real, tick frames 35.4 ms.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Fable audit 2026-10-06 (scratchpad fable_cost_audit.md), real costs on a no-tick frame: particle_volume ~7, render_scene ~4, mesh chain ~3 of 14.4 ms. Ranked identical-output cuts: (1) particle_volume cooperative per-brick gather through threadgroup memory, est 2-4x; (2) per-blob support box precomputed in shape_particle_blobs; (3) back-face cull the transmissive depth prepass (~1 ms, needs closed-mesh/camera-outside rule); (4) alias six copy-only mesh passes (~0.2 ms); (5) unified grid: whitewater liquid_cells+particle_distance rebuild the solver's water/phi (1.6 ms/tick), solid lattice built 3x per tick. Under Astra review before any build.

title: Sharing one CARGO_TARGET_DIR across worktrees reuses stale workspace-crate builds
description: Symptom (2026-10-06): building slot-8 with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=slot-1/target after building slot-2 linked manifold-renderer against a manifold-gpu built from slot-2 (missing GatedRecorder), so the build failed; with additive differences it would have silently tested the wrong code. Root cause: Cargo dep-info paths are package-relative and freshness is by file mtime, so a worktree whose files are older than the shared artifact is judged fresh even when its content differs. The overnight lead used a shared target to land cold slots under the disk reserve (land_branch with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=slot-1/target), so those gates could have run mixed trees. Fix shape: land_branch and gate_runner refuse a CARGO_TARGET_DIR outside the worktree being landed (or touch every workspace source before building when one is shared), and the slot ring frees disk by cleaning landed slots instead of sharing targets.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Evidence: the display history timing binary built through the shared release target reported 31.0 vs 33.4 ms; a clean rebuild of the same trees shows no difference (34.3 vs 34.4). Overnight 'no change' and 'faster' numbers built that way are suspect; the clean end-to-end (start 41.8-44.1 vs main 33.0-34.5, same run) holds.

title: GPU FLIP pressure smooth: latent binding-contract mismatch on binding 4
description: Symptom: gpu_flip.pressure.smooth (gpu_flip_pressure.wgsl:421, stencil(idx, select(0u, 2u, from_zero()))) references binding 4 in its entry point, and the dispatches with source 0/2 leave it unbound. Unreachable on those sources today, but conservative reflection reports it, so GpuComputePipeline::unbound_binding cannot be asserted on every pressure dispatch (only on the plain zero, gpu_flip_pressure.rs debug_assert_bound). Root cause: one entry point serves sources with different binding needs. Fix shape: bind a valid buffer at 4 on every smooth dispatch, or split the entry point by source; then assert unbound_binding on every Sink dispatch.
close_reason: Fixed in C5b on lane/pressure-cap-template: smooth binds buffer(4, v.rhs); prepare_template refuses any unbound referenced binding

title: GPU FLIP sheeting: cut the rate-1 cost (~12.9 ms at Dam Break 64) and expose Sheet Fill Rate on the water presets
description: Sheeting landed off by default (step param sheet_fill_rate, 0 on every preset). Measured at rate 1, Dam Break 64: candidates 7.65 ms, resolve 2.00, write 1.91, surface distance 0.77, detect 0.25, scan ~0.2 (total ~12.9). Almost all of it is evaluate(): each site scans 27 buckets and rebuilds each bucket list by merging eight per-cell lists; resolve and write re-evaluate every claimant. Design (Astra: Amend, sound outline): (1) build each bucket list once per substep in fixed 32-slot rows in exact merge order (4 markers per cell is a hard cap; replace selected_count with per-cell counts or sentinels; never merge in place over unread segments; keep .w as index bits), measure; (2) store per-claimant records in candidates so resolve/write stop re-evaluating: append every state-2 claimant, store only when i < capacity, overflow runs the old full recompute path after a barrier, indirect args are threadgroup counts, clear all padded ranks incl. winners, publish counts/stats with zero records, keep capacity clipping and the identity-reset guard; keep one proof path that still recomputes so the failure counter is not vacuous; (3) share the 27-bucket neighbourhood in threadgroup memory, one 64-thread workgroup per bucket, workgroup-uniform early return. Target ~3 ms, unproven until measured. Proofs: port parity unchanged, bucket rows vs CPU merge, capacity boundary, zero claimants, overflow then normal, active-inactive-active, odd dimensions, saturated rows, shuffled input, records/fallback bitwise vs the old GPU path under replay and fractional rates, off digest 0xd7472f0be4edbe51. Then expose Sheet Fill Rate (0..1) on the water presets and characterize the look against FLIP Fluids at rate 1.
notes:
Stage 1 (bucket rows built once per substep) is on main: rate-1 sheeting cost at Dam Break 64 fell from 13.4 ms to 2.9 ms, bitwise identical, same births. That meets the ~3 ms target, so stages 2 and 3 (claimant records, threadgroup bucket sharing) are dropped. Still owed: the Sheet Fill Rate slider on the water card (domain dial + wire + binding, pressure-cap pattern; it lands on the Water card because the water row owns the domain), a look comparison against FLIP Fluids at rate 1 for Peter, and two proof additions from the Fable review: an odd-grid end-to-end bitwise run (e.g. [39,41,37]) and cell_counts (scratch()[3]) in the old-vs-new comparison.
Sheet Fill Rate slider is on main (water card, 0..1, default 0). Cost at Dam Break 64: frame GPU median 14.3 ms off, 17.4 ms at rate 1. Look: Peter accepted numerical parity (GPU matches the CPU port exactly; port checked against FLIP Fluids particlesheeter.cpp) in place of a visual comparison; look tuning deferred by Peter.
close_reason: Rate-1 cost 13.4 -> 2.9 ms, bitwise identical; slider landed; look tuning deferred by Peter.

title: manifold-gpu shader compiler test fails: mesher WGSL lacks clamp_liquid_solid_at
description: Symptom: manifold-gpu test metal::shader_compiler::tests::constant_array_copies_read_from_constant_address_space panics on main 9f1fe3232 at shader_common.rs:30 with "mesher: WGSL parse error: no definition in scope for identifier: clamp_liquid_solid_at". Root cause (likely): the test assembles the mesher source without the clamp_liquid_to_solids helper that volume_surface_mesh_body.wgsl now calls (helper lives in clamp_liquid_to_solids_element.wgsl); the call arrived with the sparse-brick mesher work on 2026-10-03 (70ea38446, fe04ae1a3). The shipping mesher composes the helper in manifold-renderer, so this is likely the test fixture only; verify. Fix shape: the test builds the mesher source through the same composition function the renderer uses, not a hand-listed include set. Also: nightly trunk_health should have filed this; check why it did not.
close_reason: Claude lead

title: fluid take cache-reader test overflows the 2 MB test-thread stack on main
description: Symptom: manifold-renderer test node_graph::fluid::take::tests::fluid_take_cache_reader_keeps_its_committed_range_as_recording_advances aborts with "has overflowed its stack" (SIGABRT, 0.2 s) on main 9f1fe3232 under nextest; passes with RUST_MIN_STACK=64 MB, so it is a large stack frame, not runaway recursion. Root cause unknown. Suspects: a large struct (scene, take cache or fixed-size array) built by value on the stack in the take/cache path or its test fixture; test added in 39864c338 (Bind physics caches to committed input takes). Fix shape: find the oversized frame (cargo +nightly -Z emit-stack-sizes or check the fixture), box it; never raise the test stack size as the fix. If the same frame exists in the shipping path it can crash the content thread.

title: Landing gate misses tests that read a preset from another module
description: Symptom: the item-1 Dam Break engine-defaults landing changed gpu_flip_preset.rs and the preset JSON, and the landing gate passed, but surface_mesh_normals.rs test surface_stage_defaults_and_manifest_bindings (which builds the Dam Break render_def) went red on main (expected 0.35, preset now 0.5). Root cause: the gate maps changed files to their own module filtersets and siblings; a test in another module that builds a preset is not mapped. Fix shape: map preset sources (gpu_flip_preset.rs, assets/generator-presets/*.json) to every test that constructs them (rg for render_def/WaterScene callers), or run a preset-consumer filterset whenever a preset source changes.

title: Coupled bodies creep under a steady sideways water reaction below their friction limit
description: Symptom: a body resting on the GPU FLIP tank floor walks a little every tick under a steady sideways push below mu. Seen by the body-friction lane (lane/body-friction-contact 3436c1677): a push decoded as one lumped impulse per tick measured an apparent threshold of 0.23-0.25 for every friction, before and after the wall-friction fix. Root cause (suspected): the water reaction is applied once per tick before Box3D contact stepping (coupling.rs:484-490, physics.rs:1394-1396), so the first substep sees the whole tick impulse as a velocity kick that friction only partly cancels; tick-lumped coupling, not a simultaneous solve. Fix shape: spread the reaction across Box3D substeps as a force, or apply it inside the contact solve. Related: BUG-3ypk (GPU FLIP body friction is linear drag, not Coulomb).

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Fix shape landed in 4e26ff403 (2026-10-06): D17 applies the water reaction as a steady force over the tick, not an impulse before the step. Not measured: no creep test exists; rerun the body-friction lane threshold probe before closing.

title: Whitewater lifecycle parity needs equal motion inputs
description: L5 engine parity (whitewater_step_against_engine_emitters_150, crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/whitewater_scene_tests.rs) gates emission only. Population per type also runs one lifecycle step, on unequal motion inputs: the GPU step advects through its substep history (substep_schedule, substep_u/v/w, advect_whitewater_body.wgsl), the engine oracle (whitewater_oracle::emit_engine) once at the tick dt on the end-of-tick faces. Observed on the Dam Break at 64, 8 engine seeds: bubble population frames 31-60 GPU 15594 vs engine 14937 ± 592 (+4.4%), with emitted counts matching in that window, so the gap is typing or motion, not emission. Fix shape: feed the engine oracle the GPU substep velocities per substep, or step the engine once per substep on the same history, then gate population per type per window.

title: GPU FLIP water tangential grip is one-way; a two-way exchange must account for the FLIP transfer
description: The constrain pass blends cut faces toward the body velocity (f*v_s + (1-f)*u, gpu_flip_step.wgsl:1824-1861) and tells the body nothing, so a light body moves water for free. Native FLIP Fluids has the same one-way blend (fluidsimulation.cpp:6872-6936), so this is beyond engine parity. Fable proposed an implicit 6x6 per-body exchange (scratchpad fable_friction_design.md D2); Astra review (astra_friction_result.md) blocks it: both new and saved faces are constrained to the same solid velocity (gpu_flip_step.rs:1780), so the correction cancels in the FLIP difference (gpu_flip_step.wgsl:2258) and the composed step can create energy (unit masses, f=1: 0.5 -> 0.625 at FLIP=1). Also: the exchange is not purely tangential, must use the physical wet mask not l.solve_water (pinned pockets), needs clock gating, light-body cancellation handling, and real transfer-level regressions. Fix shape: decide new/saved-field treatment and particle-transfer accounting first, then the exchange. Split from BUG-3ypk (GPU FLIP body friction is linear drag, not Coulomb).

title: Whitewater engine oracle: obstacle-source and domain-object influence parity
description: The engine-as-configured whitewater oracle (manifold_fluids_oracle_emit_engine, crates/manifold-fluids/native/bridge.cpp; whitewater_oracle::emit_engine) covers constant default influence only: its solid carries no mesh objects, while FluidSimulation installs a domain mesh object even without obstacles (fluidsimulation.cpp:5621) and sets its influence to the current base before each InfluenceGrid update (:7012-7020), and obstacles raise influence through their own mesh objects. So L5 parity (whitewater_step_against_engine_emitters_150) says nothing about the GPU step obstacle_source path or a base changed mid-run. Fix shape: give the oracle solid mesh objects (domain object at the base level, obstacle objects at their influence) or an influence-source lattice input matching whitewater_obstacle_source, then run L5 on a Dam Break with obstacle.

title: Coupled GPU FLIP: the content thread spins on the previous tick's reaction at frame start
description: Measured 2026-10-05 (release CPU sample, waterFunv3 res 64 live): 46% of the content thread is GpuFlipDomain -> LiquidRigidOwner::settle_ready -> FrameClock::wait, a busy-yield loop (cthread_yield) waiting for the previous frame's last tick so Box3D can take its reaction. CPU encoding and GPU work never overlap across ticks for a coupled liquid, so frame time is roughly encode + GPU per tick in series, and the spin burns a core. Questions: (1) can the wait block instead of spin (no behavior change), (2) can the rigid step run one tick behind live, or settle later in the frame so the frame's render work encodes during the wait - that one changes coupling latency and is Peter's call. Read LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md first; the seam owns this.

title: Encode replay allocates new indirect command buffers every frame when a region's frame shape alternates
description: Symptom: on waterFunv3 (GPU FLIP res 64, live paced, 24 fps project, 60 Hz sim) about 12% of the content thread's samples sit in manifold_gpu::metal::replay::ReplayStore::place_for -> new_icb (-[AGXG16XFamilyIndirectCommandBuffer initWithDevice:...]) under PressureSolver::solve -> Gate::dispatch -> dispatch_compute_gated, every frame (release sample with symbols, 2026-10-05). Root cause (read, not yet proven by stats): place_for allocates a fresh ICB whenever a gated segment is recorded at slot 0, and frames alternate between one-tick and two-tick shapes, so the 3-entry replay ring keeps re-recording the tail and reallocating. Fix shape: re-recording a gated segment reuses an ICB of the same command count (free list per span), or entries are chosen by frame shape so a matching recording replays. Oracle: the replay stats (store_allocations, recorded) printed per frame in frame-time, plus a CPU sample showing new_icb gone.
notes: 2026-10-05: after the coupled second-tick fix (BUG on waterFunv3 stutter), ICB churn left the live CPU profile's top entries; a red test was not written (the obstacle scene's body history can't run at 40 fps in the scene harness). Lower priority; re-measure on the GPU FLIP preset oracle before working it.

title: Paused water: freeze at once, or finish accepted sim time first?
description: BUG-3vcnz (paused Water Basin publishes twice): the first bad commit is 979b6e895 (Land wave/water-sim-rate-blend), which removed the held-transport early return in crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/fluid.rs (~1449, now 'Finish every interval already accepted before a pause'). The CPU water worker now drains all accepted time after a pause, so the water can step a few more times after the transport stops, then holds. Contracts disagree: WATER_SIMULATION_DESIGN.md 'Transport pause: render current water; no simulation or queued beat backlog' and the fluid_pause proof (at most one publish after pause) versus LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md D4 'Speed 0 ... can complete the preceding interval'. Options: (a) freeze on pause: restore the guard, at most the batch in flight publishes; (b) finish accepted work but publish once, after the drain; (c) keep draining and relax the proof to the live clock cap. Lead recommendation: (a) or (b); the stage reads a pause as stop now.
notes: Peter's call, 2026-10-05: water freezes on pause (no simulation while paused).
close_reason: Freeze at once: paused water does not finish accepted sim time. Fix lands under BUG-3vcnz (paused Water Basin publishes twice).

title: GPU FLIP scoped landing proofs exceed the 360-second budget
description: Required gate at codex/gpu-flip-reference 977968507 measured 395 budgeted seconds. Retained transcript: slot-2/target/landing-logs/gpu-proofs-20261004T233307.034337Z-1791156787034364000.log. 208/210 lib tests and all7 integration passed; two stale narrow-band support oracles were repaired and their focused rerun passed. Slowest passed proof: gpu_flip_body_step_sparse_matches_all_tiles69.6s, four fixture/level cases with dense/sparse/poison variants across90 ticks. Existing timing catalog omits it. Preserve meaningful coverage and fixed360s budget; use established measured-slow nightly classification or evidence-based reduction, not broader reruns or tolerance changes.
acceptance_criteria: Required gate completes within360s with honest measured timing provenance; long coverage remains in nightly tests.
close_reason: Verified landing gate at6c0b0fa80 passed all17 checks; GPU leg327s within360s. Existing measured-slow nightly classification keeps the complete69.6s body proof while preserving the fixed scoped budget. Landed and pushed by land_branch.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Recorded only the measured 69.6-second sparse-body proof in the existing timing catalog, with explicit scoped-run provenance (commit63a6b7e1c). Independent review approved preserving its full90-tick coverage in nightly runs under the established60-second rule. Catalog syntax/selection checks pass. Full scoped gate budget still needs confirmation after the wall patch; do not close until actual gate result.

title: Attribute small marker reductions in128 GPU FLIP project acceptance
description:
Required GPU FLIP stability acceptance observation at candidate489444365, not yet diagnosed as a defect. Original saved projects at128,140 fixed60Hz frames, unchanged settings/quality. waterFun:138 retired samples,6,832,128 initial markers to6,832,019 (109 lost,0.001595percent), first reduction tick116. compare:139 retired samples,2,883,584 to2,883,560 (24 lost), all loss at tick48. Both no nonfinite particles, no clock cap/remainder, no unconverged pressure/density or pockets, zero RK-stage speed caps (native extreme-speed removal is NOT counted), no push refusal or narrow shortage. Existing strict inside-solid/open-boundary/outflow/crowding removal can explain legitimate loss; cause is NOT yet established. Do not call this an explosion, a proven defect, or perfect particle preservation. Pressure-classifier optimisation final renders are pixel-identical to prior d3 candidate, so it did not change the result. Need bounded attribution of removal cause at the affected ticks and comparison to engine contract; repair only if a real defect, never disable native safety to hide it. Evidence trace-pressure-parallel-classify-{water,compare}-128.json/log and pixel JSON files in this cache. This is within existing real-time GPU FLIP campaign, no unrelated work or offline feature scope.

Static inventory: both originals have six closed faces and no outflow; compare has no fluid role, water has a Collider authored at x=-100.
