title: frame-time per-dispatch tables are partial: stamped frames overflow MAX_SPANS by ~1M spans
description: Symptom: frame-time --stamp-every 1 --stamp-granularity dispatch on waterFunv3 res 64 reports sampler overflow of about 1.08M spans on every stamped frame (MAX_SPANS is 32768), so the gpu_flip_step per-dispatch table only covers the spans that fit. Rankings from it (the BUG-g75v.5 cost map) may under-count passes that land after the buffer fills. Root cause unknown; suspects: MAX_SPANS sized for node granularity, spans never recycled per frame, or the counter is cumulative. Fix shape: size the span buffer to the frame dispatch count (grow on overflow, or one buffer per stamped frame) and fail the run loudly when a table is partial.
close_reason: Landed with lane/frame-time-spans: one sampler per run at the process limit; overflow 0 at res 64. Opus lead

title: GPU FLIP: the cell sort stabilise pass is the second-largest step cost (9.4 ms ratio at res 64)

At res 64 calm it is 9.4 ms of ~120 ms in the per-dispatch ratio split (main e6888c4b6, waterFunv3). Fix shape to evaluate: per-particle rank = count of same-bin members with lower input index (parallel over particles, O(k) per particle), or a stable scatter that never needs stabilising; output must be byte-identical (stable order by (bin, input index)); combine with BUG-9ohv2 (redundant re-sort).
close_reason: Landed with lane/sort-stabilise: per-slot stable rank, stabilise 9.4 -> 1.1 ms at res 64, calm frame 64.1 -> 61.1 ms. Opus lead

title: GPU water: the pressed-lid first solves hit the 64-iteration cap unconverged; the test convergence clause never runs
description: Symptom: in the posed pressed-lid tank the first tick pressure solve stops at the 64-iteration cap unconverged (sealed frames 1, 3 density, 4 both; open frame 1). The test check "every solve converges until the lid first kills water" is vacuous because the lid kills water on frame 1 in both the old and the posed setup. Related: BUG-n3od (density solve reaches its cap under a pressed lid, closed) and BUG-6rki6 (pressure cap 64 decision). Suspects: a sealed pocket under a moving solid gets an incompatible right-hand side (the engine gives sealed water no push from the solid, pressuresolver.cpp:214); the pocket-mean passes may not cover the lid case. Fix shape: make the convergence clause run on frames before contact or assert per-solve convergence directly, then port the engine sealed-pocket rule if the residual is the incompatible part.

title: GPU water: a lid pressed into sealed water pushes it out and churns instead of removing what it sweeps
description: Symptom: in the posed pressed-lid tank (gpu_flip_box_pressed_into_a_full_tank_converges_and_escapes_when_open, sealed half), the GPU removes 506 of the 16,384 particles the lid sweeps on frame 1 and 58,194 of ~262,000 swept by frame 30; the sealed water churns at up to 4.3 m/s, the fullest cell holds 167 particles and 1,519 cells hold 64+. FLIP Fluids on the same scene keeps the water at 0.0 m/s, 8-11 a cell, and deletes what the lid sweeps (386,976 -> 163,708 live over 30 frames): sealed water takes no push from the solid (pressuresolver.cpp:214), an unmoved marker is not pushed out (fluidsimulation.cpp:8331-8332), a marker left inside the solid is removed (fluidsimulation.cpp:8483). On stage: a collider pressed into fully enclosed water jitters under it instead of sitting still. Suspects: resolve_solid treats a particle as unmoved below 1e-6 cells (6.25e-8 m at res 64) where the engine uses 1e-6 m; the f32 solve leaves sealed water slightly moving; density projection moves particles by position only. Fix shape: (a) unmoved threshold in metres (parity) with this scene as the oracle (frame 1 should remove ~16,384); if leftover motion is the real cause, (b) remove a swept particle whose pocket is sealed. Found by the tank lane (d71c98442).

title: GPU FLIP: prove the gated body passes under encode replay
description: The BUG-e6z6s (inactive FLIP slots) fix moved the level-0 body impulse, finalize and product into the pressure solve gated segment. Since the step gained the engine's turbulence, bubble and dust emitters (BUG-imy3.1) and engine physics (BUG-g75v.7), its 150-frame sums are 1.78x foam, 2.54x bubbles and 5.91x spray of that reference ([443982, 131743, 269386] vs [248895, 51919, 45556]) - expected, since the reference lacks those emitters. title: GPU FLIP frames with Native Mesh Grid refuse any whitewater that reads its lattice from the frame
description: Symptom: a GPU FLIP frame with Native Mesh Grid on (a6df7e91f, BUG-g75v.10 engine surface grid) publishes the 1.5-cell-padded mesh lattice (67 cells at res 64). A whitewater group that takes its lattice from the frame (the catalog Whitewater group, the vendored scene) then refuses every frame: 'a [64,64,64]-cell face grid does not sit centred on the [67,67,67]-cell whitewater grid'. The shipped Dam Break is unaffected (its whitewater reads the simulation grid). Root cause: the frame's published lattice changes meaning with the flag, while whitewater needs the simulation lattice (GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md: whitewater retains its separately sampled simulation-grid solid). Fix shape: the frame publishes both lattices on distinct ports (mesh grid and simulation grid) so consumers wire the one they mean, or whitewater derives its grid from the domain, never the frame. Found by the wave whitewater lane (5ec8b8eda), which pinned the vendored test scene to the simulation lattice.

title: Live GPU FLIP display may hold frame B below 60 fps: fenced publication trails the accepted pair by one frame
description: Symptom (modelled, not yet observed in the app): since particle blending pass 2 (c6c150bfa), a live GPU FLIP frame publishes a tick only after that tick's fence retires, on a later frame; export publishes on the same frame. So the published A/B pair trails the accepted pair by one display frame. D7 (docs/LIVE_SIM_CLOCK_DESIGN.md) keeps the display inside the accepted pair, but the blend reads the published pair, so below 60 fps the shown time can step unevenly or hold at B: model /tmp/slot9_published_pair.py gives 60 fps smooth at every Sim Rate; 30 fps at 20 Hz steps 17/50/33 ms and at 60 Hz sits past B every frame; 24 fps uneven at every rate (30 Hz: 67/33/33/33 ms). Matter, CPU FLIP and export are unaffected (same-frame publication). Oracle: a live GPU FLIP run at 24 fps logging display_time against B's simulation time. Fix options: keep the count and accept flag on the GPU so B advances on the frame it is encoded (no CPU wait), or add one display frame of latency for fenced publishers. Found by the wave clock-reds lane (2042c96c5).

title: Water scenes compile 8 pipelines during playback: warmup misses them, startup frames take seconds

Under the live clock those slow frames become huge spans, which trigger the first and largest water loss (BUG-969p6 (stretched last substep blows up the water)). Root cause unknown; suspects: pipelines created lazily on the first tick or first grown buffer (volume_surface_mesh growth, liquid_frame id-sorted publication, whitewater passes) that the preset warmup/prewarm path never visits. Fix shape: make warmup encode a representative tick (all stage pipelines, grown-capacity paths) before transport starts, or prewarm from the plan's pipeline list; prove with a frame-time run that logs zero cold-touch lines.

title: GPU FLIP: substep slots the clock plan never activates still cost ~16 ms each
description: Every clock slot up to the 6-substep cap encodes its passes whether or not the plan activates it. Grid-sized passes and the pressure solver's fixed iteration count launch every thread, which exits on the plan check; the sorter has no guard at all. Measured on waterFunv3 res 64 at 30 Hz (wave 70d942fae, per-slot probe, node granularity): an inactive slot costs 15.6-16.4 ms against 23.5-27.5 ms active; 2.2 inactive slots per tick on the calm mix = ~35 ms of each ~130 ms tick frame. Per inactive slot: pressure solve ~7.4 ms (smooth 3.45, restrict 0.91, classify 0.61, direction 0.54, coarse_inverse 0.50, prolong 0.47, residual 0.41), sorts ~1.7 (stabilise 1.30, count+tail 0.43), body coupling reductions 1.9, pockets 1.36, solid_extrapolate 0.41, particle mask 0.21. Fix: the clock plan writes indirect dispatch arguments for every pass in a slot, so an inactive slot launches zero threadgroups; no physics change, parity kept. Same mechanism as BUG-fwp2n (unused solver rounds cost encode time). Evidence: session scratchpad probe/probe2_slots.log, slot_split.py, probe2_slots.diff.

title: GPU FLIP publication sort costs 89 ms a frame at res 128: 33 one-bit radix passes over every slot
description: Measured 2026-10-04 on waterFunv3 (1080p, M4 Max), wave/water-sim-rate-blend at bda2e7175: node.liquid_frame p50 8.7 ms at res 64 and 89 ms at res 128 (of 575 ms). Fix shape: multi-bit digits (4 passes of 8 bits, workgroup histograms over the existing PrefixScan) over live slots only; or publish by an id-indexed scatter with no sort if the birth-id range stays bounded between rollovers; skip the sort when nothing reads the blend pair.

notes:
# MANIFOLD physics-value inventory

Read-only inventory from the Rust worktree at `/Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/.claude/worktrees/slot-1`.  Line anchors are source-of-truth definitions or defaulted storage.  A value marked **user-facing** is an exposed node parameter, a serialized setting, or a documented scene control; **internal** means solver/bridge state or a fixed numerical constant.

## 1. Shared clock and duplicated controls

| Value | Owner / anchor | Default and units | User-facing status / difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ProjectSettings.physics.sim_rate` | `crates/manifold-foundation/src/settings.rs:235-267`; re-exported and serde-wired by `manifold-core/src/settings.rs:9-20`, with legacy project construction at `:528-529` | `PhysicsSettings::legacy()` is 60 Hz for old files; derived `SimRate::default()` is 30 Hz. Allowed 15/20/30/60 Hz; interval is `1/hz` seconds. | **User-facing serialized project setting**. `ProjectSettings` uses the legacy 60-Hz serde default. Current runtime passes this interval through `PhysicsStepScope::for_settings` into `SimulationClock`; local 60-Hz fallback and solver-native constants are listed separately below. |
| fixed/reference `TICK` constants | `manifold-physics/src/clock.rs:10`; CPU FLIP `manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/fluid.rs:50`; renderer rigid `physics.rs:199` | `1/60 s`; internal reference/fallback. | **Several local constants remain**. They are used for cache/history indexing, extent defaults, tests, emission scaling, and no-accepted-interval fallbacks. Live/export accepted intervals are supplied by the shared clock; these constants do not make the whole runtime fixed at 60 Hz. |
| solver `speed` | FLIP `fluid_surface.rs:179-180`; Matter `matter_domain.rs:315-316`; GPU FLIP `gpu_flip_domain.rs:371-372`; Box3D `physics_world.rs:350-354` | `1.0`, range `0..=4`; dimensionless simulation-time multiplier. `0` holds/discards queued impulses. | **Four separately exposed node controls**. Fluid composition notes state coupled Physics World owns speed; Matter/GPU FLIP own their domain speed. `SimulationClock` retains piecewise speed history and accepted intervals (`manifold-physics/src/clock.rs:62-124, 190-340`). |
| clock reset | same four node manifests above | trigger default `0`; restart/backward seek reseeds. | **Four separate exposed reset controls**, with coupled pairs sharing a restart in the scene contracts. |
| history sampler | `fluid_surface.rs:197`; `fluid.rs` composition notes | 240 Hz stateless physics ancestry sampler; internal. | CPU FLIP user-facing docs mention this as the historical control sample rate, separate from local 60-Hz cache/history references; accepted live/export intervals may differ. |

Current clock semantics are deliberately asymmetric at a late live observation. `SimulationClock::advance` (`manifold-physics/src/clock.rs:199-355`) gates live work on nominal Sim Rate boundaries, then accepts the full owed transport span as one `ClockFrame` interval when the observation arrives late; `sim_rate_late_live_update_keeps_full_span_and_six_step_cap` (`clock.rs:669-684`) verifies a `1.07 s` span and the six-step native schedule cap. Export accepts complete nominal intervals. At full-rate 60-fps stage observations the live and export schedules coincide, but neither mode is thereby a permanently fixed `1/60 s` interval schedule, and a delayed live frame is not split into one nominal interval per display frame.

## 2. CPU FLIP / native `manifold-fluids`

### Stored settings and defaults

`FluidSettings` is serialized runtime setup at `crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/fluid.rs:85-105`, with defaults at `107-128`:

| Value | Default / units | User-facing status |
|---|---|---|
| seed | `0` | Exposed `Seed`, `0..16,777,215`, `fluid_surface.rs:160`. |
| resolution | `24` (node range `8..512`) | Exposed; native cells are derived from domain dimensions. |
| domain size | `4.0` m (node range `0.5..20`) | Exposed; optional axis-aligned `domain` transform sets full XYZ metres. |
| boundary collisions | all six `true`; order `-X,+X,-Y,+Y,-Z,+Z` | Six exposed closed-face booleans. |
| fill height | `0.4` m | Exposed, must lie strictly inside domain height. |
| initial volume | absent | Optional axis-aligned translating box; zero initial velocity; fully contained. |
| surface subdivisions | `0` (node range `0..2`) | Exposed display/meshing value, not solver dynamics. |
| `liquid` | `LiquidOptions::default()` = viscosity `0`, surface tension `0` | Exposed as Viscosity and Surface Tension, node range `0..10`; native coefficients are explicitly scale-dependent, not calibrated material units (`manifold-fluids/src/lib.rs:91-114`). |

### Native stepping, force and coupling values

* `FluidWorld::step` rejects non-positive/non-finite `dt` and ordinary calls cap `dt` at `1/30 s`; live calls allow positive `dt` and expose owner-driven native substeps (`manifold-fluids/src/lib.rs:741-895`, `manifold-fluids/src/frame.rs:20-120`). Live substeps follow native stability offers, but the final substep consumes the remaining interval when the cap is reached, so that last step can be larger than the nominal offer in order to preserve transport time.
* Native FLIP applies gravity as a body-force vector (`bridge.cpp:1266-1275`). Scene vector fields are converted to per-cell acceleration plus one-shot `delta_velocity/dt` before FFI (`manifold-fluids/src/lib.rs:671-862`): acceleration is a continuous force; delta velocity is an impulse-like one-shot velocity change.
* Rigid-fluid coupling passes physical liquid density from the scene (`fluid_surface.rs:197` composition notes); coupling reactions are pressure/viscosity impulses, consumed once per substep. Pressure impulses are mass-scaled and converted once to delta velocity by `manifold-physics/src/stepping.rs:814-818`.
* Native whitewater options are passed in `bridge.cpp:1374-1410`; emission and all three material types are enabled/disabled there. Native diffuse defaults that remain otherwise untouched are listed in section 5 below.

Joint runtime impulses are solver state, not authored defaults: each implementation zeroes warm-start impulse fields on creation or when warm starting is disabled. The current Rust path only creates/steps ordinary Box3D bodies, so these definitions are inventory coverage for a future joint bridge rather than live MANIFOLD controls.

## 8. Rigid Box3D / Physics World

### Scene-facing values

`RigidBody` is stored at `manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/physics.rs:268-321`:

| Value | Default / units | User-facing status |
|---|---|---|
| kind | dynamic | body input field; fixed/animated/dynamic. |
| density | `600 kg/m³` (`DEFAULT_DENSITY`, `physics.rs:321-322`) | Body field; mass is density × installed hull volume. |
| friction | `.5` | Body field, forwarded to Box3D shape material. |
| bounce/restitution | `.15` | Body field, forwarded to Box3D restitution. |
| transform/enabled/release/shape | transform default; enabled true; release `0`; shape `1` | Body fields; topology/scale edits rebuild. |
| world gravity | `(0,-9.81,0)` | Physics World node manifest `physics_world.rs:349-354`, range `-20..20`. |
| world speed/reset | speed `1`, reset `0`, speed `0..4` | Exposed controls coupled to the shared accepted clock interval. |
| copies | count `100`, spacing `1.25 m`, columns `16`, layout Grid | Numeric copy controls `physics_world.rs:355-358`; reset-latched bodies. |

The low-level Rust `BodyConfig::default()` is deliberately different from scene `RigidBody`: mass `1 kg`, friction `.5`, restitution `0` (`manifold-physics/src/lib.rs:245-268`). Scene code supplies density-derived mass and bounce. Per-body and global acceleration fields are optional; acceleration is converted to force `mass*a`, while `delta_velocity` is converted to impulse `mass*dv` (`manifold-physics/src/lib.rs:691-805`). `BodyImpulse` units are linear `kg·m/s` and angular `kg·m²/s` (`lib.rs:298-305`), and the batch is validated/applied once (`lib.rs:1054-1130`).

### Box3D native defaults and margins

The native bridge creates `b3DefaultWorldDef`, overrides gravity and forces single worker (`manifold-physics/native/box3d/bridge.c:176-183`). Defaults are in `box3d/src/types.c:10-79`:

* world gravity default `y=-10` before the bridge override; restitution threshold `1 m/s`, hit threshold `1 m/s`, contact speed `3 m/s`, contact Hertz `30`, contact damping ratio `10`, max linear speed `400 m/s`; sleeping and continuous collision enabled;
* body defaults: static type, sleep threshold `.05 m/s`, gravity scale `1`, sleeping enabled, awake/enabled true, contact recycling true;
* surface friction `.6`, shape density `1000 kg/m³`, restitution `0` (bridge then sets shape density `1` and scene friction/restitution); default friction mixing is `sqrt(a*b)`, restitution mixing is `max(a,b)` (`box3d/types.h:168-172`);
* `BodyConfig` scene mass is authoritative for dynamic rigid bodies; low-level body damping is not authored by the current Rust scene bridge and stays native default zero from zero-initialized `b3BodyDef`.

The current Physics World exposes no damping/contact-tuning node fields. Rust API methods exist for max linear speed and contact tuning (`manifold-physics/src/lib.rs:641-675`) but the renderer only calls max linear speed dynamically for fast authored motion (`physics.rs:1296-1304`). Contact defaults therefore remain 30 Hz / damping 10 / recovery speed 3 m/s unless external code calls the API. Box3D broad-phase margins are internal: max AABB margin `0.05 m`, per-shape fraction `.125`, contact recycling distance `10× linear slop`, mesh rest offset `1× linear slop` (`box3d/include/box3d/constants.h:75-95`).

`physics_world.rs:144` still describes the node as running fixed 60-Hz ticks; that purpose text is stale for the live clock. The accepted interval and the fixed no-interval fallback are distinguished above.

## 9. Cross-system comparison and coverage gaps

| Concept | CPU FLIP | GPU FLIP | Matter | Box3D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gravity | user-facing XYZ, default `(0,-9.81,0)` | same | same | same scene control; native unoverridden default is `-10` only before bridge override |
| density | CPU liquid density `1000 kg/m³`, passed to coupling; native liquid coefficients do not calibrate density | no exposed density dial in GPU FLIP manifest | `1000 kg/m³` atom default | scene body density `600 kg/m³`; native shape default `1000`, bridge sets shape density `1` then mass |
| damping / drag | native whitewater bubble/spray drag; liquid viscosity is separate | FLIP share `.95`; whitewater drag | liveliness and cohesion, no generic damping | body damping unavailable in scene; contact damping ratio native `10`; whitewater spray/bubble friction/drag separate |
| forces | acceleration field continuous; `delta_velocity` one-shot | force/impulse lattices, force every substep, impulse on designated first tick | force lattice every substep, impulse first substep; body reaction arrays | acceleration → force, `delta_velocity` → impulse |
| impulses | pressure/viscosity coupling reaction; mass-scaled delta-v | pressure body reaction and scene impulse lattice | 16-word reaction per body, decoded to impulse | SI center-of-mass linear/angular impulses |
| timestep | shared authored Sim Rate interval reaches the transport/clock; native/cache helper `TICK=1/60`, adaptive 1..6, CFL 5; live final remainder may stretch to preserve the interval | accepted `interval_duration/steps` at runtime; manifest fallback `TICK/steps`; `steps` 1..64, default 1; pressure auto/cap 900 | shared accepted interval, acoustic CFL 1/3, cap 128; stiffness raises substeps | accepted shared interval is passed to Box3D; `box3d_substep_count(duration)` gives 4 at nominal `1/60` and `ceil(4*duration/(1/60))` for longer intervals |
| margins | native surface/whitewater cell margins; mesh/world validation | narrow band/ghost fluid and whitewater boundary/solid margins | 3-node lattice padding, 0.9 velocity clamp | AABB/contact/restitution margins above |

Current edited-source rate ownership: `SimulationClock::advance` (`manifold-physics/src/clock.rs:199-355`) accepts the caller's shared authored interval, while `tick_starts` (`clock.rs:168-189`) gates live work on nominal boundaries and late live frames retain the full owed span. `PhysicsStepScope::for_settings` (`manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/physics.rs:163-176`) derives that interval from `PhysicsSettings.sim_rate`. `clock.rs:TICK=1/60` remains a native/fallback constant; CPU FLIP cache/history helpers retain `fluid.rs:TICK=1/60`; GPU FLIP's runtime step is `interval_duration/steps` even though its node prose still says 60 Hz; generic Euler/burst atoms still use `delta*60`; whitewater influence orchestration still injects fixed `TICK` while the other whitewater stages receive frame `dt`. Box3D receives the accepted shared interval and only uses `FIXED_TICK=1/60` for the no-accepted-interval fallback (`physics.rs:199,1198-1202`), while `box3d_substep_count` uses the actual duration. These are current source facts, not proposed migration behavior.

Remaining scope boundary: authored mesh deformers, image-flow generators, and non-physics rendering nodes are excluded. The generic particle force/state atoms and the complete native Box3D joint definition values are enumerated above; whitewater potential atoms remain in the whitewater section.

title: GPU FLIP: fluid cannot separate from a solid floor (pure upward force never lifts the pool)
description: Symptom: a flat seeded 0.64 m pool under gravity reversed to +20 m/s2 stays exactly still for 180 frames at 64 and 128 (identical particle, water-cell and air-cell counts every frame; probe gpu_flip_forced_pool_volume_probe on feat/forced-volume). The pressure solve holds the water on the floor with negative pressure; nothing breaks the symmetry. Reference: the FLIP Fluids engine does the same. _constrainVelocityFieldThread (crates/manifold-fluids/native/flip_engine/fluidsimulation.cpp:6860-6924) sets a face with weight 0 to the solid velocity and blends partial faces toward it, in both directions; there is no separating (outward-allowed, inward-zero) condition and no clamp on negative pressure. So ours matches the reference, and the fix is a departure from it. Fix shape: a separating solid boundary (Batty, Bertails and Bridson 2007 style inequality: solid-face normal velocity >= solid velocity, pressure >= 0 at those faces), solved as an LCP or with an active-set pass on the existing multigrid PCG; needs its own design pass and a still-pool / hydrostatic proof that resting water does not lift.
notes: Peter 2026-10-03: a fully sealed tank (no air anywhere) is an accepted edge case. Fix only if floor cells also go dry in open water with an air surface; otherwise the separating floor lands and the sealed case stays tracked here at lower priority.
close_reason: Landed 0316fb0b9 (batch 2): water separates from a rising floor

title: Implicit body-side friction for GPU FLIP coupled bodies
description: GPU FLIP bodies feel only the pressure reaction (engine parity, rigidfluidcoupling.cpp has no friction term). The removed explicit friction reaction rho*h^3*w*f*(u - v_s) per cut face has per-step gain k = rho*h*f*A_wet/m and diverges once k > ~2. k table: Floating Box 62.5 kg 0.30; Collision ratio 0.1 (0.8 kg) 1.56; Dam Break obstacle 1 kg h=4/64 0.5 m2 wetted 15.6; fully wetted 136. Shape for an implicit version: accumulate C = sum c_f b_f b_f^T (6x6, linear+angular) per body in impulse_finalize, solve (I + M^-1 C) dv = M^-1 P per body, fluid side uses the post-exchange body velocity. Unconditionally stable for any k.

title: landing_gate flow-gate re-queues the GPU lock once per flow and leaves no transcript on timeout: timed out at 3600s under lane contention
description:
Symptom: the feat/water-panel-controls gate's flow-gate leg failed with TIMEOUT after 3600s and kept no output. The log at slot-3 target/landing-logs/flow-gate-20261002T091634 is 111 bytes and holds only the TIMEOUT line.

Root cause (measured 2026-10-02 by the opus gate-speed lane):
1. The GPU lock was taken 46 times, once per flow. Each flow ran in its own process, and that process took the lock itself through GpuDevice::new_queued (RenderState::new in ui_snapshot/script.rs). A 46-flow gate queued for the lock 46 times, and any other lane's multi-minute GPU job could run between two flows. During the probe one holder kept the lock for 7m23s. Under lane load this turned a ~13 min leg into 60 min.
2. Output was never flushed. run_ui_flows.py printed into a pipe without flushing, so its PASS lines were still in Python's buffer when the leg was killed.
3. The app was orphaned on timeout. landing_gate.run_cmd used subprocess.run with a timeout, which kills only the direct python child. The cargo/manifold process under it kept running and kept holding the GPU lock after the gate had already reported TIMEOUT.

Fix (chore/gate-speed 694aab52f, BUG-w0hh (landing gate speed) lever c+a0):
- run_ui_flows.py builds the app binary once with no lock held. It then runs every flow from that binary under one gpu_queue hold; child processes inherit the hold through the ancestor check. Every line is flushed and shows the flow's seconds.
- landing_gate.run_cmd streams each leg into target/landing-logs while it runs. On timeout it stops and SIGKILLs the leg's whole descendant tree, found through ps. Legs stay in the gate's process group, so Ctrl-C still reaches them.
close_reason: landed on main ccddaad81 (chore/gate-speed: flow gate is one batch process, transcript on timeout)

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Root cause: a sealed pocket (water a solid closes off from air) is a pure-Neumann region, which has a solution only when its right-hand side sums to 0. A body pushing into it, or the swept, crowded layer under it, breaks that, so the pressure and density solves reach their cap. Ruling (b): remove each pocket's mean from the RHS in both solves. Implementation map (line-anchored, for takeover): /tmp/open-faces-verdict.txt, section IMPLEMENTATION MAP. In short: wgsl bindings 25 label / 26 atomic sums; seed labels = idx; the pocket sweeps propagate the minimum label between linked SEALED cells; check flags label mismatch as unresolved; new passes clear, accumulate (workgroup pre-reduced, 64-bit fixed point, exact), remove, and flux tally into stats words 14/15 (SOLVER_WORDS 6); run after divergence and after density_source; density_source drops its sealed zeroing. Fix 2 is a separate commit: density_source skips particles inside the solid at this step's pose.

title: Liquid surface level set is a homegrown hybrid, not Yu-Turk or Zhu-Bridson

title: GPU FLIP adaptive substeps on the GPU (indirect dispatch, Max Steps cap)
description: Speed phase. GPU FLIP Steps is a fixed per-tick slider (default 1). Adaptive n per tick must stay deterministic and identical in export and live, so it cannot come from a CPU readback: liquid_state runs every due tick of a frame in one command buffer, so tick t-1 has not run when tick t is encoded. Design: n per tick from that tick's own starting max speed (the engine's rule), n = clamp(ceil(v_max*dt/(CFL*h)), 1, Max Steps), computed by a tiny GPU kernel. Encode Max Steps substeps always; every dispatch goes through manifold-gpu dispatch_compute_indirect with group counts written 0 for k >= n. step_dt, flip_per_step, max_travel, the density rate and tick_seconds move from the Params uniform into a GPU buffer. The pressure solver (gpu_flip_pressure.rs) and body passes (gpu_flip_bodies.rs) encode indirect too: this is the same code the pressure-encode and dispatch-count speed work touches, so do them together. Gate: a run-twice proof that compares n sequences; reset/seek starts from the restored state; bodies see every substep; solids push test passes at n > 1.

description: Symptom: on origin/main 3ae635fda (seen from chore/flip-studio-floor, whose diff is the GPU FLIP preset only), gpu_proofs liquid_conformance fails liquid_live_frames_never_wait (frame 0), liquid_nonfinite_tick_not_published (frame 12) and liquid_overflow_is_reported, all on the node.matter_domain row with "frame N rendered with status Failed(NodeError)" at liquid_conformance.rs:401. title: GPU FLIP open-face boundaries
description: GPU FLIP's tank is closed on every face (CLOSED_FACES = 63; the step reads no closed_faces). Matter and FLIP take closed_* params per face. Without open faces a box pressing on an incompressible pool in a closed tank hands its momentum to the walls at once, so the Collision conformance check (body plus liquid momentum balance) cannot run on GPU FLIP and is exempt by name (GPU_FLIP_CLOSED_TANK in liquid/conformance.rs). On stage: no waterfall off an open edge, no pool that drains out a side. Fix shape: per-face closed params on the domain, the wall rule and pressure boundary reading them (open face = air, p = 0), particles leaving an open face removed; then drop the Collision exemption.
close_reason: Landed on main in bfd84ebf0: open-face boundaries, sealed-pocket solid velocity, capped density solve under a pressed lid

title: Liquid domain publishes zero lattice while pending on its first live frame
description: Symptom: on the first live frame of a matter or GPU FLIP liquid scene, the domain has no finished tick yet and publishes held zero lattice outputs. Downstream nodes (matter_fill, matter_frame, liquid_solid_distance) error with "lattice wire nodes_x is 0", and since BUG-hc5h (node ctx.error does not fail the frame) that fails the frame. On stage: one failed frame whenever a liquid clip starts live. liquid_live_frames_never_wait (gpu_proofs) is red on main on warm-up frame 0 for both rows. Root cause: the domain gates its geometry outputs (lattice dims, cell size) on a completed tick, but those come from params, not from the solve. Fix shape: the domain publishes its geometry outputs every frame, pending or not; only state outputs wait for the tick.
close_reason: Fixed on feat/gpu-flip-bodies 07b03a023: domains declare outputs pending until first good frame; lattice readers and liquid stage nodes treat pending inputs as pending. liquid_live_frames_never_wait green; GPU-PROOFS GATE: PASS.

title: Mesh relaxation off-cost: 0-strength copy costs 0.35-0.42 ms and +1280 MB on the Dam Break
description: Measured on feat/water-look, GPU FLIP Dam Break at 64, 300 frames, 1920x1080: the two relax_surface_mesh passes at strength 0 (the shipped default, a bit-exact copy) cost 0.420 ms GPU timestamped (0.352 ms scaled, 0.020 ms CPU), about 1.4% of a 25 ms frame and 60% of marching cubes; GPU memory 2525 MB against 1245 MB unwired, +1280 MB = 2 x 8,388,606 vertices x 80 B full-capacity output buffers. Root cause of the memory: the mesh max_capacity is 8.4M vertices against a peak live count of 618,888 (7.4%). Options: (a) accept; (b) one relax pass instead of two (halves both); (c) graph pruning of a strength-0 chain (a general mechanism, not a per-node bypass); (d) size the mesh capacity from the live count bound instead of the fixed max, which shrinks marching cubes and relaxation alike. Needs a call before landing. Parent: BUG-xwf1 (Liquid Surface mesh relaxation).
notes: 2026-10-02: hold mesh relaxation; root fix is sizing the surface mesh from the live count (shrinks memory everywhere, makes relaxation free when off). Then land relaxation on top.
close_reason: Closed

title: GPU FLIP render smoke: paused renders change 51420 pixels with particles still
description: Symptom: the GPU FLIP Dam Break render smoke (gpu_flip_render_smoke_tests.rs, --features water-race-probes, 64 cubed, 300 frames, 1920x1080) fails CRITICAL "paused renders moved particles 0 m and changed 51420 pixels": with the sim paused and particles not moving, consecutive renders still differ in 51420 pixels. Reproduces identically on feat/water-look with the mesh relaxation chain unwired, so it predates relaxation. Root cause unknown. Suspects: a frame-varying render input downstream of the surface (whitewater jitter or spawn seeded by frame, temporal noise in the volume/transmission path, or TAA-style accumulation), or the surface rebuilt with a time-dependent input while paused. Fix shape: bisect by disabling render stages (whitewater, volume scattering) on a paused frame pair to find the varying stage, then make it a pure function of sim state.
notes: Root cause: node.whitewater_step writes its output on frame N and publishes it on frame N+1 (CPU-read counts drive instance_count/live_count, so the shown pool must come from a retired frame). A held clock still called Outputs::collect, so the first paused render published the last played pool: foam changed once, then held (32 cubed/60 frames: 2289 px on paused render 0, 0 on renders 1-2; the publish log showed slot (0,0)->(1,0), counts [46,46,2]->[44,46,4]). Fix on chore/flip-pause-pixels 269fa75fb: collect only when ticks > 0 (I5). After: 0 px at 32/60 and 64/300 (dam_break and still_pool). Close when it lands.
close_reason: Landed on main in 3ae635fda (chore/flip-pause-pixels)

title: GPU FLIP step: write the body owner code and take body changes for two-way coupling
description: node.gpu_flip_step solid_face_velocity pass (shaders/gpu_flip_step.wgsl) writes no owner code into face_velocity.w and takes no per-body velocity changes. The deleted node.solid_face_velocity atom did both: w = sum over axes a of (b_a + 1)*256^a, and a dynamic body added its node.face_impulse_to_bodies sums (dv, dw) to its predicted velocity. The kept body-coupling atoms (node.pressure_face_impulse, node.friction_face_impulse, node.body_pressure_product, node.face_impulse_to_bodies) read that owner code, so they cannot be wired to the step until it returns. They were never wired in WaterDamBreakGpuFlip (changes was a zero lattice). Fix shape: when the coupling phase (GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 8, solids in the water) wires bodies into the solve, the step gains a body-sums input, its solid_face_velocity pass adds the changes and writes the owner code, and the step tests CPU reference (cpu_solid_face_velocity in gpu_flip_step_tests.rs) adds both back.
close_reason: Built on feat/gpu-flip-bodies (168494adc, 13c040e23): the step writes the owner code, takes the per-body reaction, and the domain owns the Box3D world; coupled conformance green

title: GPU FLIP coarsest multigrid level: smooth in one dispatch
description: Symptom: with the fixed 5-level V-cycle the coarsest level is 16 red-black sweep pairs each way = 64 node.pressure_smooth dispatches per V-cycle on a 4^3 (64) or 8^3 (128) lattice, 512 per main solve. Measured (gpu_flip_solve_stage_split): coarsest stage 1.79 ms of a 3.65 ms solve at 64^3 (was 0.19 ms with the exact inverse), 2.66 of 14.8 ms at 128^3; about 3.5 us per dispatch, pure overhead; about +3.8 ms per 64^3 tick (two main solves + 3-iteration density solve). Fix shape: the coarsest lattice is at most 8^3 = 512 cells across the supported 32-128, which fits one workgroup, so a barriered atom running all rounds in one dispatch (like node.coarse_inverse) removes the overhead; needs the DECOMPOSING_GENERATORS.md section 2.5 audit first (one-wire-away candidates: node.pressure_smooth with a rounds param inside one workgroup). Keep the sweep order palindromic so the preconditioner stays symmetric; pins in gpu_flip_solve_tests.rs stay valid.
close_reason: Superseded: the pressure solver module (gpu_flip_pressure.rs, feat/gpu-flip-coarse-solve 1de112344) solves the coarsest level exactly with the coarse inverse at runtime depth, so there is no coarsest smoothing left to put in one dispatch.

title: Water at res 32 logs solid-lattice errors from whitewater nodes while the frame still reports Complete
description: Symptom: exporting GPU FLIP Dam Break at Resolution 32 logs errors from node.extend_lattice, node.wavecrest_potential and node.whitewater_lifecycle: "a [1, 1, 1] solid lattice has too few or too many nodes". Frames still report Complete. Root cause unknown; suspects: the solid lattice is built at a fixed or degenerate size that does not follow Resolution, and node errors are not reaching frame status. Fix shape: the lattice follows Resolution through extents; a node error marks the frame failed, with no silent completion. Repro: gpu_flip_export_is_deterministic on feat/liquid-pause-export (8be227bd7).
notes: Root cause: a sizing bug, not a small-grid limit. gpu_flip_domain refuses any Resolution other than built_resolution (64 in WaterDamBreakGpuFlip.json), so 96 or 128 fail the same way. The refusal publishes zeroed lattice wires, LiquidLattice::from_scalars clamps 0 to 1 (lattice.rs:48), and whitewater_step reports [1,1,1]. The fix is gpu_flip_step resizing storage when Resolution changes, so it is not fixed separately. Frames still say Complete: BUG-hc5h.
close_reason: Resolution applies at run time; gpu_flip_resolution_card_resizes_at_runtime proves 64 -> 32 -> 100 with step and whitewater frames; the clamp is now lattice_refusal by name. feat/gpu-flip-coarse-solve 30477970e.

title: GPU FLIP Resolution applies on change: wire the lattice into the water atoms (seam P7b)

The fixed 5-level V-cycle removed the level count as graph structure, but Resolution still cannot apply on change: every lattice atom in gpu_flip_preset.rs holds nodes_x/y/z, cell_size and lattice_min_* as build params (Builder::lattice, lattice_box), dot_products/combine_rows hold row_length, array capacities are planned from those params and array_growth regrows only CPU-origin arrays, and band_layers (3 at 32, 4 at 64, 6 at 128 node.extend_faces copies) changes the node count. Work: wire the lattice from node.gpu_flip_domain outputs into every lattice atom and row_length; re-derive GPU-origin array capacities when the wired lattice changes; fix the extension band at the ceiling count; delete built_resolution and its refusal in gpu_flip_domain.rs; water panel end-to-end test. Gate per P7b.
notes: Also: the Resolution and Built Resolution params still declare range 8..512 (gpu_flip_domain.rs ParamDef), but anything not a multiple of 16 is refused; make the slider step in multiples of 16 from 16 when the lattice wiring lands.
close_reason: The GPU FLIP step and its pressure solver read the lattice at run time; no lattice atom holds build params. feat/gpu-flip-coarse-solve 30477970e.

title: GPU FLIP Resolution rebuild: where the water graph is rebuilt (seam P7b)
description: BUG-86kv (GPU FLIP Resolution knob) chose option (c): changing Resolution rebuilds the water graph, multigrid levels derived from the lattice at build. Nothing in the codebase rebuilds a generator graph structure from a param today, so the mechanism is a new cross-crate concept. Options: (1) edit-time regeneration: an undoable command (app-side, since editing cannot call the renderer builder) regenerates the water nodes in the def at the new lattice with gpu_flip_preset::water_def and splices them by node name, the way render_def splices the render; the def stays fully expanded and editable, but user edits inside the solver nodes are overwritten and the scene (fill, column) must be read back from the domain node. (2) build-time expansion: the def keeps the solver compact and the preset runtime expands it at build, the way scene modifiers expand from their preparation params (SetSceneModifierPreparationParamCommand, scene_modifier_expand); the shipped JSON shrinks and the solver is no longer hand-editable. Either way Resolution must stop being a live param: a modulation, automation or MIDI target would rebuild per value, so it routes like a preparation param, applied once on release. Blocks LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md P7b on feat/gpu-flip-liquid-fields.
close_reason: Superseded: Peter overruled the rebuild (BUG-86kv option c). No graph rebuild and no new mechanism; the V-cycle has a fixed 5 levels at every lattice, Resolution a multiple of 16, coarsest level smoothed by 16 red-black rounds each way. Measured PCG iterations to 1e-5 match the exact coarse solve at 32, 64 and 128, so a fixed depth does not cap Resolution. Seam P7b rewritten to match.

title: GPU FLIP Resolution knob: how the multigrid V-cycle depth follows Resolution (seam P7b)
description: LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md P7b (SWASH wired lattice) is written for the retired FFT solve (snap to the FFT plan multiple of 8). GPU FLIP now solves pressure with a multigrid V-cycle whose level count is graph structure: multigrid_levels halves while every side is even and one is over COARSEST_SIDE 4, and gpu_flip_preset.rs builds one coarsen/restrict/smooth/prolong chain per level plus a coarse_inverse at the coarsest size. So a live Resolution knob changes the node topology, not just wired scalars. Options: (a) fixed level count, Resolution snapped to a multiple of 2^L, coarsest side grows with Resolution (coarse_inverse is capped at MAX_COARSE_CELLS, so this caps Resolution); (b) a max-depth V-cycle whose surplus levels pass through when the lattice is small (needs a pass-through rule per level, more dispatches at small sizes); (c) rebuild the preset graph on Resolution change (the brief forbids a preset copy per resolution; a rebuild-on-change is a different call). Also owed for P7b: wire nodes/cell_size/lattice_min from node.gpu_flip_domain into every GPU FLIP atom (today baked as params; built_resolution refusal in gpu_flip_domain.rs), and array_growth re-deriving capacities through the tick and Krylov regions. The water panel half is already solver-neutral: LIQUID_DIAL_PARAMS has a GPU FLIP row incl. resolution, and the panel walk is liquid_domain_of over is_liquid_domain; an end-to-end panel test on the GPU FLIP dam break is not written. Blocks the P7b half of the BUG-70l4 follow-up brief.
close_reason: Peter: rebuild the water graph when Resolution changes (option c). Resolution is set in rehearsal, never tuned live; a change already reallocates grids and restarts the water.

title: GPU FLIP solids: zero solid velocity into sealed fluid pockets
description: FLIP Fluids _conditionSolidVelocityField zeroes the solid face velocity around fluid regions with no open face to air, so a moving solid cannot push into an incompressible sealed pocket (the pressure solve would have no solution). GPU FLIP (feat/gpu-flip-solids, node.solid_face_velocity) does not port it: it needs a connected-components flood fill over water cells on the GPU. Symptom to expect: a box sealing water against the tank floor or walls drives the solve to its iteration cap with a large residual. Fix shape: a label-propagation atom pair (connected water regions, region touches air) feeding a mask into node.solid_face_velocity. See docs/GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 8 (solids in the water).

description: Symptom (latent): scene_fluid_role_assignments (crates/manifold-editing/src/commands/graph/scene/fluid/roles/lifecycle.rs ~line 95) hides Add Fluid's internal initial-fill role source only when every outgoing wire hits a liquid domain at the same level. A GPU template whose domain sits inside Live Matter would route that source into the Live Matter group port, so the internal source would show up as an object assignment. Root cause: direct-child check, same class as BUG-2xcw (solver-neutral fluid lookups). Fix shape: decide internal-ness by the role source living in the group that holds the liquid domain (liquid_domains_in from manifold_core::liquid_domain), not by the wire's immediate target. Not hit today: no GPU template carries an internal role source yet.

title: Exact per-tick liquid force replay vs frame-held controls (D28)
description: Liquid forces (seam P8, Forces and impulses for GPU liquids) now give each tick its own force lattice, sampled at the tick start from the acceleration field recorded once per display frame and interpolated between frames. That is identical across frame rates only while the field moves linearly in time between frames; a curved field (an LFO, an eased clip) differs slightly at 30 fps vs 60 fps at the in-between ticks. Exact equivalence needs the matter domain to evaluate the field at every tick start through the authored-history replay (preset_runtime/physics_sampling.rs), which today excludes the matter domain on purpose: GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN D28 holds controls per display frame, and the executor asserts coupled pairs sample together. Call: accept frame-linear interpolation, or move liquid fields onto the per-tick authored replay (changes D28 for fields only).
close_reason: Decided 2026-10-03: liquid forces evaluate at every simulation tick through the per-tick authored replay, never held per display frame. Simulation and forces must not couple to display fps. Work tracked in the per-tick forces task.

title: Retire provider-era hooks and fix tier guards for Claude-only roster
description: Hook cleanup after the Claude-only roster change (2026-10-01). Staged in /tmp/routingfix/INSTALL.md on branch docs/agent-routing-claude. Real behaviour gaps: context-ceiling-guard exempts every Fable lane via LEAD_TIER=fable|k3; subagent-stop-gate EXECUTOR_TIERS excludes Opus and Fable lanes; enforcement-table.json lists missing seat-freeze-guard.py so gate_runner pre-wave fails its manifest check. Fix shape: strip with tests in one pass, delete hook + test + settings.json registration + enforcement row together.

title: GPU liquid force lattice sampled per frame, not per tick: 30 vs 60 fps export drifts under an animated field
description: Symptom (expected, unmeasured): with an animated scene force field (LFO/beat ramp into a Scene Force), a 30 fps export of a matter liquid differs from the 60 fps one, breaking seam invariant I7. Root cause: LiquidFields::prepare (liquid/fields.rs) samples the field once per display frame into one staging slot, so every tick in the frame reads the same lattice; the seam P8 text asks for per-tick lattices. Fix shape: one lattice slot per tick due this frame (bounded by the clock max ticks), indexed by tick_index in LIQUID_FIELD, plus a conformance check ExportFrameRateIndependent with an animated field. Static fields and impulses are unaffected.
close_reason: Per-tick force lattices: LiquidFields records the field each frame and samples it at every tick start; atoms read their tick lattice via first_tick/force_lattices. Proven by liquid_force_lattices_match_across_frame_rates (60 vs 30 fps identical). Curved-in-time fields: BUG-25nu.

Then delete the FLIP row BUG-xt71 exemption in liquid/conformance.rs.

title: GPU FLIP density share 1 vs 0.5: packing against missing water
description: With the half-full surface rule and the half-cell correction cap, share 1 no longer overshoots at 128 (12.1% worst past rest, was 48%). Against share 0.5 it packs less but leaves more particles missing inside: at 64 worst missing 13.8% vs 9.3% (FFT record 10.3%), last-30 6.9% vs 5.3%; at 128 14.5% vs 10.4%. Skin-corrected meshed volume max also rose (64: 11.6% vs 4.3%), though the raw mesh at frame 299 is within 1.2% (64) and 2.6% (128). Shipped at 1 per the review brief. Call: keep 1, go back to 0.5, or measure a middle share. Numbers: docs/GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 6 (measures); probe gpu_flip_refined_density_causes.

title: GPU FLIP narrower particle-to-face kernel
description: Next after the gpu-flip-multigrid landing, its own step, after or beside the ghost-fluid surface. node.particles_to_faces uses a tent with a +-1 cell box per axis, about 1.15x the reach of the engine Wyvill kernel (radius 0.866 cells, velocityadvector.cpp 467-537) and reaching the box corners; it averages more particles, smooths sheets into ropes and blurs the velocity differences that tear them. Try Wyvill or a narrower tent; keep only if sheet breakup improves at 64 and 128 with race rows no worse. Spec: docs/GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 8 (owed), parity audit item 6.

title: GPU FLIP ghost-fluid free surface
description: Next after the gpu-flip-multigrid landing, its own step. GPU FLIP uses first-order Dirichlet (air cell centre p=0), which puts the surface half a cell out; a one-cell sheet feels the wrong push and holds together instead of breaking into drops. Match the FLIP Fluids engine ghost-fluid rows (pressuresolver.cpp 820-920, theta from a particle-distance surface, clamp like _maxtheta). Gate: sheet breakup on the Dam Break at 64 and 128 against the engine; race rows no worse. Spec: docs/GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 8 (owed), parity audit item 5.
notes: Ghost rows ported (64cf01747, feat/gpu-flip-ghost-fluid). Gate mixed: breakup mean 0.30->0.38% at 64 (engine 0.42), 0.56->0.58% at 128 (engine 0.86); lid contact up 12k->20k at 64 and 142k->173k at 128; GPU ms 17.0->18.1 and 101->106. With Wyvill (BUG-98wm) on top, 64 reaches the engine mean (0.42) and 128 reaches 0.65. Open pending the coordinator's call on whether ghost stays default-on.
close_reason: Ghost-fluid free surface ships in node.gpu_flip_step and the pressure solver (finest level and CG read phi; coarse levels plain). Breakup 0.40%/0.62% vs 0.42%/0.65%. feat/gpu-flip-coarse-solve 30477970e.

title: GPU liquid template: make fluid lookups solver-neutral before GPU FLIP becomes the Add Fluid default
description: Before DEFAULT_LIQUID_TEMPLATE can point at a GPU FLIP template: (1) roles.rs:413 and roles.rs:652 only look for the liquid domain as a direct child of the fluid group, so a domain nested in a Live Matter group is missed; search through nested groups via is_liquid_domain. (2) scene_exposure/fluid_objects.rs, scene_exposure/fluid_quality.rs and manifold-app projection/scene.rs:515 match the FLIP type id; check each and move it to the is_liquid_domain predicate where it is not FLIP-specific. (3) Wire the GPU template world controls (gravity, speed, reset ports). Found during seam P9 (Add Fluid template), branch feat/liquid-p9-add-fluid.
close_reason: Landed on main in c989228ae (batch: liquid fields, occupancy map, lookups)

title: GPU FLIP dot_products caps at 64 workgroups: starves the GPU at 128³ and fixes the sum order
description: Review item 7 on 987220079. node.dot_products reduces in two passes with at most 64 workgroups in the first, so at 128³ (2.1M cells) each thread loops ~128 elements serially and the GPU is underfilled; the CG vectors row is 26% of the 128³ solve (docs/GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 6 (measures)). The fixed sum order also sets an f32 floor on r·z and p·s that is part of the ~1e-5 residual floor. Fix shape: scale the first-pass group count with the length (capacity proved on the CPU, partials array sized from it), keep the second pass in one workgroup, and measure the floor with a pairwise or Kahan partial against the f64 reference before and after.
close_reason: Landed in 82ca3721e: CG reductions fold into the passes they follow, one partial per workgroup sized from the lattice, no cap; 128^3 solve 19.9 to 18.7 ms, bit-equal direct solves

title: GPU FLIP coarse levels re-derive L at 2h with no check that r·z keeps its sign
description: Review item 6 on 987220079. The V-cycle coarse levels use the masked Laplacian re-derived at 2h (gpu_flip_preset.rs v_cycle, the pressure_smooth and pressure_residual nodes at level h·2^k), not the Galerkin product R·L·P. PCG needs an SPD preconditioner; with masked full-weighting restriction, masked trilinear prolongation and a re-derived coarse operator, symmetry holds by construction (R = Pᵀ/8, symmetric sweeps, exact symmetric coarse inverse), but positive definiteness is not proved. Symptom if it fails: r·z ≤ 0 in some iteration, β or α flip sign, CG stalls or diverges. Nothing checks it today. Fix shape: a CPU check in scripts/mgpcg_reference.py and a GPU proof that r·z > 0 every iteration on the Dam Break, deep pool and splash problems (read rz from node.conjugate_gradient state in a test), plus a refusal or Galerkin fallback if a case goes non-positive.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: GPU proof pressure_module_preconditioner_keeps_rz_negative on feat/gpu-flip-engine-port: r.z<0, p.s>0 on 704 iterations (Dam Break, deep pool, still pool). Still owed: CPU check in mgpcg_reference.py and a fallback.

title: glb_conformance_sweep panics: duplicate node handle MetalRoughSpheresNoTextures/mat_0
description: Symptom: scripts/gpu_proofs_gate.py --full-suite, tests/glb_conformance.rs glb_conformance_sweep panics at node_graph/graph.rs:223 Graph::add_node_named: duplicate handle MetalRoughSpheresNoTextures/mat_0 (mapped to NodeInstanceId(9), remapped to 11). Seen 2026-10-01 on feat/gpu-flip-multigrid, which touches no glTF import code; not checked on main. Root cause unknown; suspect the import assigning one material handle per material index while two meshes share a material, so the assembler adds the material node twice. Fix shape: dedupe material nodes by handle at assembly, then rerun the sweep.
close_reason: Root cause: static multi-material imports (build_static_compound_group) fold every part into one group body, but each part scene_object handle was only deduped against its own k (unique_group_name), and the primary part was re-stamped with the raw material name, unchecked. A first material named mat_0 collided with the primary pbr_material handle mat_0. Fix: dedupe_part_names dedupes every compound scene_object handle against all other handles in the shared body; primary re-stamp uses the slash-safe material_group_base. Regression test compound_part_names_never_collide_with_sibling_inner_handles; glb_conformance passes via gpu_proofs_gate.py. Commit 848d9d7c7 on fix/glb-duplicate-handle (not landed).

title: RT noise gate refl_history_read ceiling sits inside load noise
description: Symptom: scripts/rt_noise_gate.py goes RED on refl_history_read with no code change. An A/B under load on 2026-10-01 (origin/main c107c6881 vs fix/rt-proof-timeouts f64996e85, alternating, 3 captures each) read medians main 0.227 / 0.252, branch 0.233 / 0.251, against a 0.237 ceiling; single runs span 0.225-0.294 on both. Root cause: the 2026-08-27 baseline ceiling has no margin for run-to-run spread when the GPU is shared (captures took about 12 min, not 40-130 s). Fix shape: re-record on a quiet machine with a spread margin, or make the gate refuse to judge when capture time shows contention.

title: fluid_particle_ring_exhaustion_never_blocks fails: test rot after held-clock change
description: Symptom: lib test node_graph::fluid::particle_tests::fluid_particle_ring_exhaustion_never_blocks panics at particle_tests.rs:174 (assert!(runtime.busy)) deterministically under cargo test --features gpu-proofs. Root cause: f135d7b33 (2026-09-30, Discard Physics World impulses while paused or at Simulation Speed 0) made FluidRuntime::advance return early when held.is_held() && initialized && !blocking. HeldClock::observe marks held when the same transport time is observed twice in a row. The test calls frame(tick 8,false) and then frame(tick 8,false) again after the event signal, so the second observe at identical time is "held" and no request is sent. Not load-related; real product behavior is intended (paused water sends no new request). Fix shape: test rot. After signal(), observe a later time than the last call (e.g. tick 9, or advance time by one TICK) so transport is not held, then assert busy and completed_tick accordingly; do not loosen the assertions.
close_reason: Closed

title: Structural cards: rebuild a generator preset when a structural card changes
description: General capability (not SWASH-only): a card marked structural re-runs the generator preset build-time expansion (like scene-modifier expansion) and rebuilds the graph when it changes. First user: SWASH Steps per Frame (integer from 1 up, default 2, density solve stays on each tick last step; ~11 ms per step at 64). Forbidden: a gated zero-work step loop, a depth-3 region shortcut. Today the shipped SWASH preset is static JSON from a test-only builder, so no card can change the step count.

title: Pressure Passes as a live SWASH card
description: Peter wants SWASH pressure accuracy as a card: Auto (3n/8) or a manual pass count; a count past the Krylov kernel cap is a named refusal. Today passes are baked into krylov_basis, krylov_givens, krylov_solve, dot_products and combine_rows params and several arrays are sized from them at build, so raising passes from a card only produces per-frame refusals. Shape: on P7b (SWASH wired lattice) sizes — passes travel on a wire from swash_domain, the atoms grow storage at run time (array growth). Tooltip: cost vs accuracy. CPU extent proof must cover the extremes allowed.
close_reason: Superseded by the converged MGPCG solve in BUG-l2h3.23; no fixed pass count to expose

title: Structural RT-D4 guard: count blocking GPU waits inside render(), asserted zero, back in the default gate
description: Since BUG-ca67 (RT proofs time out the GPU) the three never_stalls_past_20ms gates (rt_p1_region_probe, rt_r1_reflection, rt_t2b_temporal_wiring) run only under rt-perf-proofs, because a wall-clock frame time in the parallel gpu_proofs binary measures the other tests. That leaves the default gate without the RT-D4 guard: enabling RT, reflections, or toggling temporal_upscale must never do a synchronous accel build or commit()+waitUntilCompleted() inside a frame. Shape: a per-thread counter in manifold-gpu bumped by every blocking wait (commit_and_wait_completed/_scheduled/_timed/_profiled, the tracer.rs waitUntilCompleted sites); the three gates read it around runtime.render() and assert zero after the warmup window, with no timing. Check first which render paths wait legitimately (headless readback, gpu_readback, layer_compositor) and keep them outside the counted span or name them. Keep the wall-clock versions as rt-perf-proofs probes.

title: SWASH Krylov pass: fewer dispatches for the vector work, after workgroup zeroing is fixed
description: Each GMRES pass does its vector work (sum of z, collar gather, two Gram-Schmidt rounds, norm, unit vector, Givens) in 13 dispatches and 3 copies, about 88 us per pass at 64 cubed and 151 at 128 on a quiet GPU. It is the solve Krylov stage, 5.9 ms of a 42 ms 64-cubed frame (56 passes). Two prototypes, both correct against an f64 CPU reference on 24 passes at 32, 64 and 128, did not beat it (feat/fft-water 8c14559ab, taken out after): one workgroup per pass is bandwidth-bound on one core (154 us at 64, 765 at 128); four dispatches of many workgroups, each finishing the last reduction in its prologue and sweeping only live collar entries, run 102 us at 64 and 164 at 128. Most of that is naga workgroup-memory zeroing: the polyfill has one thread store every workgroup array before the first barrier; 16 KB of reduction array cost about 25 us per dispatch, cutting it to 4 KB halved the pass. Next: make that zeroing cheap or unneeded (subgroup reductions in manifold-gpu, which needs the naga subgroup capability, or a parallel zeroing polyfill), re-measure the four-dispatch shape, and build it only if it beats the atoms: four atoms, one dispatch each, grouped as an Arnoldi-pass node group, the old atoms deleted. The same zeroing tax sits on every existing kernel with workgroup arrays (dot_products and others). Later, as a freeze-compiler item, not now: the compiler fusing a reduction finish into the next dispatch prologue in general.
close_reason: FFT/SWASH-specific; GPU FLIP multigrid pressure solve landed on main (410c45347) and replaced the FFT solver (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN archived)

title: Whitewater GPU cost over its 2 ms p95 target: surface_crossings walks every cell
description: GPU_WHITEWATER_DESIGN.md P6 (Side by side and cost) measured the whitewater GPU total at 2.60 ms p50 / 3.61 ms p95 at 64 (target p95 <= 2 ms, cleaner of two runs on a shared machine). node.surface_crossings is 1.44 / 1.59 ms of it: one thread per whitewater cell (343,000 at 64) walks all 144 refined edges of its footprint with a solid trilinear per edge, though almost every cell is far from the surface. Fix shape: an early-out when the footprint's refined level-set nodes all share a sign (no crossing possible), keeping the level value the cell still needs (trilinear), then re-measure with whitewater_side_by_side on a quiet machine. The lifecycle snapshot and output copies are the next largest (0.22 / 1.11 ms). Reference: whitewater_scene_tests.rs whitewater_side_by_side cost table.
notes: Quiet p95 measured 2026-10-02 (feat/liquid-odds, M4 Max, GPU-queue lock held, whitewater_side_by_side at 64, 320x180 demo, frames 11..=211): GPU whitewater total p50 1.600 / p95 1.772 ms, under the 2 ms target. The GPU FLIP whole frame is 32.1 / 33.7 ms GPU. FLIP engine whitewater cost is 37.8 / 190.1 ms. Ready to close once Peter accepts.
close_reason: Measured under GPU queue lock: whitewater p50 1.600 ms, p95 1.772 ms, under the 2 ms target (feat/liquid-odds 042714a66)

title: Whitewater P5 preset remainder: Whitewater group and copies objects in the SWASH Dam Break preset, swash_whitewater_emits, round trip

What waits for the SWASH Dam Break preset JSON (being authored by the SWASH contract worker as liquid seam P7a, SWASH on the contract): add the Whitewater group, its wires and the three copies objects (spray, foam, bubbles) to that preset and nothing else; swash_whitewater_emits running the preset through the graph; graph-tool validate and fusion clean on the preset; a preset round trip; the P5 demo PNGs at 1.5 s and 3 s from the preset. comments.text: The whitewater content this bead waits to add is already shipped: the GPU FLIP Dam Break (formerly SWASH) carries the whitewater stage and Foam/Spray/Bubbles objects, built by the water family recipe (docs/WATER_FAMILY_DESIGN.md (water family) F1a). title: SWASH FFT plan misses cost CPU encode on the frame they happen
description: The P3c region builds an MPSGraph FFT plan the first time a window shape is used (device cache, GpuDevice::fft_plan). The design wanted the full box and the first shape built at load. Measured at 64 cubed: about 1.5 ms per plan build plus 0.3-1 ms first encode quiet; miss frames encode in 17-19 ms against 12.6 ms; one run under load 9-11 showed 150-183 ms on miss frames. Shape: build plans off the content thread and meanwhile run on the smallest built shape on the ladder that holds the window (still exact: any box holding the water and collar gives the same answer), and build the whole box at load.
close_reason: Plan misses came from new window shapes; with the window taken out (fca2d6034) every FFT node runs one shape, built on first use as before P3c.

title: SWASH helper planes on the active region window
description: P3c windows the box solve only. The six-view chart helper keeps whole-box planes: 6.65 ms of a 42.6 ms 64-cubed Dam Break frame, 28.1 ms at 128 cubed. The design (docs/FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P3c part (b)) says the planes use the window longest side. On the Dam Break and the still pool that side is the box side, so nothing is lost there; a tall narrow column or a small splash in a big tank would gain. Shape: the chart atoms take the window origin and lengths as wired scalars the way the cosine chain does, with extent rules in the liquid extent proofs.
close_reason: There is no window to put the helper planes on after fca2d6034. If a GPU-decided window comes back (BUG-l2h3.7), windowing the chart is part of that work.

title: SWASH P3c part (a): grid and face passes over occupied 8-cubed blocks only
description: Not built in P3c (docs/FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P3c part (a)). Rule from the P3c outcome: the block list must be decided on the GPU from the same tick (indirect dispatch from this step classified water), never read back to the CPU, so the words are the same at every frame rate and live never waits. Ceiling at 64 cubed, render smoke before P3c (load 2.5-3.4, scaled GPU ms of a 42.6 ms frame): particle to face 1.87, extrapolation 0.40, pressure gradient 0.11, gravity and walls 0.05, divergence 0.03, classify 0.02, so about 2.5 ms; the Dam Break peaks at 42% of 8-cubed blocks holding water. Particle passes (sort, face to particle, advect) already scale with particles, not the box. Every reader of a skipped block must see defined values (cleared or masked), since arrays stay whole-box.
close_reason: SWASH-era; the occupied-block narrow band is deferred to BUG-jyot

title: Run-time node errors reach only stderr, never the performer
description: Symptom: anything a node reports through EffectNodeContext::error at run time (the MPM non-finite tick halt, the Liquid Surface mesh-capacity overflow, FLIP and matter coupling failures) is printed as "[graph error] node ..." by the executor (node_graph/execution.rs, the error_scratch drain) and goes nowhere else: no node badge, no panel line, no ContentState field. On stage the water just stops or blanks with no reason shown. Seam invariant I11 (overflow is counted and reported) only holds in the log; the P4 conformance suite reads these errors through a gpu-proofs-only tap (NodeErrorTap) because nothing else carries them. Root cause: the executor has no channel for run-time node errors beyond eprintln. Fix shape: keep the latest error per node on the runtime (bounded, deduplicated), carry it in the content state snapshot, and show it on the node and the layer the way setup refusals already show; then point the conformance suite at that channel and delete the tap.

title: Impulse cannot be fired at a body coupled to Live Matter water
description: Symptom: a scene impulse aimed at a Box3D body that shares a scene with a Live Matter (node.matter_domain) liquid fails at capture with "Impulse: graph has no prepared physics ancestry". prepare_scene_impulse resolves the body and redirects it to the matter domain fine; capture_scene_impulse_at_source then calls observe_physics_at_source, which needs physics_sample_steps. physics_sample_steps (preset_runtime/physics_sampling.rs) leaves out a matter-coupled pair on purpose (the domain records controls per display frame and owns its world), so a scene whose only physics is that pair gets None and every capture is refused. fire_scene_impulse (the product Fire path) goes through the same capture, so an Impulse modifier on a box floating in MPM water cannot fire. MatterDomain::physics_impulse_stamp and enqueue_physics_impulse already handle rigid targets, so the domain side is built. Found by the liquid conformance collision check (seam P4) trying to kick the box. Fix shape: when no node replays history, observe_physics_at_source has nothing to sample; record the observation time and admit the capture, then prove a kick on WaterFloatingBoxMatter through fire_scene_impulse on the GPU.

title: Liquid surface resolution scale at SWASH 64: 3 (finer detail) vs 2 (fits the frame budget)
description: Surface plus render on the critical path at SWASH 64 with every exact lever in (perf/liquid-surface): scale 3 is 13.1 ms on Dam Break and 11.3 on Still Pool; scale 2 is 6.7 and 5.1. Target was about 6. Look: scale 3 keeps a fine dimpled ripple pattern on the pool and crisper small droplets; scale 2 is smoother and softer, loses the smallest droplets and the finest crinkle, and splash sheets read slightly thicker. Remaining exact levers (BUG-8c4w occupied lattice bricks, BUG-8amv welded indexed mesh) are estimated at 3 to 4 ms together, which would bring scale 3 to roughly 9 to 10, not 6. Stills this session: /tmp/ls_smoke_s3b vs /tmp/ls_smoke_s2b, frames 90, 240, 300 and paused, both scenes. Needs a look call from Peter.
close_reason: Decided 2026-10-01: SWASH at 64 uses surface resolution scale 2 (cheaper, 6.65 ms surface+render vs 13.13, less dimpled).

title: Liquid surface mesh: welded indexed vertices instead of a triangle soup
description: node.volume_surface_mesh emits a triangle soup: at SWASH 64, surface scale 3, Dam Break peaks at 1.41M vertices for 469k triangles, and render_scene draws it three times (volume signed path 0.7 ms, transmissive depth prepass 0.5, transmissive layer 3.2, of which roughly half is vertex work). Marching cubes shares each edge vertex between about six triangles, so one vertex per crossed lattice edge plus an index buffer cuts vertex shading about 5x on all three draws. Estimate 1.5 to 2 ms off the render tail, look-identical. Touches the mesher output format, render_scene indexed draws, volume optics, and every consumer of the mesh; needs a design pass first. Measurements in BUG-l24y (GPU liquid surface kernels cost).

title: Liquid surface: compute only occupied lattice bricks for smoothing, count and scan
description: At SWASH 64, surface scale 3, the three node.smooth_lattice passes (0.59 ms each), node.count_surface_triangles (0.59) and the offsets scan (0.35) run over the whole 211^3 lattice every frame, though 86 percent of nodes sit at the outside cap. Fix shape: keep dense storage, derive active bricks from node.particles_near_bins at a wider reach, dispatch these passes indirectly over active bricks, and reset bricks that went inactive to the cap. Estimate 1.5 to 2 ms off the surface critical path. The mesh stays identical; the lattice is not bit-identical in cap-only bricks, because smoothing a constant cap can round by an ulp. Needs a design pass (GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md) before building. Measurements in BUG-l24y (GPU liquid surface kernels cost).

title: WaterDamBreakMatter differs between two direct runs in one process
description: Symptom: two builds of the bundled WaterDamBreakMatter in one test process (PresetRuntime, same params and frame times, encode replay off in both, pipelines warm) sometimes match in every byte and sometimes differ from frame 2 on: matter_frame.particles_b, matter_state out/grid/sort order and every liquid_* array downstream, and the rendered frame by a mean |delta| of exactly 1.186e-2 or 1.212e-2. Also seen: the step order of independent nodes (the six cube meshes) differs between two builds of the same preset. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: (1) build-order nondeterminism (hash iteration in compile or planning) changing step order or storage assignment, with a consumer depending on it; (2) process-global state that differs per build (rebuild epoch, a tick or ping-pong parity in matter_frame, async pipeline readiness); (3) block-sort order feeding a non-integer accumulation. Fix shape: two PresetRuntime builds in one process (the dam_break helper in crates/manifold-renderer/tests/gpu_proofs/encode_replay.rs on feat/encode-replay does this), print plan step order and the Matter tick per frame for both, find the first array that differs at frame 2. title: SWASH FFTs: keep MPSGraph or write our own compute FFT kernels
description: Encode replay (docs/ENCODE_REPLAY_DESIGN.md on feat/encode-replay) cannot record MPSGraph work into an indirect command buffer, and MPSGraph FFTs are about 46% of SWASH CPU encode (280 x 22-25 us = 6.3-7.1 ms per frame at 64). Options: (a) cache the wrapper objects GpuFft::encode builds per call, about 1.4 ms saved, keeps FFT design D9; (b) replace MPSGraph with our own compute FFT kernels, which the approved Vulkan backend needs anyway and which makes the whole solve loop recordable, reverses D9. Lead recommendation: (a) now, decide (b) on the encode-replay P1b measured numbers; lean (b) because Vulkan needs it regardless. Peter decides.
notes: Decided 2026-10-01: build our own compute FFT kernels (Vulkan needs them regardless), switch SWASH to them only if their GPU time matches or beats MPSGraph at SWASH sizes; measure a prototype first.
close_reason: FFT/SWASH-specific; GPU FLIP multigrid pressure solve landed on main (410c45347) and replaced the FFT solver (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN archived)

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Own FFT kernels also unlock the P3c active region (option B): a window the GPU decides from the same tick, with lengths read from a GPU buffer, so no CPU read-back, no lag and no pad beyond the collar. The read-back window was built, measured and taken out (feat/fft-water fca2d6034) because under the liquid tick region it cannot be the same at every frame rate without a pad covering the whole box. What it bought, render smoke frame GPU p50, contended (load 5-12): 64 still pool 41.4 to 36.7 ms (4.6 ms, box solve 8.1 to 6.4); 64 Dam Break 42.6 to 41.7 ms (about 1 ms); 128 Dam Break 234.8 to 230.6 ms, window 97% of the box on average because the splash reaches the lid. Record: docs/FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P3c Outcome. -- Opus 5.5, SWASH worker seat

title: Liquid Surface: apply the solid and border after the last smoothing pass
description: Found while building the liquid lattice rail (LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md P2b). node.particle_volume sets lattice border nodes to the band value and caps solid nodes at max(phi, 0), then up to three node.smooth_lattice passes run on the result, and node.count_surface_triangles and node.volume_surface_mesh read the smoothed lattice. None of the three later atoms reads the solid lattice, so smoothing can pull liquid-side values into wall-solid and border nodes: the mesh can poke into walls or open at the lattice edge at high Smoothing and Resolution Scale. Not observed on stage yet; derived from the pipeline order. Fix shape: make the wall/border clamp the last step before meshing (a clamp atom after smoothing that reads the solid lattice, or the solid wired into the mesher atoms), shared by FLIP and MPM. Then add the structural test: dials at their extremes, every border node stays air. The padding-is-solid check already lives in liquid/lattice.rs.
close_reason: Landed on main (5e28328f4 RT proof timeouts; 13e3fc4d1 liquid seam P2b-P4)

title: divide_by_value fused region shrinks to its one-element divisor
description: Symptom: node.divide_by_value declares no fused output capacity, so a fused region holding it uses the default min over every required array input, gathered ones included. Its divisor is one element, so the fused kernel anchors at count = min(arrayLength(&src_0), arrayLength(&src_1)) = 1 and node.wgsl_compute sizes dst to 1: only out[0] is written. Unfused, its output follows values. Seen in the fused WGSL of WaterDamBreakMatter with node.matter_face_component feeding divide_by_value (face grid work, BUG-imy3 GPU whitewater). Latent today: no shipped graph fuses divide_by_value with a producer (SWASH feeds it from boundaries). Root cause: the atom relies on the default MinInputs capacity although its divisor is a gathered scalar, the same shape remap_cut_weights solved with FromInput. Fix shape: add output_capacity: FusedOutputCapacity::FromInput { input: "values" } to the primitive! plus a fused-vs-unfused proof with a producer; consider probing capacity composition with descending synthetic lengths too, so a gathered short input is caught for every atom rather than per atom.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Fixed on feat/gpu-flip-multigrid: node.divide_by_value declares output_capacity FromInput{values}, so a fused region counts from the values row, not the one-element divisor. Proof: gpu_flip_residual_into_divide_fuses (fused = unfused bit for bit, one region). Ready to close at landing.

title: Add Light redo mints the light a new NodeId, so undo then redo changes the graph
description: Symptom: AddSceneLightCommand execute, undo, execute gives a different graph: the light node_id changes (seen as ae5a634f then ce71372b in scene_liquid_recognition_survives_edit_undo_save_and_reload). title: WaterDamBreakMatter thumbnail renders differently run to run
description: Symptom: generate-preset-thumbnails on WaterDamBreakMatter (same JSON, same code) gave a different PNG in 1 of 6 runs: 7,979 of 36,864 pixels, max channel delta 81; the particles and spray sit in a slightly different state. Fix shape: thumbnail and other offline renders run the domain in its offline (waiting) mode so output never depends on GPU timing; add a render-twice-and-compare determinism check for the physics presets. title: Arrays the host reads after the frame are not protected from buffer reuse
description: Symptom: none observed yet (SWASH scene-test reads came out unchanged), but instrumentation dump_array_resources (preset_runtime/instrumentation.rs:322) and harnesses like the SWASH scene runner read intermediate arrays after the frame, and the static array plan can hand their buffer to a later array, so the read could see another array contents.
