title: SWASH separating walls inside the pressure solve (walls push water, never pull)
description: Water at a solid wall can be held by suction: with no flow through the wall face, the incompressible solve pulls a water layer against the lid instead of letting it fall away. A real separating wall lets water leave a wall face (flow away from the wall allowed, wall pressure never negative), solved inside the pressure solve, probably as extra unknowns on wall faces through the face-collar machinery P3b of docs/FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md builds. Evidence (2026-09-30, 64 cubed Dam Break, fft_water_splash_causes_64 against fft_water_engine_race): a crude version, pressure read as max(p, 0) in every cell touching a box wall inside node.subtract_pressure, with the 0.2-cell wall margin, took the share of particles above 3 m at frame 134 from 0.088% to 0.011% (engine 0.010%) and emptied the lid by frame 119. It cannot ship: the projection is left with about 180 times the divergence (left undone rms 0.42/s against 0.0023). Patch of the crude version: /tmp/separating_walls.patch (not durable; it is a subtract_pressure_at(cell, n, separating) helper returning select(p, max(p, 0.0), separating && cell on a wall) used for both sides of the pressure step, plus a Separating Walls 0/1 param and a WaterScene field). Blocked on the BUG-h8or (lid slabs) wall-placement probe: the engine reaches 0.010% with no separating wall, and its wall sits half a cell past its last free face while SWASH walls sit on it. If matching that placement closes the gap, this task is not needed.
notes: 2026-09-30: the wall-placement question from BUG-h8or (lid slabs) could not be settled with a particle margin as a stand-in (see that bead). A faithful test needs fractional wall cells, the P3b solid machinery. Re-judge this task after that test.

title: SWASH Dam Break splash flattens into slabs along the lid at 1.5 s
description: Symptom: at 64 cubed, frame 90 (1.5 s) of the SWASH Dam Break render, the left and middle splash columns reach the 4 m lid and spread into flat horizontal strips along it. The FLIP exports and the WaterDamBreakGpu preset at the same frame only touch the lid at the far right corner; their left columns stop short. Root cause unknown. Suspects: SWASH loses less energy than FLIP, so the columns climb higher (compare the race motion reports, highest point per frame); or the lid acts no-slip or sticky, so water that touches it clings instead of falling. Fix shape: compare the highest-point curve of SWASH vs the engine race over frames 60-120 first; if the heights match, look at the lid boundary condition. Seen in look/water-material stills (swash_look_variants_64, frames 90 and 240).
notes:
2026-09-30, 64 cubed, fft_water_splash_causes_64 against fft_water_engine_race (whitewater off, no obstacle). Geometry matches WaterDamBreak.json. Energy matches: speed mean, p99, top and highest point per frame are within a few percent of the engine. The gap is how long water stays at the lid. Particles within 10 cm of the lid at frames 59/74/89/104/119/134: SWASH 495/676/916/662/370/179, engine 86/90/105/82/13/0. Share above 3 m at frame 134: SWASH 0.157%, engine 0.010%. Not the density correction: rate 0 holds more. Cause 1: node.faces_to_particles clamps particles 0.001 cells off a wall face, where the grid wall-normal velocity is about 0, so a particle pressed on the lid barely moves off it. The engine keeps particles 0.2 cells off a wall that sits half a cell past its last free face, where the normal velocity is 70% of the interior. A 0.2-cell margin: frame 134 above 3 m 0.088%, lid empty by frame 149, packing 0.3 points worse. 0.3 cells: 0.042%. Cause 2: suction. A no-penetration lid lets the pressure hold a water layer up. A crude max(p, 0) at wall cells plus the 0.2 margin gives 0.011% at frame 134, matching the engine, but leaves about 180 times the divergence (left undone rms 0.42/s against 0.0023), so it cannot ship. The proper version is a separating wall condition in the solve. Not explained: at frames 59-89 SWASH still holds 3-5 times the engine lid layer with both changes (sep + 0.3 margin: 514/520/353), so the frame 90 slabs shrink by about half but stay. Tried and refuted: zeroing the FLIP old grid wall faces (the engine convention) made it worse (1084 at frame 89).
2026-09-30, side-wall sheet probe (fft_water_splash_causes_64 and fft_water_engine_splash_64, water within 25 cm of the side walls, every 5 frames), with the 0.2-cell margin shipped. Same mass and speed: share above 2 m 0.47-0.59% SWASH against 0.41-0.51% engine at frames 39-59, mean rising speed within 0.3 m/s at every frame. Different shape: the SWASH sheet above 2.5 m is thin and hugs the wall (mean 4.5-5.5 cm from the wall, under a cell) where the engine sheet is 11-22 cm thick, and the SWASH top runs 0.25-0.6 m higher from frame 14 on, reaching the lid at frame 49; the engine sheet tops out at 3.65 m at frame 59 and never reaches the lid. So the frame 59-89 lid layer is the thin wall film running up to the lid. Wall placement test, margin as a stand-in for the engine wall sitting half a cell past its last free face: 0.45 cells gives 448/574/526 lid particles at frames 59/74/89 (0.2 gives 477/632/843); 0.7 gives none, but the stand-in is not faithful: SWASH wall cells stay full water cells in the density and pressure solves, so water kept off part of them crowds (past rest last 30 frames 12.5% at 0.45, 23.5% at 0.7, against 6.8% at 0.2) and the 0.7 run lost energy (top speed 9 against 12.6 m/s, splash above 2 m at frame 74 0.42% against the engine 1.74%). A faithful test needs fractional wall cells (face and volume weights, as the engine variational solve has), the machinery P3b brings for solids.

title: Liquid Surface mesh capacity is fixed, overflow blanks the water
description: Symptom: the GPU Liquid Surface mesher has a fixed vertex capacity (8.39M). SWASH 128 Dam Break used 83.6% at the splash peak; 256 at surface scale 2 is expected to overflow, and on overflow the mesher empties the mesh (named, safe, but the water vanishes on stage). Root cause: capacity is a fixed param, not derived from the surface lattice. This is a hard ceiling of the kind we do not ship. Fix shape: capacity sized from the surface lattice and grown on demand the way fluid array growth works, counted in the memory census, refused only by the device-memory rail. Measured on feat/fft-water smoke ladder.
notes: 2026-09-30 smoke ladder, run as shipped (capacity 8,388,606): 128 at surface scale 3 peaked at 7,012,956 vertices (83.6%), no overflow. 256 has no overflow number: the build refuses it first. The modifier buffer budget projected 22.70 GB against the 22.61 GB the runtime allows (75% of the recommended working set on the 36 GB M4 Max) at surface scale 1; the smoke estimate for the whole frame is 26.37 GB at scale 1 and 29.43 GB at scale 2. So on this machine the device-memory rail, not the vertex capacity, is the first limit at 256.
close_reason: Closed

title: Array planner reuses no temporaries in SWASH graphs: 256 cubed needs 26 GB, 22 face grids all live
description: Symptom: plan_array_allocations on the SWASH Dam Break (water_def or render_def, feat/fft-water, test fft_water_memory_at_every_lattice) returns 305 fresh allocations and 0 Alias reuses although the plan carries 222 free_after entries. At 256 cubed with surface resolution_scale 1 that is 26.3 GB of arrays, of which about 12 GB is 22 same-size FaceSample grids (257^3 x 32 B = 0.54 GB each: faces, old_extend x2, gravity, project, new_extend x2, density project, advect_extend x2, per step) that are never live at once. 256 cannot run on a 36 GB M4 Max because of it. Root cause: unknown. Suspects in resource_allocation.rs plan_array_allocations: excluded_resources (substep region held resources, carries_resources nodes, IoBridge/NonGpu boundary steps such as running_total), the canvas_arrays propagation loop, or the reusable key (PortType, bytes) never matching. Fix shape: find which exclusion swallows ordinary per-step temporaries and narrow it; gate with a planner test on the SWASH water_def that same-size face grids share roots, plus the SWASH CPU extent proofs and GPU scene guards. Separate cheaper lever: the surface three smoothing passes can ping-pong two buffers.
close_reason: Landed on main in f5782a9b7 (array planner reuse and host-read protection)

title: SWASH collar at its proven bound: one shared Krylov basis plus indirect dispatch from the collar total
description: Approved by the lead (2026-09-30), sequenced into phase 3 (speed), after the race. Today the collar capacity is 8n^2 and overflow is a named error every frame it lasts (running_total capacity: "needs N, holds M", test fluid_running_total_names_a_total_past_its_capacity). Proven bound: a collar cell is air beside water and the 7-cell cross tiles space, so the collar is at most 6n^3/7. Sizing every collar array to 6n^3/7 costs (fft_water_collar_capacity_memory, meshed Dam Break): +68 MB at 64^3, +587 MB at 128^3; growth at 128^3 is the Krylov bases +333 MB, chart_entries +107 MB, combine_rows +40 MB. One basis shared by both steps brings 128^3 to about +414 MB. Shape: one krylov_basis owned across the steps; every collar-length dispatch goes indirect from the collar running total extent (the node.volume_surface_mesh / LiveExtent pattern), so cost follows the live collar, not capacity; the row extra slot (the constant c) moves to index 0 or to the live count so the zero tail stays exact. Gate: the CPU extent proof at 6n^3/7, overflow count zero on the Dam Break, P3 race timings within noise of fixed capacity.
notes: Recount after the position-only density solve (a second 8-pass collar solve per step): at the 6n^3/7 bound the meshed Dam Break grows +152 MB at 64^3 (1290 to 1442 MB) and +1.32 GB at 128^3 (5340 to 6660 MB). Growth at 128^3: Krylov bases +453 MB and current +27 MB, chart_entries +107, combine_rows +80, collar_gather, chart_spread and divide_by_value +53 each. One basis shared across both steps and both solves (26 rows) would be 187 MB instead of 518 MB at the bound.
close_reason: FFT/SWASH-specific; GPU FLIP multigrid pressure solve landed on main (410c45347) and replaced the FFT solver (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN archived)

title: Slot ring hands a slot that is in active use to a second agent
description: Symptom: twice on 2026-09-30 a worker lost its slot mid-work. The SWASH builder lost slot-2 to flip-threads after its context rolled over, and the liquid-seam designer lost slot-2 to look/water-material 32 minutes into its work. The second agent re-pointed the checkout at its own branch, leaving the first agent's files dirty in a checkout it no longer owned. No work was lost only because it had been pushed. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: the lease is tied to a pid that changes when an agent resumes or rolls over (the lease shown as held by the parent claude pid); acquire treats a slot whose lease pid is gone, or whose HEAD is on origin, as reusable even when the worktree has fresh uncommitted edits. Fix shape: acquire must refuse any slot with uncommitted changes or recent file mtimes, regardless of lease state, and leases should key on the agent identity, not a pid. See scripts/agent-worktree.py.

title: SWASH render smoke at 96 and 128: scaling curve and stage split
description: Owed from the SWASH render smoke (branch test/swash-render-smoke, harness swash_render_smoke_tests.rs). 64 is clean (900 frames, Dam Break and still pool). The 96 then 128 runs were blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier in the worker seat, so the scaling curve Peter asked for has one point. title: MPM still pool surface is rough at rest
description: Symptom: WaterStillPoolMatter at res 64 never settles to a flat surface. The Liquid Surface on its particles shows 6.3 deg slope rms at 1-2 cells and 6.5 deg at 2-4 cells at 2 s and 6 s (same numbers both times), where the FLIP still pool is flat (0.02 deg). Particle radius and spacing match FLIP (0.31 dx radius, nearest neighbour 0.30 dx), so it is particle position noise at rest, not the mesher. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: BUG-m9g8 (MPM D5 fixed point loses momentum and inflates J at low-mass grid nodes), BUG-8akp (MPM J grows without bound at Cohesion 0). Fix shape: find what keeps rest particles jittering (A2 settling/ringing gate in GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md section 7 (look gates) would catch it), fix in the solver. Mesher-side mitigation measured in GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md P6f: isotropic blobs halve the surface roughness.

title: swash-residual-bar: how SWASH residual is judged against the double-precision FLIP Fluids engine
description: Peter decides. The P4 win condition (docs/FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md, Peter decisions) says SWASH must match or beat the FLIP Fluids engine on the incompressibility residual. The engine solves its pressure in double precision to 1e-9 relative (fluidsimulation.h _pressureSolveTolerance = 1e-9, max 900 PCG iterations, and it accepts anything under 1.0 when it hits 900). SWASH is f32 on the GPU: measured median relative residual 1.15e-3 at 24 passes and 5.7e-5 at 32 passes at 64x64x64 (P1). f32 keeps about 7 digits, so no f32 solve can store a pressure accurate to 1e-9; read literally, the residual count is lost before the race. Options: (a) judge residual by its visible effect, i.e. volume drift over 300 frames and the still-pool proof; (b) a stated threshold (e.g. the residual at which volume drift stops changing); (c) keep the literal bar, which means SWASH cannot win. Option (d), mixed precision iterative refinement with a double-float residual, is unmeasured and would roughly double the solve cost. P3 reports both solvers residuals (RMS face divergence after / before projection, same oracle on both) whichever way this goes. Needed before P4, not before P3.
close_reason: FFT/SWASH-specific; GPU FLIP multigrid pressure solve landed on main (410c45347) and replaced the FFT solver (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN archived)

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text:
Pass-count rule, measured 2026-09-30 by fft_water_refined_leftover_passes (128³ Dam Break, the step alone, 300 frames, feat/fft-water).

The 128³ divergence comes from too few passes for the collar, not from a wrong target. Measured against the step's own right-hand side (the divergence of the gravity-forced faces over the water cells), all of the leftover sits in water cells beside air, about 8% of water cells. Wall and interior cells hold 2.5e-4 /s rms at every pass count; that floor does not move with passes.

passes | rms median | worst step rms | relative to rhs, median / worst | worst cell | surface cells past 1/s
24 | 1.1e-2 | 0.97 | 4.5e-3 / 0.16 | 59 /s | 4.0%
32 | 1.4e-3 | 0.34 | 6.1e-4 / 0.062 | 14 /s | 0.73%
48 | 1.6e-4 | 0.023 | 6.6e-5 / 3.8e-3 | 1.1 /s | 0

rms median by collar quarter (collars run 19k to 66k cells):
- 24 passes: 2.5e-3, 7.3e-3, 5.9e-2, 0.17
- 32 passes: 1.2e-4, 1.1e-3, 5.8e-3, 4.7e-2
- 48 passes: 1.1e-4, 1.0e-4, 2.3e-4, 1.2e-3

The worst cells are on the side-wall run-up sheet at frames 50 to 52, collar about 60k: the sheet from BUG-h8or (lid slabs).

Proposed rule: passes = 3n/8 on an n³ lattice. The passes a solve needs grow with the square root of its collar, and a scene's collar grows as n², so passes grow with n.
- 24 at 64³ and 48 at 128³ give the same median, 1.5e-4 and 1.6e-4. 256³ would take 96.
- It is fixed when the graph is built, with no per-frame readback (D5).
- The input is the lattice side, not the collar's proven bound 6n³/7 from child .2 (collar at its proven bound) of BUG-l2h3. That worst case grows as n³ and would ask for n^1.5 passes.
- The constant 3/8 comes from this bead's bar: it holds 128³ to what 64³ gives at 24 passes. Even at 48 passes, the quarter with the largest collars sits at 1.2e-3, ten times the floor. At the 32-to-48 rate, clearing it takes about 58 passes.

Cap: the Krylov kernels now hold 64 passes (krylov_givens::MAX_PASSES). That is the declared passes max on krylov_basis, krylov_givens and krylov_solve. A count past it is refused at build by name (params_refusal, surfaced as IllegalParams) and never clamped. 256³ at 96 passes is past the cap. The next step there is sizing the kernels' local arrays from the param when the pipeline is built, not another constant. Not built.

Cost: each pass is one box solve plus projections against every earlier basis row. 48 passes cost about 2× the box solves of 24 and about 4× the projection work. Not timed yet.

Recheck: rerun this table once P3b's fractional walls are in, because films thinner than a cell may be part of why big collars converge slowly.

Untested lever: every solve starts from zero today. A warm start from the previous step's pressure could cut the passes a collar needs without changing the rule's shape.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Warm start measured, 2026-10-01 (feat/fft-water, fft_water_warm_leftover_64 and _128): no rule change. Starting each solve from the last step's collar sources cuts the start residual |b| 3x at the splash peak and 8x settled (64), but the rest converges slower per pass. At the worst frame (splash, frames 50-90) equal passes give rms worst 6.6e-3 cold vs 5.9e-3 warm at 64 (24 passes) and 2.3e-2 vs 2.6e-2 at 128 (48 passes). Fewer passes lose outright: warm 16 at 64 leaves 8.0e-2, warm 40 at 128 leaves 0.11. Cause: 19% (64) and 42% (128) of each splash step's collar cells are new, so the carry has nothing for them. The 3n/8 rule stands, set from the worst frame.

title: GPU whitewater (spray, foam, bubbles) on the particle-frame seam, solver-agnostic
description: Peter, 2026-09-30: the GPU water must beat the FLIP Fluids engine it replaces, and whitewater is a large part of that look (reference exports: ~/Downloads/waterExportTestVert80Res.mp4, waterBoxTest64.mp4). Today whitewater is generated only by the vendored FLIP Fluids CPU engine (crates/manifold-fluids/native/flip_engine/diffuseparticlesimulation.cpp). SWASH (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md) plans none; GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md P6 plans whitewater atoms for MPM only; GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md P8 only routes FLIP-generated whitewater. Work: one design for GPU whitewater atoms that read the particle-frame seam (positions, velocities) plus the surface level set, porting FLIP Fluids diffuse model (wavecrest + turbulence + energy emission potentials, spray/foam/bubble classification, ballistic spray, advected foam/bubbles with buoyancy, lifetimes), so SWASH, MPM and FLIP feed the same generator. Gate: side by side with the FLIP Fluids engine on the same particles, Peter judges. Supersedes the MPM-only P6 whitewater plan.
notes:
Inventory measured 2026-09-30 (CPU FLIP, res 64 Dam Break, 343k particles; the full report is in the lead session transcript). Look ranking by pixels changed: renderer scattering 7%, volume path length 6.5%, subdivision 6%, mesh smoothing 4%, whitewater 1.3–2.3% (local, high contrast; almost all foam from wavecrest emission), absorption tint 1%. Bubbles ≤0.23%, spray ≤0.09%, turbulence emission inert at rate 175. Cost: whitewater 42–55 ms/tick, of which ~92% is the emitter scan over all liquid particles (serial classification ~12, turbulence ~11, inside emitters ~6, surface emitters ~4) plus a 10–14 ms curvature grid; the whitewater particles own lifecycle is ~1 ms. Plan: port the emitter scan (wavecrest + energy potentials, emission count, jitter, type split) to GPU atoms fed by the solver velocity field and liquid SDF; keep the lifecycle (advection, buoyancy/drag, collisions, lifetime, removal) as the unchanged FLIP C++ fed through shared memory (needs a MAC velocity grid: SWASH has one; the liquid SDF must come from the GPU). Drop turbulence emission unless recalibrated. Traps: emission rounds per emitter per substep, so amount depends on dt and needs recalibration; there is no bit-exact oracle, so oracles are statistical (counts over time, spatial histograms). Renderer optics, instancing and materials are already solver-agnostic.
Design 2026-09-30: docs/GPU_WHITEWATER_DESIGN.md on feat/gpu-whitewater, PROPOSED, six phases (P1 is the liquid seam P10 grid outputs). Awaiting approval before P1.

title: fft-water-fusion-param-capacity: fused buffer codegen cannot anchor a region on a param-sized output
description: SWASH P1 tracked debt (ADDING_PRIMITIVES BLOCKED path). The design names two fusable pairs in the FFT water pressure solve: cosine_spectrum -> cosine_poisson_divide (box solve) and cosine_spectrum -> cosine_surface_scale (surface helper). fusion_report on crates/manifold-renderer/tests/fixtures/presets/fft_water_pressure.json finds 0 regions: both pairs are refused. Root cause: cosine_spectrum reads its half-spectrum input by BufferGather and sizes its output from its lattice params (nodes_x*nodes_y*nodes_z), which is neither MinInputs nor MultipleOf, so build_region has no coincident count anchor and fails closed (FREEZE_COMPILER_MAP.md section 4, buffer-atom gates). Fix shape: extend FusedOutputCapacity/CapacityExpr with a param-product term (the product of named member params), emitted into the fused count anchor and the @fused_output_capacity dst sizing, the way BUG-orm4 (scene-mirror-blocked-output-multiplier-capacity) added MultipleOf. When it lands: retire fft_water_pressure_has_no_fused_region in primitives/swash_extent_tests.rs and add the mandatory fused-vs-unfused proof through fft_water_matches_reference. Cost at stake: two pairs per Krylov pass (one in the helper, one in the box solve), each one dispatch plus one full-array write and read.
notes:
SWASH P3 adds one more pair on the same root cause: cells_with_particles -> face_divergence (coincident water input; both sized by nodes_x*nodes_y*nodes_z). When the param-product anchor lands, also retire fft_water_step_has_no_fused_region (primitives/swash_extent_tests.rs) and add a frozen-vs-unfrozen run of the Dam Break step (swash_scene_tests.rs). Every other P3 edge ends at a gather input or crosses the pressure solve, so it is cut by design.
Same refusal hits node.face_sample_component (GPU whitewater, BUG-imy3): its output is param-sized, face_len of its nodes_x/y/z lattice and axis, so a coincident consumer never folds into it (asserted in primitives/face_grid_extent_tests.rs face_grid_fusion_in_host_graphs). When the param-product term lands, that assertion flips and the face component owes its own fused-vs-unfused proof. Note its size also depends on axis (one axis gets n+1), so the term needs a per-axis +1, not a bare product.
close_reason: FFT/SWASH-specific; GPU FLIP multigrid pressure solve landed on main (410c45347) and replaced the FFT solver (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN archived)

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Built on feat/fft-water (37b3b0c63), not landed. FusedOutputCapacity::ParamProduct plus CapacityExpr Param/Product (marker par()/prod()); the count is the output lattice clamped by non-bounding member lattices and coincident array externals, refused when a clamp bites at configured params. Declared on cosine_spectrum, cells_with_particles, face_divergence. SWASH fuses 5 cosine pairs per solve, 15 a frame at 64^3 (121 fewer dispatches). cells_with_particles -> face_divergence does not fuse: the water lattice fans out and buffer regions are single-output. Proofs: lattice_sized_region_counts_its_lattice, lattice_sized_region_clamps_by_its_members_and_coincident_reads, fft_water_frozen_graphs_cover_every_dispatch (CPU extent, every lattice), fft_water_frozen_solve_matches_unfrozen and fft_water_frozen_step_matches_unfrozen (bit for bit). Still open: node.face_sample_component needs a per-axis n+1 term (BUG-imy3, GPU whitewater).

title: Live matter GPU time above res ~100: cap the card, add a budget, or leave it
description: Separate from the buffer bug in BUG-bnp9 (GPU MPM water locks the Mac above resolution 64). With buffers fixed, cost still scales with res: GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md measured 128^3 at 30 Hz (4.2M points, 68 substeps a frame) at p95 1140 ms of GPU per frame; res 64 is 37 ms per tick at 513k points. Live runs up to MAX_LIVE_TICKS = 3 ticks per display frame, so res 128+ can submit multi-second command buffers that starve WindowServer and look like a freeze even with every buffer in bounds. The Resolution card goes to 512 and Grid Budget (default 8M nodes) admits up to res 193. Options: lower the card max for the live presets, add a GPU-time or point budget refusal like Grid Budget, or leave it as is and rely on the named budget error. Peter to choose.

title: storage_budget cleanup recognizes ~20% of a real target: .rcgu.o objects and hashed executables never deleted
description: Symptom: slot cap logs "removed 0 cache files from 94.4G over the 25G cap" again and again; slots sit at 17-94G. Measured on idle slot-4 (16.0G): only 3.2G matches _recognized_cargo_file (rlib/rmeta/.d/dylib). Kept: 3.65G deps/*.rcgu.o (split-debuginfo=unpacked per-codegen-unit objects, name-hash.cgu.id.rcgu.o, fails _HASHED_ARTIFACT single-extension rule), 4.5G hashed test/tool executables (kept by design), 4.3G build/*/out products (kept by design, arbitrary build-script data), fingerprint lib-<name> hash files. Fix shape: recognize deps/<name>-<hash>.<cgu>.<id>.rcgu.o and .fingerprint/<hashdir>/<kind>-<name>; hashed executables are a Peter call (rebuildable; live-process check already guards running ones). Cap should compare against recognized bytes, not du.

title: matter_to_particles runs every substep; gate it to the tick-start sort
description: Symptom: node.matter_to_particles converts the whole MatterPoint capacity to FluidParticle records on every substep (34x per frame at Stiffness 1), though its only reader, node.sort_particles_into_cells, runs once per tick (enabled = tick_start). description: At the preset Surface Particle Scale 2.2, the anisotropic kernels reach 0.68 cell (FLIP marker radius 0.31 cell), about 1.4 particle spacings, so the surface shows particle rows: ridges along the flow at res 32 (sharper at scale 4) and a crinkled pool at res 64. Shared scan: primitives/prefix_scan.rs. Fix shape: add a buffer variant of the boundary spec so these become generated boundary kernels. Filed by the GPU fluid surface build seat (Opus 5.5).

title: check-presets fails on Shatter scene-modifier preset
description: Symptom: check-presets reports 107 ok, 1 failed. assets/scene-modifier-presets/Shatter.json fails with "InvalidRecipe at shatter: enable Physics on the object before adding Shatter". Same on base 333cad8b8 and origin/main 582db1c76; the preset, scene_modifier_expand/compiler/shatter.rs and check_presets.rs are unchanged between them. Root cause unknown. Suspects: check-presets validates a scene-modifier preset standalone, with no host object carrying Physics, so the compiler precondition added with internal Box3D Shatter fires. Fix shape: have check-presets validate scene-modifier presets against a host object that satisfies declared prerequisites (or let the preset declare them), not relax the compiler check. Found by the GPU fluid surface build seat (Opus 5.5).

title: Slot ring lease holder dies with the shell; leased worker slots get stolen after 30 min
description: agent-worktree.py acquire records os.getppid() (the per-command zsh) as holder_pid, so every agent-held lease looks dead within seconds and becomes stealable after DEAD_HOLDER_GRACE_H (0.5 h). Symptom 2026-09-29: two worker slots (slot-2, slot-0) were checked out from under running Opus workers by another session acquire; no work lost only because workers had just pushed. Root cause: holder_pid default; workers never refresh lease mtime. Fix shape: default holder_pid to the long-lived claude process (walk up from getppid to the first process named claude) or refresh lease mtime on every git write in the worktree via the bash hook; and make acquire refuse a slot whose working tree is dirty regardless of lease age.

title: math, scale_offset_value and the three switch nodes: required input shadows a param so the param can never be the fallback
description: Found during the renderer test prune (2026-09-29) while building the port-shadow registry sweep. Symptom: node.math, node.scale_offset_value and the three switch nodes declare an input as required that shadows a param; a shadowed param is meant to be the fallback when the input is unwired, but a required input can never be unwired, so the param is dead. Root cause: primitive! declarations mark the input required. Fix shape: make those inputs optional so the param fallback works, or drop the param; then the sweep rule in primitives/mod.rs can lose its named exemption list. Root cause unknown; suspects: touched-crate detection reads the wrong diff base after merging origin/main into the branch (branch already contained main), or the skip path lacks a reason line. Fix shape: gate prints why each step was skipped, and touched-crate detection uses merge-base with origin/main. Related: BUG-e29g (test suite audit campaign).

title: Gatekeeper first-run scan starves cargo builds: find why checks degrade 0.4s to 25s, cut fresh-binary count
description: macOS Gatekeeper first-run scan (syspolicyd + XprotectService) serializes every freshly built binary: build scripts, nextest test binaries, hello-world alike. Normal cost 0.4s/file; on 2026-09-29 evening it degraded to ~25s/file with 3 cargo sessions building fresh worktrees (565 build-script scans + ~50 test binaries in 70 min), so cargo run --release sat at "manifold-renderer(build)" for minutes with the build script parked at _dyld_start. Same starvation hit the nightly trunk_health run 05:00-07:00 (90s medians). Diagnostic signature: process 0% CPU, ~80KB RSS, sample shows only _dyld_start. Fix: add Terminal (and the Codex app) to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Tools so binaries launched from them skip assessment; document in docs/DEVELOPMENT_REFERENCE.md and guide_debugging_doctrine memory. Peter rebooted to clear it.
notes:
2026-09-29 after a machine restart: syspolicyd at 56-73% CPU doing per-binary notarization lookups plus XProtect scans; fresh build scripts in slot-9, slot-1 and main sat in _dyld_start at 0% CPU for 5-7 min, and a scratchpad python script waited ~3 min. The queue drains slowly; kill-and-retry does not help because the relinked binary re-enters the queue.

2026-09-30: the terminal here is Ghostty, not Terminal.app, so the Developer Tools entry to add is Ghostty (plus the Codex app). spctl developer-mode enable-terminal only adds Terminal.app, so it does not cover this setup. Unverified: whether a tmux server started from Ghostty inherits the exemption, and whether launchd-started nightly jobs can be covered at all.

2026-09-30 Peter: no Developer Tools exemption, not for Ghostty and not for a cargo-only launcher app. Fix shape is now (1) find the root cause of the 60x slowdown (watch syspolicyd logs during a fresh worktree build: network notarization lookups? cold cache after reboot? concurrency?), and (2) cut how many never-seen binaries a build makes: fold 52 test binaries into a few, and check whether byte-identical rebuilds (sccache across slots) skip the rescan.

2026-09-30: slot acquire already picks the warmest slot, but enforce_target_cap wipes a slot's whole cache once it passes 25G, which turns the next build into ~500 fresh build scripts. The 25G cap may be what makes cold builds common. Check before designing a cold-build queue.

2026-09-30 (later): the 25G-cap-forces-cold-builds theory is wrong. The cap almost never deletes anything (see the storage_budget recognition bead). Cold builds last night came from fresh slots instead (slot-3, slot-9 show cold).

title: AddAudioModCommand undo loses the replaced modulation
description: Static finding during the 2026-09-29 audio routing review. In crates/manifold-editing/src/commands/audio_mod.rs, AddAudioModCommand::execute removes any existing modulation with the same param_id and inserts the new one. Its undo only removes the new modulation; it never restores the previous value. This violates the replacement behavior explicitly supported by the command. Current UI callers generally choose Add only when their local snapshot has no modulation, so an ordinary native UI reproduction has not been established; a stale snapshot reaching newer content state is a possible trigger, not a verified reproduction. Fix shape: preserve the replaced modulation and its position for undo, respecting local-snapshot execution followed by content execution. Validate replacement, normal add, repeated undo/redo, and two-project execution. No changes made during the routing workstream.

title: git -C <dir> reset --hard runs unprompted via the Bash(git -C *) allow rule
description: Symptom: PERMISSION_BOUNDARY.md section 4b (full-list audit) accepts Bash(git -C *) on the claim that preToolUseBash.py still prompts reset/clean/rebase/force. The hook only leaves those unapproved; for a single command it returns no verdict, and the harness then matches the static rule git -C *, so `git -C <dir> reset --hard` (or clean -fdx) runs with no prompt. Force-push is covered by destructive_outward_guard; reset/clean/rebase/gc/filter-branch are not. Fix shape: add a destructive-git ASK guard next to destructive_outward_guard (runs before allow, in every mode) for reset --hard, clean -f*, rebase, gc --prune, filter-branch, checkout -- . / restore on dirty trees as needed; or narrow the git -C rule. Needs the section 4 review.

title: Clip move and paste only check video vs generator, so clips land on audio, group and DMX layers
description: Symptom (derived from code, not reproduced live): dragging a clip up or down across layers, or pasting a copied region, can put a video clip on an audio, group or DMX layer, an audio clip on a video layer (move path), or a DMX clip on a video layer. Root cause: the type rule is the Unity-era two-type check, written when only Video and Generator existed. Move drag (manifold-ui interaction_overlay.rs ~3094, host.layer_is_generator which is Generator-only, editing_host.rs:192) compares src_is_gen vs dst_is_gen only. paste_clips (manifold-editing service.rs ~526-541) compares is_generator vs layer==Generator plus a one-way audio guard; copy marks a DMX-layer clip as is_generator=false, and paste never checks Group (create_clip_at_position does). No downstream guard in commands/clip.rs. Also: PasteResult.skipped_count is never read, so skipped clips vanish silently. Fix shape: one core rule, LayerType::accepts(clip kind) (or clip-kind enum from the source layer type) used by move drag, paste, duplicate and create; record the source LayerType in ClipboardEntry instead of two bools; toast when paste skips clips. Test: move/paste a video clip onto Audio, Group, Dmx is refused; DMX clip onto Video refused.
close_reason: fixed in the fix/timeline-edge-cases landing: LayerType::accepts_clips_from is the one rule for move drag and paste (generator and DMX share a kind, groups hold none); paste skips report through a toast; DMX clips trim like generator clips. Test: layers_only_accept_clips_of_their_own_kind, paste_video_clip_onto_audio_group_or_dmx_layer_is_skipped

title: Region selection can start before beat 0, shifting copy/paste and duplicate right
description: Symptom: drag a region selection starting at the timeline left edge and pulling past it (or into the layer header area) at scroll 0; copy+paste or Cmd+D of that region lands clips late by the amount the region hangs before beat 0. Root cause: region drag never clamps to beat 0. begin_region_drag/update_region_drag (manifold-ui interaction_overlay.rs ~3522-3574) use viewport.pixel_to_beat (panels/viewport/coordinate.rs:46, no floor) and snap_to_grid (no floor), so set_region accepts start_beat < 0. Downstream: EditingService::copy_clips uses region.start_beat as origin, so a clip at beat 0 gets beat_offset = 0 - start (e.g. +1); duplicate_clips offsets by region.duration_beats() which includes the negative part (region -1..8 duplicates to beat 9, not 8). Shift-click region extension (interaction_overlay.rs ~79) takes the same unclamped beat. Fix shape: clamp at the single authority UIState::set_region (start/end .max(Beats::ZERO)) so every producer is covered; add a test: region -1..8 over a clip at 0, copy then paste at 0 lands at 0, duplicate lands at 8. Not reproduced live; derived from code.
close_reason: fixed in the fix/timeline-edge-cases landing: UIState::set_region floors both ends at beat 0, so copy/paste and duplicate offsets start at the real region. Test: region_dragged_past_the_left_edge_starts_at_beat_zero

title: Complete coupled input-take identity and paired cache playback
description:
P9 remains in progress in slot-9. Completed locally: bounded resolved-input journal/replay; take v5 project timing and authored graph provenance; paired cache v10 with explicit legacy readers; reproducible seed/source identity; portable collected assets; authenticated project-time cache lookup with nonzero/pre-roll origins, speed changes, holds and backward seeks. Physics history reuses immutable copy-on-write project tempo snapshots and the canonical f64 TempoMapConverter, samples exact tempo boundaries, preserves held tempo through edits/rebuilds, and retains exact external host beat stamps. Generator/effect/manual impulse hosts supply the same project map.

Bound cache preflight now validates the completed recorded clock against current project tempo on the native worker, including inserted or removed tempo changes between samples and clipped failed prefixes. Future-only edits remain compatible. Playback map edits cancel stale replies and revalidate; live edits preserve the native owner. Legacy unproven timing is rejected when current-project validation is requested. Recording rejects changes in clock-provenance presence.

Generator authored graph identity now includes fluid/coupled rigid ancestry, resolved collider masks, event-only field ancestry, and relevant binding/reshape semantics. Layout, unrelated appearance and cache controls are excluded. Bound cache preflight validates the last committed source identity. Held source-only edits commit without native ticks; stale replies cannot acknowledge newer edits. Source errors survive reset/rebuild, block Record/Playback, and leave Live available. Undo reopens a compatible cache.

Per-instance source validation now uses the existing PresetInstance on generator render, warmup, thumbnail and manual impulse hosts. It hashes relevant manual bases, semantic specs and existing driver/envelope/audio/automation/Ableton authored configurations, excluding effective values, runtime state and sampled bases owned by enabled automation/Ableton. Compatible refresh/rebuild preserves the host digest; preparation-error recovery waits for a fresh host observation. No parallel modulation model.

Effect-chain source validation now shares the per-EffectSlot state used by generators. Card-local node maps handle duplicate stable IDs and segment prefixes; source errors remain local. Build/run install current authored graph and PresetInstance controls, refresh on graph edits, and reinstall identities after native-node harvest. A bounded production Metal chain proof records/reloads two empty domains and checks isolated base/graph edits, undo and rebuild with changed controls. Existing generator-only scene-modifier admission is unchanged.

Prepared-geometry preflight now compares current role meshes and all rigid/prototype hulls against the authenticated take setup by content, including membership, scale, shape, fragment parents and coupling participation. Current sampled poses/controls are excluded. Validation is on the owning worker at cache open; changed or missing geometry rejects before frame publication, fresh allocations and moved take directories remain compatible, and unbound legacy caches cannot validate scene assets. No per-frame filesystem reads or geometry scans were added. The shared glTF decoded-mesh cache now hashes the primary file and all buffers resolved by the canonical parser, and flattens the same retained snapshot on a miss. Missing or truncated dependencies reject before cache lookup; relocated identical assets retain reuse. Mesh-only decode does not decode unused images.

Remaining P9: current-source identity across project-wide audio-send, macro/MIDI and clip/event dependencies, and asset-path normalization and full external-source coverage (including animation contents and same-path source replacement); active-take behaviour for discontinuous tempo edits. Keep arbitrary-scene guards until these are complete. P5/P7 source/audio/effect route acceptance still needs its final audit. P10 still needs higher-quality replay/output settings distinct from captured inputs, Record finalization that drains timing/source metadata, initial tick-zero liquid surface, and Bake/quality/export UI. Sustained rendered coupled acceptance and P11 fields remain open. Existing contract: docs/FLUID_ENGINE_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md. No landing or public push authorized.


Applied host string selectors now enter card-scoped take identity after existing default/override handling, including retained omitted values and rebuild reobservation. Unrelated appearance/cache inputs are excluded; raw paths remain strict. Collection now carries glTF external buffers/images with the primary model. Complete collected-project take acceptance remains open.
acceptance_criteria: Record, reload and replay resolved scene roles, fields, event assignments and paired poses without live audio; explicit failures for corrupt/incomplete/mismatched input; dependency changes invalidate cache while materials do not; complete source identity precedes user-facing arbitrary-scene cache playback. P10 bake/export UI remains separate planned work.

Reviewed fixture changes keep declared bounds valid and flatten retained buffers only after backing files are changed/deleted. title: Implement two-way FLIP and Box3D coupling with a numerical feasibility gate
description:
Include two-way FLIP/Box3D interaction in the active slot-9 workstream through manifold-physics, existing collision proxies and native solvers. No landing or public push is authorized.

Verified foundations: mass-aware native pressure PCG/preconditioning (4b36ff307), actual mesh boundary interpolation/transpose (f8a835c2c), generic BodyDynamics/BodyImpulse API and prescribed viscous stress capture (6014327d4). Delayed viscous feedback was rejected by an eight-case energy test (58bd9d506), especially for light bodies/high viscosity.

Checkpoint 9d5b02dab adds joint viscosity, which extends the same native PCG with normalized body velocity changes, full world inertia, shared strain cross terms and the exact body diagonal. The ordinary fluid matrix remains native. A two-body independent physical-mass oracle gives solution error 2.48e-7 and reaction/response error 5.74e-7, zero measured symmetry/diagonal mismatch, and passive energy ratio 0.780411. Thirty-three frozen-geometry native cases cover translation/rotation, density ratios 0.1/1/10, viscosity 1/10 m2/s, dt 1/60 and 1/120, and a varying boundary constraint derivative. Maximum energy ratio is 0.949469, body response mismatch 6.42e-6 and transpose mismatch 5.36e-14. Fixed mobility exactly preserves the original solve. Eight cases put a planar free surface through or just above a light translating/rotating body; their maximum energy ratio is 0.168593 using independently calculated staggered liquid volume. Failed, invalid and empty captures are checked; the coupled path rejects the ordinary loose iteration-limit fallback. Twelve coupling tests and two ordinary native regressions pass.

Production native integration now passes five short CPU tests using real rotated Box3D hulls. Owner-driven FLIP substeps accept full body snapshots, use physical density and combined viscosity/pressure, and expose linear/angular impulses plus solved changes. Across three frames at density ratios 0.1/1/10 and kinematic viscosity 0/1, immediate Box3D response mismatch is at most 1.77e-7 (limit 5e-5). Empty/disabled recipients, prescribed density scaling, invalid tensors, stale output, pending-offer mutation and abandonment are covered. Box3D advances geometry after each reaction; this is not sustained moving/floating acceptance.

Remaining: qualify sustained moving geometry/advection, floating equilibrium and contact alignment; connect existing app owners at shared substeps and coherent accepted poses; author physical density through existing params; verify stale/duplicate epoch handling and replay/export. Prepared native storage currently uses conservative O(grid faces x bound bodies) capacities and requires memory/cost qualification before dense multi-body production use. No user tuning knobs or silent degradation.

P8b in docs/FLUID_ENGINE_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md remains authoritative. Reuse existing native PCG. A substantial underlying solver replacement requires the scope discussion Peter requested. No heuristic buoyancy/drag, arbitrary damping/caps or altered authored mass to conceal instability.
acceptance_criteria: P8b numerical gates establish physical reaction units, buoyancy, angular exchange, viscous response and stable coherent stepping; otherwise record evidence for the requested separate-solver scope discussion. Reuse existing physics ownership, proxies, controls and take/cache infrastructure.

Cause indicated by source and observed geometry: masks in these recipes use mesh_spatial_mask sample_mode=1, assigning one strength to each source triangle. fragment_cuts remaps those constant triangle weights, and morph_mesh blends each triangle by a different amount, tearing neighbouring faces through the feather. Exact planar band/cell cutting does not remove these later discontinuities. MaskedPeel enables the mask by default. SurfacePeel, VortexFragments, OrderedRecon and OrderedReconHit have the same optional mask path; SurfacePeelHit does not have a mask. Directional stagger in OrderedRecon/Hit also uses per-face envelope weights and needs a coherence check as part of the eventual correction.

No production fix applied during this diagnostic check. Choose continuous vertex fields versus fragment-coherent weights deliberately; preserve user-authored sampling modes, saved snapshots, live bindings and fusion, and update the current mathematical-field contract if semantics change. Do not simply raise MSAA: raster AA is already working and cannot mend separated triangles. Add a regression for geometry continuity through a nonzero feather, not just nonempty render or fractional alpha.

Evidence currently /tmp/manifold-cut-audit/MaskedPeel.png and sibling raw RGBA16F files. Audit harness in codex/fragment-cut-audit slot-5; preservation details follow after optimized-renderer validation.

V1 defaults threshold=.65/sensitivity=.85; current V1 additionally applies the authored area/aspect/size filter. V2 brightness preparation is CPU-mirrored Rec.709 luma and separable radius-1 denoise at longest dimension 320. Both decoded RGB and sRGB-linearized RGB were checked because this bypasses the app's video colour path. Results are detector probes, NOT a historical app playback comparison, tracking smoothness proof, or GPU mask equivalence proof. Original V1 analysis dimensions are normalized to the same dimensions for this comparison. Colour/motion variants, actual bundled generators, playback latency, full HUD, group wet/dry and identity continuity were not exercised. Initial attempt mixing bundled/current and Homebrew/old libraries failed with duplicate OpenMP before results; isolated builds resolved it without bypassing runtime protection.

Measured: liquid old V1 had 3-7 detections and zero empty frames in decoded RGB; current V1 had 0-5 and 13/50 empty. Linearized check preserved direction: old 3-6/zero empty; current 0-5/10 empty. This supports a detection regression candidate, not universal old-version superiority. People: old decoded RGB empty in all 50, linearized one region each; current empty 17/50 decoded or 14/50 linearized. V2 brightness selected 1-2 broad regions; decoded-RGB contact sheets show sky coverage, not people. TV: old V1 and V2 both detected two regions throughout both input encodings; current output was more variable, strongly encoding-dependent. Controlled bright rectangle: all detect except the deliberate gap. Dark rectangle on white: both V1s detect; V2 brightness returns zero because the connected white background exceeds max area. Post-detection mask Invert cannot turn this into detecting the dark shape.

Static findings: current V1 equalizes contrast (76d6a4867) and filters after an eight-result native cap; original filters >50% boxes before capping, current preset rejects >30% (bea52925b). Current V1 preset grace=1 graph execution; old held 3 detection cycles. V2 boxes only include observed tracks; retention does not visually hold them. region_mask_body.wgsl uses observed labels, not smoothed boxes: Smoothing cannot stabilize silhouette boundaries. Largest reselects the currently greatest measured AREA on each publication; it is not a persistent chosen target. Only All/Largest are exposed. Existing overlay-resolution debt remains BUG-nn13.

Recommended bounded implementation sequence: (1) reproduce the liquid loss in the actual app and isolate contrast normalization versus grouping/filter changes; recover useful V1-style edge/contrast detection while retaining V2 reusable label/mask plumbing. Do not blindly revert all changes. (2) Specify common visible selection semantics, dark/bright/edge source behavior and detection preview. (3) Add explicit shape-versus-box mask semantics, temporal loss behavior and persistent selected-region behavior; don't claim box smoothing solves masks or freeze stale silhouettes without an agreed policy. (4) Verify tracking and group coverage together on the supplied clips, plus crossing/merging and dropout controls. Full tracker replacement is not justified by this initial evidence.

title: Dynamic to Fixed or Animated transitions retain native bullet flag and miss collisions
description: Review at 7c0352258 of ed326c019: physics.rs clears native bullet state only when entering Dynamic (445-447); configure_fast_bodies clears only the Rust cache for non-Dynamic bodies. title: UI headless PNG captures omit linear-to-sRGB output conversion
description:
Source-confirmed UI capture boundary mismatch, investigated 2026-09-22. ui_snapshot/render.rs::save_bgra_png (line 954) takes linear BGRA8 UI readback, swaps B/R, and writes a PNG without linear-to-sRGB display encoding. Real windows tag the same linear values as ExtendedLinearSRGB for macOS colour conversion. frame/present.rs::bug060_dump_png and manifold-renderer/tests/ui_color_swatches.rs also save linear UNORM bytes without display encoding. This explains a systematic darkening mechanism in UI capture tools; no paired live/headless render was performed this session.

Future fix: share an explicit display-ready PNG encoder with correct RGB transfer, alpha handling and sRGB metadata. Audit callers by actual source encoding to avoid double encoding; do not apply HDR scene tonemapping to ordinary UI indiscriminately. Validate known swatches numerically and one paired live/headless scene. This is separate from the main window 8-bit linear precision/HDR clipping issue.

title: Main-window preview loses HDR and dark precision in linear 8-bit presentation
description:
Investigation 2026-09-22 of current source, prompted by Peter asking about UI/headless colour and HDR. No application changes or live visual comparison performed.

Main workspace and graph-editor presentation use linear Bgra8Unorm, despite ExtendedLinearSRGB + EDR configuration. Workspace content arrives through an Rgba16Float preview bridge, then ui_frame::composite_main_ui_base draws it through a textureSample-only blit into Bgra8Unorm ui_offscreen; present.rs copies that to a Bgra8Unorm drawable. Values above 1 cannot survive that storage. Dark values are also quantized on a linear 8-bit grid. This is not a limitation on all internal rendering textures or the separate output window, which uses Rgba16Float end to end at presentation.

Evidence: app.rs surface at 2089, sample-only shader/pipeline at 2138-2166, resize_ui_offscreen at 3256; ui_frame.rs preview draw at 297; content_pipeline.rs preview pipeline at 1316-1345, direct output present at 3081; app_lifecycle.rs output surface at 1326 and graph editor at 1434. manifold-gpu/metal/surface.rs sets the requested pixel format verbatim; configure_edr changes colour space/EDR flags, not pixel format.

History: 310fbc05f migrated UI caches to Bgra8Unorm. dce2f7553 (2026-03-31) replaced the main window Rgba16Float-preferred surface with hardcoded Bgra8Unorm, retaining EDR setup. No downgrade rationale found in these commits. Historical intent is evidenced, historical runtime success is not proven.

Related presentation concern to resolve within design: content_pipeline has one edr_headroom and one post-tonemap final_output shared by preview/output. app.rs::update_edr_headroom can send changes from either display; a surface-format-only fix does not establish correct independent mapping on mixed SDR/HDR displays.

Attempted bounded scratch Swift/Metal numerical probe: first compilation failed due to overlapping Swift buffer access; corrected version compiled but could not obtain a Metal device in the sandbox. Stopped after two failures. No GPU numeric or live visual result claimed. Apple documents BGRA8Unorm as normalized 8-bit and requires an above-1-capable format such as RGBA16Float for linear EDR.

Acceptance for future fix: explicit window presentation contract; preserve above-white and dark-ramp values through main preview on supported HDR hardware; keep ordinary UI brightness stable; map SDR and HDR displays intentionally; verify actual live output and focused GPU proof before claiming visual parity. Do not blanket-convert every internal texture.

App uses SceneLinear through master FX with independent workspace/output/graph mapping and explicit SDR video/recording conversion. Float UI capture encodes sRGB before 8-bit quantization and writes PNG metadata. Focused clippy with UI features passed; six production GPU proofs plus three policy tests passed; all12 capture/native CPU tests passed; one inspector PNG rendered and inspected. Native launcher blocked by repository execution-budget hook after exact permit; no launch occurred. Hardware follow-up BUG-qdn7 tracks native window and external display acceptance. comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Additional source audit after Peter linked this to automatic best-display configuration: edr_surface.rs::query_screen_headroom prefers maximumPotentialExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue over maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue. Potential capability and currently available headroom are different; Apple directs adaptive tone mapping to current available headroom. app.rs sends UpdateEdrHeadroom from either window into content_pipeline.edr_headroom, and one post-tonemap final_output feeds both destinations. Changes therefore overwrite one shared target rather than independently adapting each window. ClearOutputSurface only detaches the surface and does not itself restore primary-window headroom. These are source findings, not live mixed-display reproductions. Fix design should cover independent destination mapping, current-vs-potential capability, output close/open and display/brightness changes, stable SDR UI white, and an HDR-capable main preview target. Merely switching BGRA8 to RGBA16Float is insufficient for the full automatic-display contract. Apple reference: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/performing-your-own-tone-mapping and WWDC22 Explore EDR on iOS (includes NSScreen guidance).

title: Physics scene authoring: reconcile shared solver bodies on object duplication and removal
description: PhysicsSolids uses root-scope SceneObject nodes fed by shared node.physics_world pose_N outputs. Existing DuplicateSceneObjectCommand clones only the producer node/group without incoming wires; RemoveSceneObjectCommand removes only the object producer, leaving shared solver body descriptions connected. Extend scene authoring ownership for physics body/pose pairs before treating this demo as a general physics scene editor; support undo/redo and nested scopes without cloning the shared world. Current scope is six-body playback plus property controls.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate creates a distinct hull in the same world; remove disconnects the corresponding body and leaves no dangling wires or invisible collider; undo/redo and scene exposure ownership roundtrip are covered.
notes:

title: Coincident optional array pre-reads unguarded — short wired weights reads OOB (standalone + fused)
description: Coincident array input pre-reads are eager and unguarded: standalone.rs:673 (let e_<port> = buf_<port>[idx];) and fused_buffer.rs:558 (let e_<e> = src_<e>[idx];) read at every dispatched idx. For OPTIONAL inputs (the deformer family weights planes) dispatch is bounded by required inputs only — a wired-but-short weights buffer (weights_len < count, which run() explicitly tolerates with a warning) reads out of bounds where the body gate idx < weights_len would have discarded the value. Metal storage OOB is the AGX page-fault/hang class (BUG-84fv (gpu hang hard lockup) history). Pre-existing for most of the optional-weights family (they declared Coincident all along); 7c9b76e6b extended it to mesh_spatial_mask (gather to coincident). Unwired is safe: standalone binds the count-sized src as dummy, fused threads a zero literal. Fix shape: clamp optional coincident pre-reads — select(zero, buf[min(idx, len-1)], len > 0) — gated on the port being optional so required-input kernels keep byte-identical WGSL. Add a GPU proof wiring a deliberately short weights plane.

title: Unwired frame-time input that is also a declared param breaks fused derived-uniform marker accounting (BUG-e3p6.4 follow-up)
description: When a frame_time_input is ALSO a declared param (node.ripple_mesh time), the fused buffer codegen emits n0_time in the Params struct at its PARAM position (fused_buffer.rs skips re-emitting it in the derived block to avoid a duplicate field), but emit_derived_uniform_markers computes the marker word count from effective_derived = [weights_len, time] — so the marker claims 2 words starting at n0_weights_len, covering n0_weights_len + n1_weights_len, and NOTHING refreshes n0_time (the generic pack writes the seeded param default 0). Symptom: fused ripple with unwired time renders the undisplaced mesh (proven while authoring rt_dynamic_fusion: fused y == input y). The rt_dynamic_fusion proof wires time from a value node (the documented beat-ramp pattern) to stay clear. Fix shape: make the marker/struct accounting agree — either emit frame-time params only in the derived block, or make the marker cover the actual contiguous emitted fields and have the generic pack apply the frame-clock fallback for unwired frame-time param fields.
notes: 2026-09-17 k3 review note: corner is PRE-EXISTING (noise_displace/glitch_jitter had [time]-only recomputes against 2-word [weights_len, time] blocks before 7c9b76e6b — has_recompute was already true, so they could already fuse into it). 7c9b76e6b did not widen exposure; their array_ports are empty so no mapping is emitted. Fix remains the marker/struct accounting agreement.

title: Scene modifier angular controls do not consistently support seamless continuous animation

Follow-up audit during modifier consolidation: the discontinuity is in the shared transform_mesh_patches primitive, not the card or LFO. Both local curl and global orbit multiply angle by enabled times a spatial sine field. Full-turn loops cannot preserve that exact angle-to-weight interpretation. The existing Phase parameter already moves the influence field periodically with Orbit/Curl held as deformation amounts. A separate full-turn phase for orbit/spin is a contained extension of this primitive plus recipe controls and GPU/native endpoint proofs; it does not require a new animation engine, Math View work, or broad rewrite. Soft influence and enabled semantics must be decided explicitly; do not silently change saved weighted angles or merely mark them wraps=true. No weighted-angle behavior changed by consolidation.

Fresh cards use 0 to 360 degrees; saved stock Recon half-turn ranges expand to a full turn, while values/defaults/IDs/bindings and custom calibrated ranges are retained. Feature-enabled app clippy passed. Required landing and GPU gate still running. Earlier separate-control proposal is superseded; Math View remains parked.

The real holes: (1) Bpm is serde-transparent with a pub field — project-file load bypasses the clamp entirely (bpm 0.0 in JSON -> 60/0 = inf in settings.seconds_per_beat); (2) direct Bpm(x) construction bypasses; (3) audio_warp.rs:112/audio_mixdown.rs:220 raw 60.0/clip_bpm guard >0.0 but not the upper bound. Fix shape: load-time validation of Bpm fields in the V1/V2 deserial path (not a shared-helper refactor), replace the two raw audio sites with the converter, keep the converter clamp as defense-in-depth. Do NOT start by routing everything through one helper — the boundary is construction, not the division.
close_reason: Landed: Deserialize clamps to 20-300 (regression test), all spb sites route through TempoMapConverter, dead helpers deleted. Gate green, verdict stamped.

title: RT denoiser passes overwrite shared parameter buffers before submission
description: Read-only audit on 2026-09-09 found atrous_pass and atrous_post_pass upload parameters into a single CPU-mapped buffer, then bind it with setBuffer. render_scene loops over different step values using that same buffer without a submit/completion boundary inside the loop. Thus earlier encoded dispatches do not retain their intended parameter values. Seen in slot-5 raytrace.rs atrous_pass (~7525), atrous_post_pass (~7655), render_scene.rs ATROUS_ITERATIONS loop (~6492) and denoise_iterations loop (~6740); generic encoder.rs Buffer binding uses setBuffer, not an inline snapshot. Static correctness defect; no runtime reproduction performed. Downstream of the reported trace hangs and not established as their cause. Fix with existing inline-byte binding infrastructure or per-dispatch immutable parameter storage, preserving requested step values.
acceptance_criteria: Each denoiser dispatch retains its own step/settings until completion; focused proof distinguishes steps rather than only checking output finiteness. Do not claim this fixes Corrosion trace hangs without causal evidence.
notes: Prepared fix in slot-7 branch codex/rt-readiness-denoiser-landing: both atrous passes use existing inline-byte parameter snapshots. Static review only; Peter explicitly deferred GPU tests, heavy compilation and landing before meeting. Meaningful multi-pass regression proof and landing checks remain pending. Not claimed as a fix for export hangs.
close_reason: Fixed with per-dispatch inline-byte snapshots for both atrous APIs. GPU regression verifies batched distinct steps against individually submitted references; clippy, changed-crate tests and full GPU-proofs landing gate passed. Landed via codex/rt-readiness-denoiser-landing. Not established as the cause of the earlier export hangs.

title: scene-loop-seam-cut-under-live-param-modulation
description: Scene Loop seam cuts when card params are modulated by non-phase sources. Math: wrap purity compares the phase-0 frame against the phase-1 frame one loop apart; any scene-visible param whose value differs across that boundary produces a hard cut. One-shot live rides cost exactly one cut then settle (both sides agree after the wrap); continuous beat-driven modulation (LFO/envelope on Jitter, Spacing, etc.) cuts EVERY wrap — the D8 aperiodic-driver class. Built-in movement controls (sway/look/zoom/flow) are phase-periodic with integer cycles so they never cut. Product gap: nothing warns when a non-phase modulation binds to a loop row. Options: (a) binding-time warning, (b) phase-periodic envelope support for loop rows, (c) document as performer knowledge. Raised by Peter 2026-09-06 while diagnosing Stone Effects wrap hitches (see also scene-loop-far-edge-hole-fog-default and BUG-jvlq).

A fused reflect would dispatch input-capacity threads and leave the mirrored half of the output buffer unwritten (garbage InstanceTransforms on screen, show-breaking). title: reflect-array fusion blocked: fused buffer codegen cannot express non-coincident output capacity

title: 3d-scene-feedback-and-scene-space-mirror
description:
Extension direction from Peter 2026-09-05 on top of Scene Loop: "3D scene stylised feedback... 3D scene mirrors, twists, pulses, explosions, steps."

Survey: SCENE_FX_DESIGN shipped P0-P4 2026-08-22 — mesh deformers (bend/twist/taper/morph/shatter/ripple/melt/voxelize/noise_displace/glitch_jitter), the per-object modifier rack in the scene panel, and Skin Video (a layer output bound into another layer scene graph as a texture). Twist/explosion/step aesthetics are therefore one rack-add away on looped scenes.

Genuinely new:
1. Closed-loop 3D feedback — the scene previous-frame render re-bound into the same scene (trails/echoes in world space). render_scene is Terminal so its output is not consumable. Two-layer workaround exists today (layer A renders the scene, layer B skins A output onto the same model via Skin Video = world-space video feedback with one extra frame of latency). The real version needs render_scene output exposed as a texture plus one-frame feedback loop handling (SCENE_FX D5 already allows previous-frame reads for layer skins).
2. True scene-space planar mirror — fold_mesh mirrors one mesh across a plane; a mirrored-room reflection (reflect the whole scene, second render pass) does not exist.

Placement decision (Peter, 2026-09-05): deformers stay in the per-object rack (Scene Setup, object-level Add Modifier) — they are object properties, and on a looped scene a deformer on the object already hits every copy via scene_array instancing; duplicating them as clip-level modifier cards would create a second home for the same control. Scene Mirror and Scene Feedback are genuinely scene-wide: new modifier kinds in the + Add Modifier menu (today: Scene Loop, Scene Fog) — each is a descriptor + plan builder + trace signature, zero new UI.

Note: deformer animation on a looping camera must stay phase-driven (beat_ramp) or the visual loop seams even when the camera path wraps pure (INV-3).

description: Scene Loop card exposes no camera framing controls. When the modifier is applied, the camera path is base_camera → camera_switch → camera_lens → render; modifier ON selects node.loop_camera, which owns position AND near/far/fov_y (plan builder derives near=extent/200, far=cell×count+extent at apply — SCENE_LOOP_DESIGN D6 — but nothing surfaces them). The Scene Loop card curates only motion rows (spacing/lateral/height/flow/stride/sway/look sway/zoom pulse), so clipping plane, FOV, home, and rotation offset are only reachable via "edit in graph" on the loop_camera node. Lens block (focus/f-stop/shutter/exposure) works either way — camera_lens sits after the switch. Requested by Peter 2026-09-05 ("would be nice to be able to move the camera around with this scene modifier still" + xyz/rotation offsets on top of the motion). Fix shape: curated Near/Far/FOV/Home + offset params on node.loop_camera (position offsets are wrap-safe constants — INV-3 only constrains time-varying terms to be phase-driven, SCENE_LOOP_DESIGN D8; static xyz/rot offsets are pure constants and safe). Note lateral/height/home already cover the cross-section + travel-axis start, so the genuinely new surface is a rotation offset (roll/pitch/yaw applied after look-at basis construction) plus possibly a world-space xyz offset; sway/look-sway already provide the animated variant as phase functions. Consider seeding near/far/fov from the base camera at apply instead of scene-bounds constants.

title: jitter-seam-visual-seamlessness-call
description: SCENE_MODIFIER_FRAMEWORK P4 escalation, Peter call: per-instance jitter makes the loop seam swap the nearest copy orientation — position-continuous and deterministic, exact-seam pixel gate stays 0, but the near-seam (phase 0.99999) pixel diff measures 113 with jitter live vs 0 without. A constant-per-index hash (the only way to zero the near-seam) is no jitter at all. Options if the seam ever reads visibly with jitter live: (a) accept — the wrap is beat-locked and the swap lands exactly on the downbeat, arguably musical; (b) window the jitter amount by sin(pi*phase) so copies are identical at the seam and maximally varied mid-loop (loses the static-corridor feel, adds a breathing quality); (c) key jitter on (idx mod window) so the seam sees identical orientations at the cost of a periodic corridor. The P4 lane did NOT build any of these. Deferred until Peter sees it live on the sakura.

title: modifier-coupled-rows-bypassed-by-modulation-writes
description: SCENE_MODIFIER_FRAMEWORK P4: coupled rows (Stride→scene_array.count, Spacing→cells+home) resolve their coupling only on the card write paths (scrub Begin/Move/Commit + SceneSetupParamChanged). A performer driving Stride via OSC/Ableton/MIDI/macro mapping writes only the primary binding — scene_array.count desyncs until the next card drag, so the instance array no longer covers the strided travel (camera flies past the last copy). Live behavior, not theoretical: every modifier row exposes E/D/ABL/A chrome. Fix shapes (pick at fix time): (a) binding-write hook — ChangeGraphParamCommand consults the kind coupled_writes decl and expands to the secondary writes in one undo unit (the app-side resolution moves into the command, all write paths inherit); (b) an explicit copies-follow-stride rule in scene_array (count derived from stride at eval). (a) is the root fix — one expansion point, every surface inherits; (b) is a stopgap. Found by the P4 lane 2026-09-05; the card path itself is correct (dispatch tests pin it).

title: flow-gate incremental marker misses flows whose driven surface is deleted without a path overlap
description: Symptom: on the SCENE_MODIFIER_FRAMEWORK P3 lane (lane/scene-modifier-p3), deleting the Scene Setup panel Scene Loop section (scene_setup_loop.rs + the SceneSelection::SceneLoop outliner row) regressed four gltfscene flows — scene-setup-light-intensity-drag, scene-setup-shadow-softness-dropdown, scene-card-convergence-c-p1d-light-scrub-drawer, scene-setup-modifier-stack — but scripts/run_ui_flows.py --touched <range> (the landing gate's incremental pass) did NOT re-run any of them on the deleting HEAD, so the breakage only surfaced in the full flow gate. Root cause: the marker pass matches touched paths against scripts/ui-flows/manifest.json path_triggers prefixes; deleting a panel section shrinks the layout every downstream flow's absolute Point gestures were calibrated to, but no touched path names those flows' scripts — the driven-surface deletion has no path overlap with the flows that drive it. This is the BUG-252 (eight-scene-flow-scripts-dead-at-step-2-on-stale-fixture) class one level down: BUG-252 was flows that never run at all; this is flows that DO run incrementally but are missed when the change is a deletion/layout-shift rather than a touch of their value-path file. Fix shape (named, not executed here): make the incremental pass conservative on deletions — any deleted .rs path under crates/manifold-ui/src/panels/ (or any path whose removal shrinks a panel layout) widens the re-run set to every flow mapped to scenes that panel builds, or simpler: a deleted file re-runs the full manifest for its former path_triggers prefixes' scenes. P3's four regressed flows were re-calibrated in the P3 fixup commit; this bead is the gate hole itself.

title: split-audio-clip-tail-plays-from-file-start
description: Splitting an audio clip (s key) leaves the tail clip with in_point unchanged (0 = file start), so the tail replays from the start of the audio instead of continuing from the split point. Root cause: EditingService::split_clip_at_beat (service.rs:526) guards the in_point advance on video_clip_id only; audio clips are discriminated by audio_file_path. Same video-only guard in trim_clip_to_region (service.rs:658) and region-boundary interior split (service.rs:864). Fix: advance in_point for any source-media clip. Noted, not fixed here: the advance uses project spb everywhere, but playback for clips with recorded_bpm>0 advances source time at 60/recorded_bpm (engine.rs:2134) — warped clips trimmed/split get a warp-ratio offset in in_point; UI trim-left (interaction_overlay.rs:2115) has the same gap.

title: LED blend dispatch sized by compositor, not LED target — partial black LED composite
description:
Found by the BUG-2ptv (LED output dead) oracle-test lane. Symptom: with a 64x64 compositor and 8x120 LED grid, blend_layers_to_led leaves rows 64..119 of led_main black (448/960 pixels), while the screen composite is correct.

Root cause: BlendResources caches compositor width/height at construction (crates/manifold-renderer/src/layer_compositor.rs ~line 68-70, dispatch at ~line 149) and always dispatches that many workgroups. The blend shader guards on textureDimensions(t_base) (generators/shaders/compositor_blend_compute.wgsl line 24-26), so threads beyond the compositor-sized dispatch never run for the LED-sized base. In production (fullscreen compositor >= LED grid in both dims) the dispatch covers the LED target, which is why the rig path looks alive — but any config where the LED grid is taller/wider than the compositor output (small window, headless/test, tall LED walls) silently blacks the overflow region. Same class applies to any future cross-size blend_pass user.

Fix shape: dispatch from the target (or base) texture dims per call — e.g. blend_pass takes explicit dispatch dims, or reads dims from the bound textures via a small uniform/push constant. Root fix, not a LED-only special case.

title: Motion blur may smear across clip launch gaps
description:
Peter (2026-08-29): motion blur might smear more than expected when a clip launches, goes off, then on/off repeatedly. Peter (2026-09-04): blur also visible on hard clip cuts (clip A → clip B, no gap) — confirmed-observed in the field.

ROOT-CAUSED 2026-09-04 (k3 lead, reasoned not probed): node.motion_blur is stateless; the smear source is RenderScene velocity history. prev_model/prev_view_proj (render_scene.rs:4447, 4703) reset ONLY on rebuild() (object/light-count change, :1871) and never consult TemporalResetDetector (rt_reset_detector), the owner_key=hash(clip_id) cut/seek detector already in the same node, currently wired only to RT accumulation + MetalFX upscale. On a hard cut the pooled node is re-driven by a different clip while prev_view_proj still holds clip A camera state → first frame computes ndc_now - ndc_prev across two scenes → garbage velocity clamped to max_blur_px → full-strength smear flash. Gap/relaunch case: same stale-history mechanism.

Fix shape: call rt_reset_detector.detect_reset unconditionally once per evaluate (today gated on will_rt_accumulate || temporal_upscale at :4353, so on non-RT scenes the detector never advances), and when it trips also clear prev_model/prev_view_proj/prev_cam_state — the node own "no history yet" rule then gives zero velocity on the cut frame. Respects the ONE-shared-reset-path rule (temporal_reset.rs header).
close_reason: FIXED 2026-09-04 (k3 lead): velocity history wired to the shared TemporalResetDetector — cleared on cut/seek, detector unconditional per frame; RT/upscale re-enable resets preserved via explicit resume latches. Clippy green, renderer nextest 1722 pass, GPU-proofs gate + landing gate green.

title: RT glitches when FPS target is missed (temporal path vs dropped frames)
description: Symptom (Peter, live app, helmetGlitches.manifold): with RT on and the helmet rotating, bright flash/"glitch" frames appear; capping FPS to 30 makes them stop. Correlates with MISSING the FPS target, not motion speed — at 30fps the per-frame rotation step is larger yet clean. Headless rt-capture (--frame-clock, every frame on time) cannot reproduce it: 240-frame RT-on vs RT-off A/B shows identical flash statistics, so the artifact lives in the missed-deadline path. Suspects: (a) temporal accumulation/history-rejection logic reacting to irregular frame times or catch-up ticks, (b) the async accel refit stale-trace window (BUG-320 latch) interacting with dropped frames. Fix shape: audit the RT temporal path for assumptions of uniform dt (accumulate weight, reset detector, refit scheduling) and make behavior deadline-miss-safe. Note: this bug class is invisible to frame-clocked harnesses — the RT gate needs a deadline-miss mode or live soak to cover it.

title: RT spatial denoise inert under continuous motion
description: Stage-3 atrous (85e4e63ec) shows no visible effect in real moving projects: helmetGlitches.manifold 240-frame A/B (High vs Off, rt-capture --frame-clock) = composite diff ~2% of pixels at mean 0.03/255, identical frame-to-frame boil (2.036 vs 2.040). Root cause: proven on converged temporal history (paused static emissive fixture); under motion history never converges, per-frame low-spp noise dominates, and a variance-guided spatial filter cannot remove it. Fix shape: gate the feature honestly (docs/settings copy naming static-scene scope) or extend it to per-frame noise under motion; add helmetGlitches as a permanent motion A/B fixture in the RT gate so static-only wins cannot ship again.

title: ReLAX upgrade 4: variance-based history clamping
description: Reject outliers before they enter accumulated history: track plausible luminance range per pixel from recent history + neighborhood, squash anything wildly outside. Fireflies die at the door instead of haunting history for frames. Blocked on BUG-eytk. Complements the pre-blur clamp (BUG-mkgh): this one protects history, that one protects blur kernels.

title: ReLAX upgrade 3: disocclusion boost (spatial fallback on history-miss)
description: Where history is invalid (newly revealed geometry, post-cut, post-gesture), immediately filter at full spatial strength and relax as history builds, instead of waiting ~2.5s to re-converge. Shrinks the ugly window after cuts/reveals from seconds to frames. Blocked on BUG-eytk.

title: ReLAX upgrade 2: specular reprojection (virtual motion vectors)
description: Reflections slide across static surfaces when the camera moves (view-dependent). Keep a second motion answer for the reflected world and reproject specular along the reflection direction. Kills glossy-floor boiling in camera moves. Blocked on BUG-eytk. Specular motion data carries into DLSS RR inputs.

title: ReLAX upgrade 1: hit-distance-guided blur kernels
description: Size the a-trous blur per pixel by how far the reflection ray traveled: near reflections stay sharp, far ones blur hard. Hit distance is already a G-buffer channel. Fixes glossy-surface mush in hero shots. Blocked on BUG-eytk (SVGF base). The channel also feeds DLSS RR later — this is permanent infra.

title: Pre-blur firefly clamp — stop DoF/bloom smearing RT outliers into bokeh blobs

title: RT zero-intensity sun direction leak blocks near-plane reduction
description: Symptom: lowering orbit_camera DEFAULT_NEAR 0.05→0.01 breaks two gpu-proofs byte-identity gates — rt_multi_caster_shadow::zero_intensity_sun_direction_change_is_byte_identical (max abs diff 4.88e-4 over 128x128) and rt_object_cast_shadows::rt_cast_shadows_off_brightens_shadow_but_keeps_occluder_drawn.
