title: MPM: move coupled bodies by the coupled motion law
description: docs/LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md D15/D16 "Not yet": MPM keeps its own per-substep body move (matter_move_bodies_body.wgsl), which rebuilds displacement from reaction-history moments, so supports (D16) do not shape its prediction and an endpoint projection alone would be wrong there. Shape: project the per-substep increments against the support points with the same per-patch contact rule, prove against coupled_state_at, then lift the HandoverAgreement exemption for MPM.

title: GPU FLIP tests: CHUNK_OVERRIDE global races the coupled round replay proof
description: Symptom: gpu_flip_body_tests::gpu_flip_coupled_round_replay_matches_direct fails "one execute per chunk of rounds" (3 executes, expected 2) when run in the same cargo test process as gpu_flip_body_chunk_sizes_match_main_golden; it passes alone (confirmed 2026-10-06 on feat/liquid-body-handoff). Root cause: gpu_flip_pressure.rs keeps a process-wide static CHUNK_OVERRIDE (set_round_chunk, ~441) that the chunk-size test sets while other tests in the process build pressure templates. Fix shape: make the override per solver (a field or a builder arg on PressureSolver) instead of a global, so tests cannot leak chunk sizes into each other.

title: GPU FLIP: CFL clock body speed bound ignores contact projection
description: gpu_flip_clock.wgsl coupled_body_speed bounds a coupled body by v0 + a*t + P/m before the D16 contact projection (LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md section 2.1 (Body handoff amendment)). It stays an upper bound, so it is safe, but a box resting on the floor is planned as if falling at g*t, which can force extra steps per tick. Fix shape: read the contacts array in the clock and project the same way as liquid_body_state, or bound by the posed rows of the previous step. Measure step counts on a resting-box scene first; drop if it never changes the plan. Found on feat/liquid-body-handoff.

title: GPU FLIP: surface solid and whitewater obstacle pose bodies at p+v*t, not the coupled law
description: LIQUID_SOLVER_SEAM_DESIGN.md section 2.1 (Body handoff amendment) D15: the liquid poses coupled bodies by coupled_state_at / liquid_body_state (posed rows in gpu_flip_step.wgsl pose_bodies). Two readers outside the step still pose raw rows at p + v*t: the published surface solid and whitewater_obstacle_source_body.wgsl (also keep_whitewater_body.wgsl). On stage: the mesh surface and whitewater can disagree with where the water saw the box by up to half of (a*t + P/m)*t (about 5 mm at 30 Hz for a falling box). Fix shape: publish the posed rows of the tick end from the domain and have both atoms read them, or evaluate liquid_body_state in each atom with the contacts array. Found on feat/liquid-body-handoff.

title: land_branch never deletes the landed branch: the released slot still has it checked out
description: Symptom: every land_branch.py run ends with 'NOTE: branch delete failed (cannot delete branch ... used by worktree at .../slot-N)'; the lead then detaches the slot and deletes by hand (seen on four landings 2026-10-06). Root cause: land_branch releases the slot (agent-worktree.py release) but release leaves the worktree on the branch, then git branch -d refuses. Fix shape: land_branch (or release, for a landed branch) detaches the slot at the merged tip before the delete, after the merge-base --is-ancestor check passes.

title: Landing GPU-proof timing cache: three follow-ups from Fable review
description: From the review of the landing GPU-proof timing fix (93988823c). Not blockers. (1) remember_times keys on the whole-run verdict, so a red nightly teaches nothing; switch it to per-test-ok for completed, non-hung runs, the same rule --record-times now uses. (2) Add a dirty flag (from git status --porcelain) to each learned entry, so provenance is honest when someone runs --learn-times by hand. (3) Body promotion in gpu_scope.changed_test_filters counts comment-only hunks inside a test as a change; drop them with diff_scope.code_lines. Also: tests whose doc comment or pub(super) sits between #[test] and fn, and edits to lines above the fn, do not promote. That direction is safe (the test is deferred and listed).

title: gpu_queue pass reuse can fake a run-twice determinism check
description: Found by the whitewater P0 lane (2026-10-06): running the same GPU test command twice through scripts/gpu_queue.py replays the first pass on the second call (pass-reuse by command fingerprint), so a "passes twice in a row" determinism gate silently runs once. The lane only got a real second run by changing the command (--test-threads=1). Fix shape: a documented flag to force execution (e.g. --no-reuse), and use it in briefs that ask for repeat runs; or never reuse a pass for the same command within one session window when the caller asks for repetition.

title: particle_volume cooperative brick gather: built and measured slower, dropped
description: Built per the brick gather design: bitwise after an exact-position helper (fma), but particle_volume ran 1.5-4.5x slower than the generated kernel on the Dam Break oracle at CHUNK 64/128/256 (barriers and uneven lanes). Nothing landed; code on branch feat/volume-brick-gather (34ec73ef1); result in docs/archive/PARTICLE_VOLUME_BRICK_GATHER_DESIGN.md section 10 (Result) and the GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md lever table.
close_reason: Measured and dropped; recorded in docs.

title: Physics offline-to-live handoff writes an earlier timestamp into input history
description: Symptom: when a physics world runs offline and then gets a live scope without a reset, the frame fails: "physics input history cannot move backward within an epoch", node.physics_world output empty (seen in physics_boxes_render_motion_and_latch_count_until_reset). Root cause (Astra, read-only): historical sampling calls clock.observe_speed while the clock still remembers offline mode (physics.rs:942); the full advance then switches to live (clock.rs:282), caps and reanchors time, and physics.rs:1121 records the earlier simulation timestamp, which history correctly rejects. Unknown whether any stage path reuses a runtime across this mode change (export after preview is the suspect). Fix shape: decide the mode switch before sampling, or reset history on a mode change; add a focused offline->live handoff test.
notes: Checked (2026-10-06): export runs on the same engine and generator runtimes (content_export.rs:412-500), but on finishing it seeks back to the saved beat, and any backward time jump resets the physics world (physics.rs:908-922), so offline and live never share an epoch. Remaining narrow case: an export range that ends before the playhead; the restore seek is then forward, no reset, and the next live frame could hit the backward-history write. Peter: likely a non-issue; parked at P3.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Peter, 2026-10-07: one blank physics frame after scrub-then-play without a reset is acceptable.

title: GPU FLIP pressure template rebuilds on every Auto/fixed Iterations switch
description: Symptom (static review by Astra, 2026-10-06, not yet observed live): the round template inlines the stop tolerance (-1.0 for a fixed Iterations count, TOLERANCE for Auto; gpu_flip_pressure.rs Stop::tolerance). The template store replaces the least-recently-used idle slot on a miss (crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/template.rs build()), so with one idle slot, a performer toggling Iterations between 0 (Auto) and a positive count rebuilds the template on every switch (a CPU walk and ~1280 command writes per solve on that frame). Changing positive counts alone keeps the tolerance and does not rebuild. Root cause: tolerance is baked into the round params instead of read from a buffer. Fix shape: move the tolerance into the GPU-side stop record (a buffer the template reads), so one template serves both stops; or key the store so both variants stay resident. Verify first with a live toggle and the template stats (builds, command_writes).

title: Dispatch-granularity profiling reports zero-threadgroup dispatches as invalid spans
description: Symptom: frame-time --stamp-granularity dispatch on the GPU FLIP oracle reports ~519k invalid spans and unusable per-dispatch numbers. Root cause (Fable audit 2026-10-06): a zero-threadgroup dispatch never executes, so its boundary samples keep an older frame value and resolve_stamps drops the pair as invalid (manifold-gpu/src/metal/profiling.rs:361-366, 401-406); every dead gated round does this once replay is off. Fix shape: classify a pair whose stamps are both stale as skipped (zero length, counted per node), keep invalid for COUNTER_ERROR/0/reversed; frame-clock abort (frame_time.rs:875-879) fires on invalid/overflow only. The skipped count then measures dead dispatches directly.

title: ProjectSettings.vsync_enabled doc claims frame_rate snaps to a display divisor; nothing reads it
description: Found by Astra reviewing project_tool set-frame-rate (2026-10-06): crates/manifold-core/src/settings.rs documents vsync_enabled as locking content rendering to display vsync and snapping frame_rate to a display divisor, but no runtime code reads vsync_enabled; loading sets the timer from frame_rate directly (content_commands.rs ~1498, frame_timer.rs ~429). Fix: correct the comment to what the code does, or wire it if vsync pacing is still wanted (decision for Peter if the latter).

title: Graph node errors drain to stderr, never reach runtime.errors()
description: Symptom: a node that fails at execute time is marked Failed(NodeError), but its message is drained to stderr only; runtime.errors() comes back empty, so tests and the UI cannot see why a node failed. Found by Astra during the display-history (P1) review. Root cause: the executor error drain (suspect crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/execution.rs near the FrameRenderStatus::Failed merge, ~2052) is not wired to the runtime error list. Fix shape: forward each drained node error into the runtime error list the same frame, keep stderr as a mirror; add a test that a failing node shows up in runtime.errors().

title: Mix Arrays output capacity grows but never shrinks
description: Symptom: changing the GPU FLIP Dam Break Resolution card 64 -> 32 made node.mix_arrays (solid_blend) refuse: "output capacity must follow a (a=186624 bytes, out=1257728 bytes)". Root cause: the executor plans the mix output capacity once and never shrinks it, so a shrunk input no longer matches. Liquid Frame works around it by keeping the solid lattice and walls grow-only (feat/flip-display-history), as FrameRing did. That workaround cannot apply to consumers that need an exact size: Particle Volume rejects any interior that is not the exact cell count. Fix shape: let planned array capacities follow a provided input shrink (re-plan or resize the output on provided-size change), then drop the grow-only solid workaround.

title: GPU FLIP sheeting: per-solid sheeting strength multiplier
description: Native _updateSheetSeeding multiplies the sheet fill rate by the nearest solid object sheeting strength within 2h of a solid (fluidsimulation.cpp 7158-7170, MeshObject::getSheetingStrength, default 1). The GPU sheeting stage (gpu_flip_sheeting.rs) has no such multiplier: LiquidBody rows carry no sheeting strength. Fix shape: add a per-body sheeting strength to the body rows (domain role param), read the solid distance and closest body at the seed in the write pass, clamp rate*strength to [0,1] before the draw. Parent: BUG-j9l9w (GPU FLIP sheeting).

title: GPU FLIP surface: brick nodes rewrite the canonical exterior into every inactive slot each frame
description: Overnight goal item 2 (free speedups). Each brick-scheduled surface node (particle_volume, smooth_lattice, volume_surface_mesh, smooth_surface_mesh, surface_mesh_normals) runs pass 2 of liquid_bricks::dispatch every frame: a dense dispatch writing the canonical exterior value into every inactive slot. Measured 2026-10-05 on the GPU FLIP Dam Break oracle (res 64, 30 Hz, engine defaults, dispatch-stamped): the profiler tags by node, so the pass could not be split out, but smooth_lattice costs 0.082 ms for all four of its dispatches including its exterior pass, which bounds the exterior pass near 0.04 ms a node and about 0.25 ms a frame across all five (under 1% of a 33 ms frame). Blocked as not worth the risk now: skipping it needs the lattice outputs kept intact across frames (graph buffers can be reused between frames) plus a retired-brick list so only bricks that just went inactive get rewritten. Revisit when the frame is near budget and a split profile shows it above ~1%. Fix shape when it matters: pin the outputs, keep last frame mask, exterior-write only (last active AND now inactive).

title: Frame perf probe reads whitewater counts as 0: preview scalar outputs empty
description: Symptom: gpu_flip_frame_perf prints whitewater live particles 0 on every frame of the shipped Dam Break, while a headless render of the same preset shows foam and spray. runtime.preview_scalar_io() returns the whitewater node's input scalars but an empty output list, so Counts::read falls back to 0 through unwrap_or(0.0) (tests/gpu_proofs/gpu_flip_frame_perf.rs Counts::read). Root cause unknown: suspects are output scalars of a replayed or GPU-written node never reaching the preview copy, or the preview copying outputs only for nodes the editor watches. Fix shape: publish the counts through the path the app's whitewater panel reads, and make the probe fail when a named port is missing instead of reading 0.
close_reason: Fixed by the frame-perf proof landing (BUG-x9bpm): gpu_flip_frame_perf now dumps the whitewater node's counts_out and prints live particles (p50 about 13.6k on the shipped Dam Break).

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Root cause found 2026-10-05: WhitewaterStep::run in tick mode (distance wired, as the shipped GPU FLIP presets are) returns right after advance_tick without any ctx.outputs.set_scalar, so foam_count/bubble_count/spray_count/dust_count/emitted/thinned/pool_full are never published; the per-kind counts exist only on the GPU (publish_counts writes counts_out words 0-2 and 8). Fix needs a one-frame-late fenced readback of counts_out in tick mode, the way advance() reports, without adding a wait.

title: Liquid conformance landings run 2x the GPU proof budget: slow proofs not in gpu_test_times.json
description: A landing that touches tests/gpu_proofs/liquid_conformance.rs runs the whole liquid suite: 725 s against the 360 s budget on 2026-10-05, all green. Slowest: liquid_coupled_live_frame_rate 192.6 s, liquid_live_flip_force_and_coupling_match_accepted_progress 148.1 s, gpu_flip_body_reaction_matches_engine_substeps 85 s, liquid_live_700ms_frame_preserves_128_pool_and_matches_two_fixed_steps 77.5 s. None is in scripts/gpu_test_times.json, so none is skipped at landing. Fix: record times (scripts/gpu_proofs_gate.py --all --record-times) or shorten them.

title: GPU FLIP body pose predictor ignores Box3D's impulse-then-gravity motion
description: GPU FLIP coupling timing (Astra consult 2026-10-05): the fluid poses bodies at position + velocity * tick (liquid_solid_distance_body.wgsl), but Box3D applies the reaction impulse first and integrates gravity over N internal substeps, so its end pose differs by about g*dt^2*(N-1)/(2N) per tick and a stationary float needs a downward endpoint velocity that feeds the next solve. Matter predicts with acceleration and reaction timing (matter_move_bodies_body.wgsl). Fix shape: spread the reaction over the accepted interval alongside gravity and give the fluid a matching pose predictor, preserving impulse and torque totals and frame-grouping independence. Size: about 0.02-0.04 cells a tick; not shown to move any proof.
close_reason: Fixed by the body handoff landing 4e26ff403 (2026-10-06): D15 one coupled motion law poses bodies for GPU FLIP, D17 queues the reaction as a steady force over the tick instead of an impulse first.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Not minor: see BUG-a8qyy. Floating-box restlessness and water drain scale with tick length (0 drain at 60 Hz, 490 particles/s at 15 Hz) and match this mismatch's predicted size within 1.5-2.3x.

title: GPU FLIP water-race proof feature lacks water_perf dependency
description: At slot1 checkpoint2d1eaa94c, cargo check -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs,water-race-probes --tests fails E0433 at tests/gpu_proofs/gpu_flip_frame_perf.rs165,209: primitives::water_perf is gated on fluid-perf-proofs, while water-race-probes only enables gpu-proofs. Existing feature combination mismatch, not new runtime code. Targeted library tests compile and run with these features; release app also builds. Found during bounded GPU FLIP marker histogram proof. Log /Users/peterkiemann/.cache/manifold/water-campaign-20261004/marker-histogram-check.log. Deferred harness fix; no broad feature sweep or unrelated changes.
acceptance_criteria: Align the selected FLIP performance test module with its instrumentation feature; verify the exact failed compile target without changing runtime behaviour.
close_reason: water-race-probes now enables fluid-perf-proofs; gpu_flip_frame_perf builds and runs under it. Claude lead

title: Publication sort at res 128: skip all-zero leading digit passes and sort 4 elements a thread
description: After the 4-bit pair sort, liquid_frame costs 9.7 ms per tick at res 128 (waterFunv3). Live birth ids likely fit in ~24 bits, so a GPU OR of live ids could gate the top all-zero digit passes off (keep pair parity, e.g. gate in pairs or end with a gated copy), and 4 elements per thread would lengthen scatter runs. Lane estimate 20-30% off. Output must stay byte-identical to particle_publication::reference.

title: Make the publication pair sort the shared radix_sort_pairs of GAUSSIAN_SPLATS_DESIGN.md D8
description: lane/publication-radix landed a portable WGSL stable LSD radix sort of (u32 key, u32 index) pairs inside particle_publication.rs (4-bit digits, tile histograms, PrefixScan, workgroup-ranked stable scatter), proven byte-identical to a CPU reference. GAUSSIAN_SPLATS_DESIGN.md D8 plans a shared node_graph/gpu_sort.rs radix_sort_pairs(encoder, keys, values, count) and P2 builds it. When splats P2 starts, extract this sort into that module rather than writing a second one. Note: an MSL-only 8-bit radix sort also exists in crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace/emissive.rs (emissive light table), not reusable from WGSL.

title: CPU-only whitewater tests live in gpu-proofs-gated modules, so default nextest and landing never run them
description: whitewater_scene_fuses_without_gpu, vendored_whitewater_scene_loads_and_compiles_without_gpu and whitewater_emitter_fusion_compiles_without_device need no device but sit inside modules compiled only with the gpu-proofs feature, so the default nextest run and the landing gate's CPU legs skip them; the vendored compile test went stale unnoticed (stale splice after particle blending pass 2). Move them into #[cfg(test)] modules built without gpu-proofs, and check the other *_tests.rs GPU modules for the same pattern.

title: WaterDamBreakGpu water scattering: authored node value is dead, the card default overrides it
description: Symptom: graph-tool validate on WaterDamBreakGpu.json reports a chain note: water_material.volume_scattering_density is authored 0.055 but the card param water_scattering (default 0.1) overwrites it at build time, so 0.055 never reaches the render. Same on main. Root cause: preset node value and card binding default disagree. Fix shape: decide which look is intended (0.1 is what has shipped and rendered), then set the node param to match or mark the binding defaultMirrorsNodeParam so one value owns it; if the preset is builder-generated, fix the builder, not the JSON.

title: GPU FLIP: APIC transfer option and mesh-shaped or mid-run fluid objects, as the engine has
description: From the read-only engine audit (Astra task-mus1xfb6, 2026-10-03). Engine offers APIC through the bridge (fluidsimulation.cpp:7323); GPU has FLIP/PIC only. Engine consumes queued fluid mesh objects, including additions after the run starts (fluidsimulation.cpp:9164, bridge.cpp:887); GPU rejects InitialFill mesh roles (liquid/bodies.rs:294) and fills boxes only. Port both from the engine when the campaign reaches the instrument features.

title: GPU FLIP viscosity, ported from the FLIP Fluids engine viscosity solver
description: The engine water card has viscosity 0-10 (WaterDamBreak.json, Fluid section); GPU FLIP has none, so thick liquids are engine-only. Reference: viscositysolver.cpp and FluidSimulation::_applyViscosityToVelocityField (fluidsimulation.cpp:6335). Fix shape: CPU reference port proven against the engine first; GPU stage after the live clock (BUG-7qzk) lands. Peter approved 2026-10-03.

title: GPU FLIP surface tension, ported from the FLIP Fluids engine
description: The engine water card has surface_tension 0-10 (WaterDamBreak.json, Fluid section); GPU FLIP has no surface tension.
