title: tracer_reconstruction_compiles_nothing flakes when run beside other manifold-gpu tests
description: Symptom: cargo test -p manifold-gpu --lib fails 'second tracer construction compiled pipelines'; passes alone. Root cause: it reads a device-global compile counter while sibling tests compile pipelines in the same process. Fix shape: count compiles per tracer/device instance, or snapshot the counter scoped to the tracer under test.

title: Delete whitewater_step legacy level-set path once saved projects are migrated
description: feat/whitewater-per-tick (BUG-215v) moved the only shipped preset (WaterDamBreakGpuFlip) to per-tick whitewater. whitewater_step.rs keeps the old once-per-frame level_set interface and its publication ring for saved graphs. Check whether any saved .manifold project embeds a graph that uses level_set (project_tool), migrate it, then delete the legacy path.

title: Liquid solid distance drops body lattice nodes past a thin body's padding
description: Symptom: none seen yet. Thin, wide-scaled colliders get a solid band of only a fraction of a liquid cell. Root cause: build_distance (fluid_role.rs) pads by 2 lattice nodes in local units. Under scale (4 m by 0.4 m lid) that is 0.025 m in y, under half a 64^3 cell. liquid_solid_distance_body.wgsl, region_distance and the nearest-body lookup (gpu_flip_step.wgsl:365, 678) and grid_to_matter_body.wgsl:156 skip nodes past it, so those nodes read only the walls. A CPU proof showed this does not unseal the sealed-lid pool (BUG-ekb3 (sealed-lid water speed)). Fix shape: extrapolate past the lattice (the value at the nearest lattice point plus the distance to it), matching how the engine mesh level set covers the whole grid.

title: Auto perf scaler: hold a target FPS by trimming subtle quality first
description: Idea from Peter (2026-10-03), not designed. A slow feedback loop reads per-node GPU timings (already on main) and trims the least visible costs first to hold a target frame rate: surface mesh resolution, whitewater count, RT/shadow samples, coarse pressure Solve Level. Never touches what changes behaviour: sim grid resolution, tick size. Needs hysteresis (one knob at a time, no flicker) and an on-screen indicator. Depends on the clock stretching steps instead of dropping time, so a missed frame never means slow motion.

title: Sim tick region: four calls before build (SIM_TICK_REGION_DESIGN.md)
description: Design on feat/sim-fixed-tick-region 04936929a, PROPOSED. Calls: C1 live stall policy (drop+re-anchor like liquids / lag and catch up / keep time lower quality) - lead recommends drop live, never drop export; blocks P2. C2 does mosh stay tied to input frames. C3 is holding live-video inputs per frame inside a tick acceptable. C4 60 Hz sim on 120 fps project steps every other frame vs per-region texture copy to interpolate - lead recommends Sim Rate default = project FPS so no judder and no copy.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Parked by Peter 2026-10-03: focus is GPU FLIP water only. Design stays on feat/sim-fixed-tick-region 04936929a.

title: Frame-clocked timer feeds target dt when frames are missed
description: Symptom (suspected): dt-driven sims run slow vs transport on a slow machine in frame_clocked mode. Root cause: manifold-app frame_timer.rs:368 returns target_frame_duration not wall dt. Fix: moot once sims move to fixed ticks keyed to transport; else feed transport delta. Audit /tmp/fps_coupling_audit.md

title: inject_burst point and one-euro alpha depend on frame rate
description: Symptom: burst lands at a different spot live vs export or at another fps; one-euro smoothing slightly rate-dependent. Root cause: inject_burst.rs:169 random_inject_uv seeded by frame_count; one_euro_filter.rs:24 alpha 1/(1+tau/dt) first-order. Fix: seed by trigger count; exact alpha. Audit /tmp/fps_coupling_audit.md

title: ReactionDiffusion runs 4 substeps per display frame
description: Symptom: Gray-Scott pattern grows 2x faster at 120 fps, slower in a 24 fps export. Root cause: ReactionDiffusion.json fixed 4 React substeps per frame. Fix: tick region at a fixed rate. Audit /tmp/fps_coupling_audit.md

title: Texture feedback trails decay per frame: length depends on fps
description: Symptom: trails/mosh persistence half as long at 120 fps, double at 30 (StylizedFeedback, Watercolor, MetallicGlass, Lightning, OilyFluid, DataMosh, MotionMosh). Root cause: node.feedback (temporal.rs) one-frame delay mixed by a constant amount each display frame. Fix: amount^(dt*60) at the mix, or a fixed-tick region. Audit /tmp/fps_coupling_audit.md

title: Particle generators integrate per display frame (Euler dt, per-frame kicks)
description: Symptom: FluidSim2D/3D, ParticleText, Cymatics move differently by fps; diffusion/anti-clump jitter roughly 2x stronger at 120 fps. Root cause: euler_step_particles.rs:124 (+_3d:118, apply_radial_burst:197) variable-dt Euler; anti_clump_particles.rs:158 and array_diffuse_particles.rs:137 apply an unscaled kick per frame seeded by frame_count. Fix: run the array_feedback particle loop in a fixed-tick region, seed by tick index. Audit /tmp/fps_coupling_audit.md

title: frame-time harness: clip end is wall-clock, stamped frames burn the clip early
description: Symptom: at 128 on waterFunv3 the level-0 clip stops ticking at stamped frame 132 and level-1 at 145, so PNGs at frame 140 come out black. Suspect: frame-time advances transport on wall time, and slow stamped frames consume the clip faster than the frame count. Fix shape: frame-time drives transport by a fixed 1/fps per frame so frame N is the same scene time on every run.

title: Whitewater W6: sign-bit prepass for surface_crossings
description: Dam Break 64 probe (2026-10-02, feat/whitewater-speed-1 after W1-W7): node.whitewater_step.crossings is the biggest whitewater dispatch at 0.325-0.334 ms p50 (p95 0.54-0.57) of a 1.84 ms stamped whitewater step, so 0.33 ms is the ceiling; realistic gain 0.1-0.2 ms after paying for the pack pass. Shape: a pass over the refined level-set nodes packs sign bits (32 nodes per word along x, ~350 KB); surface_crossings reads 9-18 words per cell for the sign test instead of 27 scattered f32 and does the edge walk (same reads, same arithmetic) only for cells that change sign, so output stays bit-exact. Proof: the existing CPU-expected surface_crossings proof unchanged plus the cross-frame proof and fused-vs-unfused. Kill lines (plan): crossings under 0.2 ms, or the prepass costs more than it saves on the first measurement; survives the first at 64. Ordering: below the gpu_flip_step solver (44 ms stamped) and render_scene transmissive prepass (4.9 ms); do not start before those move. Plan: /tmp/fable-whitewater-speed-plan.txt W6 (copy into the bead if that file is gone).

title: Whitewater W2: live-bound pool passes by indirect dispatch
description: Dam Break 64 probe (2026-10-02, feat/whitewater-speed-1 after W1-W7): live whitewater p50 6262 / p95 9314 / max 9432 of capacity 100,000, pool_full on 0 frames; the 11 candidate pool kernels (advect, retype, age, sort.count/clear/scatter, keep, live_flags, compact, split_flags, split; preserve_foam already skipped) sum 0.196 ms p50 in the timestamped split, so that is the ceiling of the gain. Shape: compact_state/append_state also write ceil(live/256) into an indirect-args buffer; pool kernels dispatch_compute_indirect; keep still writes flags over full capacity (0 past live), sort count/scatter bound too; scans stay CPU-sized. Bit-exactness condition: every bound pass reads slots only below live and every slot past live a later pass reads is empty (kind 3). Proof: whitewater_step_matches_cpu_across_frames + the vendored lifecycle proof, plus a poisoned ping-pong tail proof asserting identical output. Kill lines (plan): live >= 0.8 x capacity or pool passes under 0.15 ms; survives both at 64 but barely. Ordering: below the gpu_flip_step solver (44 ms stamped) and render_scene transmissive prepass (4.9 ms); do not start before those move. Plan: /tmp/fable-whitewater-speed-plan.txt W2 (copy into the bead if that file is gone).

title: rigid_body card: show the derived mass (density x hull volume) as a readout
description: No per-node stats channel exists; EffectNodeContext has outputs, error, pending only. Needs a readout channel.

title: Freshly linked app binary pays ~40 s on its first launch (flow gate pays it once per gate)
description:
Symptom: the first run of a freshly linked ui-snapshot app binary takes ~40 s longer than every later run. Measured 2026-10-02 on slot-8: run_ui_flows.py scene-setup-add-object took 57.9 s on the first run after the link and 17.4 s on the second, with cargo confirming no rebuild in between (binary mtime unchanged, "Finished 0.40s"). Every landing gate relinks, so every flow gate pays this once.

Root cause: unknown. Suspects: macOS first-exec scan (syspolicyd / XProtect) of the new ~174 MB unsigned binary, or Metal's shader compile cache being keyed per binary so the UI pipelines compile cold.

Oracle: relink the binary (any change to manifold-app), then time two empty-script runs back to back (target/debug/manifold ui-snap timeline --script <file containing []>) under scripts/gpu_queue.py, and read `log show --last 5m --predicate 'process == "syspolicyd" OR process == "XprotectService" OR process == "MTLCompilerService"'` around the first exec. If the scan is the cost, an ad-hoc codesign after link or excluding target/ from the scan is the fix shape; if it is shader compile, a persistent Metal binary archive is.

title: Open-face boundaries raised Dam Break 64 solve iterations ~20% (pressure 11/14/17 -> 11/17/20, density 10/14/17 -> 12/18/19)
description: Measured by the B1 lane on HEAD vs the pre-open-faces B2 base, iteration counts identical between HEAD and B1 so the rise is from the merged open-faces work (bfd84ebf0). Each extra iteration is a full multigrid round at 64. Question to answer: is the extra work inherent to the open-face operator (weaker diagonal dominance at open faces) or a tolerance/stop-record artefact? Oracle: residual-per-iteration dump on Dam Break 64 before and after bfd84ebf0. Fix shape unknown until answered. Numbers in /tmp/fable-liquid-speed-verdict.txt B1 section.

title: Relax strength-0 skip needs executor array alias + wired-scalar skip visibility (S1, ~0.5 ms)
description: S1 render-speed: skip relax_surface_mesh when its wired strength is 0 (~0.5 ms of a 29.5 ms Dam Break frame; relax stamps 0.49-0.52 ms). Blocked on an executor feature, not a primitive change: skip_passthrough in effect_node.rs is textures-only (backend.alias_2d, compatible() checks texture_2d) and decides from inst.params only, while WaterDamBreakGpuFlip wires strength from a node.value (Mesh Relaxation = 0.0). Needs: array alias in the backend (borrowed_array, cleared on clear_skip_aliases and tenant change), executor array compat plus live-extent copy src to dst, and wired-scalar visibility in the skip decision. Lead said do not build it yet.

title: GPU FLIP density source: face-neighbour air test (blub live branch) to settle the Dam Break at its volume
description: Dam Break settles +1.7% above volume on main. Porting blub density_projection_gather_error.comp live branch whole (face-only wall weights + face-only air test) gives +0.36% depth but turns three still-pool proofs red: a seeded wall cell reads 7.5625 under rest 8 and the source pulls water to the walls. Our 26-neighbour wall weights stay as a recorded departure; the air test alone is on feat/dam-break-volume (slot-0) awaiting a GPU run after B1 lands.

title: gpu_flip_bodies.rs: lift the MAX_GROUPS = 64 per-body partial cap
description: crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/gpu_flip_bodies.rs caps the per-body partial reduction at MAX_GROUPS = 64 workgroups, so a body whose cells exceed 64*256 is reduced by a strided loop over the cap rather than one group per 256 cells. The pressure solver no longer has any such cap (partials sized from the lattice, binding 16, 256-wide finalize; feat/liquid-speed-3). Do the same here: size the per-body partials from the body cell count, remove the cap and its strided loop, prove fused-vs-unfused bit-equal on gpu_flip_body_push. Found while closing BUG-l2h3.22 (dot_products 64-workgroup cap).

title: GPU FLIP sealed pockets: null-space-aware solve instead of a one-cell pin
description: A sealed pocket pinned at one leader cell converges at about half the rate of water with a free surface: 22 to 30 rounds on the pressed-lid test frames 1 to 10 against 11 to 17 on the Dam Break, and 72 at frame 12 after the lid kills 8k particles (measured 2026-10-02, residual still halving per round at the 64 cap, so conditioning, not singularity or the f32 floor). Fix shape: project the per-pocket mean out of the residual and the preconditioner output each round (the textbook pure-Neumann multigrid treatment), using the existing pocket_sum carry reductions; drop the pin. Costs two pocket reductions per round. Price it against the speed numbers from BUG-l2h3.24 before building. Only matters when water is fully enclosed with no air, which is rare on stage.

title: GPU FLIP MAX_ITERATIONS 64 to 32: physics-visible cap cut, Peter decides
description: Lever C of the BUG-l2h3.24 speed plan. Measured max is 17 rounds at 1 step on the Dam Break with the obstacle; the scene test ceiling is already 32 per step. Cutting the cap halves the dead-round cost without GPU-driven execution (-8.5 ms CPU, -4.8 ms GPU at 64), but any solve that would need 33 to 64 rounds raises the capped error instead of converging, so it is physics-visible. Once lever A (gated encode replay) lands the GPU half is moot and the CPU saving is about 1 ms. Recommendation: decide after A lands with its numbers.
close_reason: Moot: the GPU-driven solve (lever A of BUG-l2h3.24) makes unexecuted rounds free, so the cap stays a safety ceiling at 64. Peter, 2026-10-02.

title: GPU FLIP settle: why a converged pressure stop lifts particles through the density projection
description: GPU FLIP Dam Break settle: under the converged pressure stop (Auto) alone, the 1-step worst energy rise after frame 400 went from +8.5e-5 E0 (fixed 8 iterations, bd5ac9580) to +2.5e-4 E0; density fixed at 8 with pressure Auto gave +1.2e-4. All worst frames are ~3e-4 KE<->PE swaps in the first settling slosh, PE-led under Auto. With the engine FLIP share and extension layers ported (be507af2a) the full port is back to +7.8e-5 (1 step) and +3.0e-5 (2 steps), under the 1e-4 bound, so nothing is red. Open question: why a more exact pressure field lifts particles via the density projection. Unproven suspect: the density projection moves particles further when pressure is more exact and that movement does work. Oracle: log the density move change in PE per frame for frames 400-430, Auto vs fixed 8, on the current tip. Not a landing blocker; do not raise the bound.

title: GPU FLIP at 128 for 60 fps: tall-cell grid plus narrow particle band
description: Idea for 128^3 live at 60 fps (today about 135 ms/frame at 128, needs ~8x). Narrow-band FLIP (Ferstl 2016) keeps particles only in a few-cell band at the surface; deep water is grid velocity plus level set. That cuts particle work 3-5x but leaves the full pressure solve. Restricted tall-cell grids (Chentanez and Mueller 2011, real-time Eulerian water) collapse deep columns into one tall cell, which shrinks the pressure solve. Both build on the current grid FLIP: walls, bodies, whitewater and the mesher carry over. Start only after 64^3 holds volume and runs at 60 fps.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Also explore here: adaptive step count per tick (GPU-resident n from max speed, indirect dispatch, Max Steps cap). Deferred 2026-10-02: fixed 1 step per tick is the default until then.

title: Freeze compiler does not know about provided array outputs
description: Risk: the freeze compiler has no notion of provided array outputs (provides_array_output/provided_array_output), so fusing a node that owns its output buffer, such as volume_surface_mesh after BUG-j34u (GPU FLIP mesh sizing), would bind the wrong or no storage. Today volume_surface_mesh is unfused in every preset (graph-tool fusion), so nothing is affected. Fix shape: the fusion planner treats a provided output as a group boundary (or refuses to fuse the node) and a test proves it.

title: Retire zero-lattice sentinels after liquid pending fix
description: Pending-input handling is per consumer. With BUG-hx08 (liquid domain publishes zero lattice while pending) fixed, liquid domains declare their outputs pending until their first good frame. Downstream liquid stage nodes now early-out on NodeInputs::any_pending. Two pre-existing zero sentinels still treat "no frame yet" as a zero lattice and could now be dead or replaced with a pending check: sort_particles_into_cells (invalid_box && count==0 quiet return) and particle_volume ("a producer without a frame yet publishes no lattice"). Check which producers still feed them zeros, such as CPU FLIP fluid_surface. Then decide between deleting the sentinels and a runtime-level rule: skip evaluate when an input is pending unless the node opts in to partial results, like render_scene and physics_world. That rule would remove the class instead of patching each validating consumer.
close_reason: Closed

title: Landing gate clippy skips examples
description: scripts/landing_gate.py line 350 runs cargo clippy with --tests only, so example files (e.g. manifold-renderer/examples/fluid_capture.rs) are never linted at landing. Fix shape: add --examples to the touched-package clippy call, or --all-targets if bench/bin targets are also missed; check the cost on manifold-renderer first.

title: WaterDamBreakGpuFlip ships without the studio floor its engine twin has
description: Symptom: WaterDamBreakGpuFlip.json renders over black, while WaterDamBreak.json (the FLIP Fluids engine race reference) sits on a grey studio floor. Side-by-side race clips are not like for like. Root cause: the GPU FLIP preset was authored without the studio_floor group of 4 nodes (cube_mesh, pbr_material, transform_3d with scale 2000x0.2x2000 at pos_y -0.28, scene_object wired to render_scene object_6). Fix shape: add the same four nodes to WaterDamBreakGpuFlip.json on object_6, which is free. A /tmp copy with exactly that edit is /tmp/liquid-race/WaterDamBreakGpuFlipStudio.json.
notes: Fixed on chore/flip-studio-floor f8a6bdf4c: the engine preset four floor nodes on WaterDamBreakGpuFlip object_6, file written by the builder test (UPDATE_GPU_FLIP_PRESET=1), thumbnail and node catalog regenerated. Close on landing.
close_reason: Closed

title: fluid_capture example cannot load GPU FLIP presets
description: The fluid_capture example refuses WaterDamBreakGpuFlip with "preset has no fluid_surface node and no node.matter_domain": it knows the FLIP Fluids engine and Matter domains but not node.gpu_flip_domain. Look renders for GPU FLIP went through render-generator-preset (--frames N --max-frames N gives frame N exactly) instead. Fix shape: teach fluid_capture to find node.gpu_flip_domain the same way it finds node.matter_domain, or retire it in favour of render-generator-preset for preset stills.
notes: Fixed on chore/flip-capture e3d01647c: fluid_capture finds the liquid through the seam (is_liquid_domain plus the one node whose registry outputs carry the particle frame), with no per-solver type ids. It loads WaterDamBreakGpuFlip (frame node "frame"), WaterDamBreakMatter and WaterDamBreak. The wall limit now starts after the GPU queue is acquired. Close on landing.

title: relax_surface_mesh cannot head a fused region: no fused output capacity fits a gathered anchor beside other gathers
description: node.relax_surface_mesh (Liquid Surface mesh relaxation, feat/water-look) is Pointwise with every input BufferGather. As a producer the region builder refuses it ("array output capacity disagrees with the declared fused shape", MANIFOLD_REGION_DEBUG=1): FromInput needs one Coincident anchor and MultipleOf needs the named port to be the only array input. volume_surface_mesh and particle_volume share this state. It is pinned standalone by liquid_surface_tests::fluid_relax_surface_mesh_stays_standalone_in_the_fused_view, which fails when it starts fusing. Owed: when the freeze compiler grows a capacity shape for a gathered anchor (e.g. FromInput on a named gathered port), the fused-vs-unfused proof for relax_surface_mesh, replacing the pin. Parent work: BUG-xwf1 (Liquid Surface mesh relaxation).

title: Show::new held names hold nothing on the GPU FLIP render def
description: Symptom: in whitewater_scene_tests, Show::new(def, size, false, held) with held = frame / liquid_smooth_z (ids that exist in runtime.graph) then frames left dump_arrays_all empty ("frame.particles_b is not held; held: []"). set_dump_visible resolves names through effect_nodes slot node_map, which seems not to match these generator node ids. Root cause: unknown. Suspects: generator runtime from_def_with_device has no effect_nodes slot, or node_map keys differ from graph node_id. The whitewater-oracle capture() (emitter_oracle, feature whitewater-oracle) uses the same held path, so whitewater_emitter_matches_flip is suspect, unverified. Workaround in liquid_blocks_tests: Show::set_dump_all on capture frames. Fix shape: make held names resolve for generator runtimes, or move capture() to set_dump_all. Signed: Claude Opus 5.5, lane seat (liquid-blocks).
close_reason: Duplicate of BUG-bqwx (node-scoped array dump set holds nothing on a generator runtime)

title: Slot caches keep stale build-script out/ libraries
description: Second-largest slot cache class after BUG-vnp8: build-script out/ products. Each warm slot holds up to 7 stale build/spirv-tools-sys-<hash>/out/libspirv-tools.a copies at ~588 MB (measured 2026-10-02: 8-11 GiB per slot, ~50 GiB pool-wide). storage_budget.py keeps out/ on purpose: Cargo does not rerun a build script whose out/ vanished, so file-level deletion would leave a fresh fingerprint pointing at a missing .a. Fix shape: remove whole stale build/<pkg>-<hash> units together with their .fingerprint twin (unit-level, not file-level), or raise the per-slot cap to absorb them. Not urgent now that hashed executables (the 100 GiB class) are reclaimable.

title: Deep-pool pressure fixtures cannot be regenerated
description: tests/fixtures/deep_pool_pressure_problems.bin.zst and deep_pool_density_problems.bin.zst were written by gpu_flip_write_deep_pool_fixtures, deleted with the GPU FLIP atom graph (feat/gpu-flip-coarse-solve). The fixtures still gate pressure_module_matches_reference_deep_pool and the Auto iteration rule (GPU_FLIP_PRESSURE_SOLVE.md section 4, iteration counts). Fix: a fixture writer that dumps the solve inputs from node.gpu_flip_step (classify, open fractions, divergence, phi), or accept them as frozen data and say so in the doc.

title: Node-scoped array dump set holds nothing on a generator runtime
description: Symptom: PresetRuntime::set_dump_visible(None, &[names]) on the GPU FLIP Dam Break generator (unfrozen) leaves dump_arrays_all() empty, even for top-level nodes like "frame"; whitewater_emitter_matches_flip (O2, whitewater-oracle) failed with "frame.particles_b is not held; held: []". set_dump_all(true) works. Root cause unknown. Suspects: instrumentation.rs set_dump_visible_with_context matching node_map of the generator EffectSlot (build.rs:650 segment), or dump_array_resources only recording under dump-all. Fix shape: find why the visible set does not reach array capture; then the thumbnail atlas path for generators may share it. Workaround in whitewater_scene_tests Show::new uses set_dump_all.
close_reason: node-scoped dump_array_set; on chore/whitewater-sweep

title: GPU queue wait line names the process cwd, not the worktree it runs from
description: Symptom: the gpu-queue wait line said the holder gpu_proofs_gate was in the main checkout while the script was slot-0/scripts/gpu_proofs_gate.py run with cwd at the main checkout. Root cause: the holder label records cwd. Fix shape: record the worktree of the script path (git toplevel of argv[0]) in gpu.holder alongside cwd.

title: face_gravity fused capacity is MinInputs, unfused is the face lattice
description: Symptom: node.face_gravity declares no output_capacity in its primitive!, so the freeze compiler sizes its fused output by the default MinInputs (the faces input length), while array_output_capacity returns face_capacity(params) ((n+1)^3 from nodes_x/y/z). Fused and unfused outputs can differ in length when faces is longer or shorter than the lattice; harmless in the shipped GPU FLIP step (faces is exactly the face grid there) but the two contracts disagree. Root cause: missing declaration, found during feat/gpu-flip-solids. Fix shape: add output_capacity: FusedOutputCapacity::ParamProduct { params: &LATTICE_PARAMS, plus: 1 } like subtract_pressure and constrain_solid_faces, regen the fused snapshot, check other face-grid atoms (extend_faces, particles_to_faces) for the same gap.

title: Retire Grafana usage stack and Codex tooling?
description: With the litellm proxy gone, scripts/grafana/*, scripts/claude_usage_export.py and its launchd plist (com.manifold.claude-usage-export) read and write the litellm Postgres DB, so the usage and fleet dashboards are dead. Also scripts/codex_*.py, their tests and AGENTS.md remain wired into landing_gate.py tooling_checks. Peter decides: retire the Grafana usage stack and/or the Codex tooling, or keep them.

title: GPU FLIP sparse tile storage: memory and work scale with the water, not the box
description: After phase 3 tile skipping (active tiles inside a dense box) lands: store only active 8^3 tiles (plus a ring) so memory and time scale with water volume, enabling much larger tanks/resolutions. Multigrid works per tile hierarchy. Octrees (adaptive cell size) judged not worth it for now: harder pressure solve, GPU-unfriendly, and the visible surface needs full detail anyway. Raised by Peter 2026-10-01.

title: Matter domain can issue impulse receipts for ticks that never ran after a compute error
description: Symptom: if node.matter_domain errors after LiquidImpulses::observe_frame has advanced the clock (e.g. a FieldBinding or upload error later in run), drain_applied can report an impulse as applied for a tick whose GPU work was never encoded. Root cause: receipts are released on clock advance, not on successful encode. Suspects: matter_domain.rs run() ordering around LiquidFields::upload. Fix shape: release applied receipts only after the frame encodes, or roll the impulse back to the queue on error.
close_reason: Receipts commit only after the matter domain prepares and uploads the frame fields (commit_frame); failed or held frames abandon to discarded receipts, drains abandon as a backstop. Proven by liquid_impulse_failed_frame_discards.

title: Tune CPU FLIP engine settings from the GPU FLIP parity audit
description: Use the parity table (/tmp/flip_parity/PARITY.md, from the GPU FLIP vs engine audit) to find where the CPU FLIP engine takes shortcuts, and improve its exposed settings and defaults (step/CFL rule, wall handling knobs, density/volume behaviour). Settings only; engine source stays unedited so it remains the reference. Do it after the GPU FLIP wall and step fixes land. Proposed by Peter 2026-10-01.
close_reason: Misread: Peter meant the engine source as a reference for improving GPU FLIP, not tuning the engine.

title: node.combine_rows declares MinInputs fusion capacity while its output follows the row_length param
description: Symptom: none live. combine_rows has no output_capacity clause, so it declares MinInputs, but array_output_capacity returns row_length, and coef is a one-element gather. MinInputs over base, matrix and coef would count 1. The build_region probe sees the mismatch and keeps the atom unfused, so the CG axpys never fuse (gpu_flip_solve_and_step_do_not_fuse). Root cause: the declaration does not match the output rule (the BUG-sk62 class). Fix shape: declare output_capacity ParamProduct over row_length (or FromInput base), then add a fused-against-unfused proof with a coincident neighbour, as gpu_flip_atom_tests does for divide_by_value.

title: Measure naga's loop bounding in every kernel loop
description: naga 28 SPIR-V Options default force_loop_bounding: true, which the shared shader pipeline (manifold-gpu shader_common.rs compile_to_optimized_spirv) keeps. It adds a two-word countdown to every loop in every compiled kernel, seen in the MSL as a uint2 counter checked and decremented each iteration (for example in the workgroup-zeroing proof kernels). It is there so the Metal compiler cannot assume an infinite loop away. The cost per iteration is a few ALU ops in every loop app-wide: marching cubes, reductions, P2G loops, the Krylov kernels. Unknown whether it is measurable. Next: time one loop-heavy kernel with it on and off. Only if the difference is real, weigh turning it off; that needs a guarantee every loop terminates, the same kind of guarantee the workgroup-zeroing work weighed and did not need. Found while fixing the workgroup-memory zeroing (perf/workgroup-zero-init).

title: closes-trailer-guard rejects dotted child bead ids (BUG-l2h3.3)
description: The Closes: trailer check in .claude/hooks/closes-trailer-guard.py only accepts ids like BUG-abcd, so child ids like BUG-l2h3.3 fail to parse and landings must use Closes: none plus manual bd close. Fix: accept an optional .N suffix in the id pattern.

title: liquid_stats does not scan the face grid for non-finite values
description: I8 (a non-finite tick is never published) gates face publication on the particle stats word 0. A tick with finite particles but non-finite faces would publish the faces. Shape: liquid_stats (and matter_stats) add the face grid to the non-finite count when faces are published, or the frame publish kernel checks each face.

title: Coupled matter display clock lags one extra tick at 30 fps export
description: Symptom: in a coupled matter scene exported at 30 fps, display_time trails one tick more than at 60 fps. Root cause unknown; suspect the coupled pair steps the rigid owner after the liquid tick so the frame clock sees the previous display time. Fix shape: decide the coupled display contract (display one tick behind simulation regardless of stride) and assert it in the export check.

title: Re-test the MTL4 temporal scaler after each macOS update
description: The MTL4 temporal scaler is off by default since BUG-ca67 (RT proofs time out the GPU), 2026-10-01, macOS 26.6.1 on M4 Max. Temporal upscale uses classic MTLFX. Symptom it guards against: an MTL4 temporal scaler that follows an earlier one on the same device hangs its MTL4 command buffer until the MTL4 queue watchdog kills it at about 4 s (MTL4CommandQueueErrorTimeout); the classic frame waiting on it stalls 4 s or times out, and a classic timeout makes macOS ignore the process queue. Repro, with the gpu_proofs binary built by cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs --test gpu_proofs --no-run: (1) MANIFOLD_MTL4FX_TEMPORAL=1 <gpu_proofs binary> --test-threads=1 rt_p4_metalfx_temporal rt_t2b_temporal_wiring (was: 4 s stall 4 of 4 runs, timeout 2 of 4; each module alone clean); (2) MANIFOLD_MTL4FX_TEMPORAL=1 cargo test -p manifold-gpu m4_temporal_scaler_encodes_one_frame (smoke). Re-enable only when (1) is clean 3 of 3 and the full gpu_proofs binary is clean in parallel with the flag set. Before re-enabling, also fix two latent races in metalfx_m4.rs MTL4Bridge under concurrent use: event values are handed out at encode time but signalled in commit order on one shared timeline, and the allocator ring slot claim is not atomic.

title: Fan-out buffer regions: split a fused component at the escaping output instead of refusing it whole
description: Found in GPU whitewater P5 (whitewater_spawn_chain_fuses in whitewater_extent_tests.rs). A fused buffer region writes one output (FREEZE_COMPILER_MAP.md section 4, region gates: fan-out buffer region refused). When a coincident chain has two consumers outside it, partition_regions unions the whole chain and build_region then refuses it, so every member runs unfused. Whitewater: jitter, sample, energy, wavecrest and count fold into one kernel while the counts are the only way out, but spawn_whitewater also gathers the sampled particles and the energy, so all five now run as five dispatches. Fix shape: when a buffer component would be refused as fan-out, cut it at each member whose output escapes, materialise that output, and build the pieces separately (with spawn gathering energy that gives 3 dispatches; with spawn recomputing the energy potential from the gathered velocity, 2). Needs the fused-against-unfused proofs and the GPU proofs gate, since it changes fusion for every preset with such a shape. Measure first: P6 reports the whitewater GPU cost against its 2 ms budget.

title: Thumbnail warm-up advances time while async nodes are still pending
description: Symptom: render_preset_thumbnail (preset_thumbnail.rs) runs a fixed 60-frame warm-up with advancing time, then pumps more frames until io_pending and warmup_pending settle. Frames rendered while an async source is still preparing still move the clock, so how far a preset has run when the thumbnail is taken depends on how fast its background work finished. BUG-qssh (WaterDamBreakMatter thumbnail differs run to run) was this class for the liquid colliders and is fixed on feat/liquid-seam-build by making offline liquids wait for their collider lattices; other async sources (IoBridge file sources, other warm-up channels) can still drift. Fix shape: hold the recipe clock while anything is pending (render with dt 0 until settled), then run the fixed warm-up; prove with the forced-contention thumbnail test pattern from tests/gpu_proofs/liquid_conformance.rs.

title: FLIP fill-height refusal is lumped and does not name Initial Fill Height
description: Symptom: a FLIP domain (node.fluid_surface) refuses a bad fill height with the lumped text "Water: invalid domain, resolution, fill height, surface detail or mesh capacity", which does not carry the panel label Initial Fill Height or say which control is wrong. Seam invariant I10 wants every refusal to name its control in the panel words; the conformance table leaves FLIP as built (design D3) so the check does not cover this case. Fix shape: split the native setup validation into per-control refusals that use the param labels, then add a FLIP refusal case to liquid/conformance.rs.

title: MPM fixed-point accumulator overflow is never reported
description: Symptom: the matter P2G grid accumulates into i32 fixed point. node.matter_stats measures the peak accumulator magnitude (max_accum) and the clamped node count every tick, but only GPU proofs read them (matter_scene.rs headroom check, matter_look.rs); the domain never reports an accumulator at or near overflow, so a wrapped sum would move water wrongly with no error. This is a gap in seam invariant I11 (overflow is counted and reported). The fixtures stay well under 2^30 today. Fix shape: when max_accum reaches the saturation band, report it by name through the node error path (and the run-time error channel once that reaches the UI), naming the controls that raise it; add the case to the MPM row overflow check in liquid/conformance.rs.

title: Initial velocity on rigid bodies and liquid fills
description: Rigid bodies and liquid fills start at rest; there is no authored starting velocity. Scene impulses can give a body one after the first frame (not yet on bodies coupled to Live Matter, see the matter-coupled impulse bug), and nothing can give a liquid fill one: liquid impulses are refused until seam P8. The liquid conformance collision check wanted the seam design scene (zero gravity, a liquid blob striking a free box at 1 m/s) and fell back to a box falling onto a weightless pool with a premise window. Phase 6 forces work will want this too. Shape: a start velocity on node.rigid_body (linear, maybe angular) applied at the epoch start, and a start velocity on the liquid fill box, both reset with the epoch.

title: fluid_particle_ring_exhaustion_never_blocks fails under GPU load
description: Symptom: crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/fluid/particle_tests.rs fluid_particle_ring_exhaustion_never_blocks panics at line 174 (assert runtime.busy) on two consecutive runs on perf/liquid-surface while the shared GPU was loaded (load 7-30). The test signals the GPU event then expects the very next non-blocking frame to have sent a request. Root cause: unknown; suspect the CPU does not yet observe the signalled shared event when the non-blocking frame runs, so the test races the event, not the ring. The surface change on that branch does not touch this path (no preset, no surface atom). Fix shape: wait on the event value (or poll with a bounded timeout) before the non-blocking frame, so the test asserts ring behaviour rather than signal latency.
close_reason: Duplicate of BUG-sqbl (three renderer lib tests red, pre-existing), which lists fluid_particle_ring_exhaustion_never_blocks

title: Generic-over-T one-frame array delay: fold array_feedback and liquid_feedback
description: Three typed twins of one delay exist: node.array_feedback (Array(Particle)), node.liquid_feedback (Array(FluidParticle), seed required) and node.field_feedback (Array(f32), zero start). They share emit_delayed and capture_for_next_frame in array_feedback.rs, with a DelayStart mode, so logic is not duplicated. Each still needs its own primitive! block, because a port's element type is part of its static signature and Permissive matching is consumer-only and allow-listed (validation.rs). Fix shape: a primitive macro (or registry-side generic) that stamps a typed delay per element type from one declaration, so the next type is one line. Worth it at the fourth type, not before.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Now two twins, not three: node.field_feedback was deleted on feat/fft-water with the SWASH warm start, and the DelayStart mode went with it. The fold is still worth it only at a new element type.

title: MPM face grid: extend one layer so matter scenes can host whitewater
description: The MPM face grid publishes face_valid_layers 0: own faces and one layer across carry velocity, but only 67.7% of faces one layer out along their axis do (Dam Break at 64, 45 ticks, face_grid_demo_swash_and_matter_side_by_side). Whitewater refuses a grid under 1 layer, so no MPM scene can host it. Shape: one extension pass on the seam arrays (a zero face with carrying 6-neighbours of the same component takes their mean, FLIP extrapolation style), run after the three matter_face_component nodes, then raise MATTER_FACE_VALID_LAYERS. Only worth doing if an MPM scene should get whitewater (GPU_WHITEWATER_DESIGN.md D13 makes SWASH the host).

title: Factory thumbnails go stale silently when code changes the render
description: factory_thumbnails_fresh hashes only the preset JSON bytes, so a code change that alters a render never flags its thumbnail. Seen: WaterFloatingBoxMatter.png as committed (last regenerated in 6ae10a0c3) differs from what feat/fft-water code renders for the same JSON by 3,152 of 36,864 pixels (max channel delta 51), reproducible across runs and with the pre-whitewater matter_frame. Fix shape: regenerate the stale thumbnail when feat/fft-water lands; consider a nightly render-and-compare over the factory presets in trunk_health instead of a JSON-only hash.

title: Substep region arrays never return their storage after the region ends
description: Arrays touched by a substep region are treated as live across the whole outer region (correct), but they are never released at the region last step, so later steps cannot reuse them. Returning that storage is the next memory saving after the planner-reuse fix (feat/planner-reuse). Guard: the lifetime checker in resource_allocation::lifetimes must keep passing, including nested fixtures.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Built on feat/substep-region-release 4a9a51e31 (off feat/planner-reuse, not landed): plan_array_allocations returns a region held_resources to the reusable pool after the region last step. Lifetime oracle green on bundled presets and the nested copy-chain fixture (test now asserts post-nest reuse of region storage); nextest manifold-renderer 2116 passed; gpu_proofs substeps 8/8 incl. nested_region_shared_storage_matches_dedicated and post_frame_readers_never_see_reused_storage. Bundled presets gain nothing yet: the Matter presets 10-14 region-held arrays are all growing (dedicated). Parked for BUG-l2h3.7.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Correction: for the Matter presets the planner reuse count stays 0 with this change (their region-held arrays find no later taker); I did not check which of them are growing.

title: Substep region body captured by an outside non-substep feedback node is not refused
description: Symptom: the plan compiler accepts a graph where a node inside a substep region body is captured by a feedback node outside the region that is not itself a substep boundary. Found during nested substep regions (seam P5/P6) on feat/nested-substep-regions, out of scope there. Root cause: the region validation only checks captures by the region boundary itself. Fix shape: add a named MalformedSubstepRegion refusal plus a CPU test, next to the six nesting refusals in substeps.rs.

title: SWASH render: water read as clear glass because its surface mesh was open at the tank walls and floor
description:
Symptom: SWASH Dam Break through render_def (WaterDamBreakGpu.json render graph) read as see-through glass. Scattering 0.055 to 5 and absorption distance 3 to 0.5 m changed the water pixels by at most 6/255. The shipped preset (FLIP engine into the same Liquid Surface group, same material) showed the milky teal depth body.

Root cause (observed): the SWASH scene builder fed the Liquid Surface group the bare tank as its lattice (bounds = the 4 m inner box, nodes n+1) with an all-zero solid lattice. The seam contract (GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md section 3.2) says grid_bounds is the padded lattice and solid is the wall distance. With liquid touching the lattice border, the smoothing passes (node.smooth_lattice, after node.particle_volume) pull the border nodes inside the liquid, so marching cubes emits no closing faces: at frame 240 only 7,931 floor vertices where about 200k are expected. The volume path pass then sees entries with no exits. A debug fs_pbr readback measured the SWASH path at median -9.0 m (96% negative, then clamped to 0), against +1.13 m on the preset.

Fix (branch look/water-material): WaterScene::with_closed_surface gives the surface MatterLattice::from_layout(domain_layout(...)) bounds and nodes, and the harness writes matter_frame::wall_distance_lattice(lattice, 63) as solid. After it: SWASH path median 1.15 m, closing faces on every side, render smoke 64 clean over 900 frames (mesh within 4 cm of the walls).

Owed: (1) the meshed-volume oracle (swash_volume.rs volume_and_area) assumes the open mesh, so with_surface keeps the bare lattice for it. When SWASH publishes the seam for real (BUG-pi9b), the oracle has to move to a closed-mesh volume. (2) D15 says border nodes are band, but smooth_lattice breaks that for any producer whose liquid reaches the border. Decide whether smoothing should pass border nodes through.
notes:
Owed item 1 done on look/water-material (dabe21462): with_surface is the one closed builder; volume_and_area reads the closed mesh (tank-clipped divergence flux). At 64 Dam Break, old vs new drift: frame 89 -9.25% vs -0.97%, frame 299 -0.08% vs +0.12%, max 11.85% vs 2.41%, skin 30.2 vs 30.7 mm. Owed item 2 (smooth_lattice and the D15 border) goes to the seam worker as a rail: surface lattices only ever come from the padded domain layout. Lead call, 2026-09-30.
Material follow-up on look/water-material c5b3563a8: WaterDamBreakGpu water now scattering 0.1, absorption distance 2.5, tints (0.35,0.76,0.76) and (0.70,0.88,0.88); matched to the FLIP exports within 2 sRGB levels.

title: Headless fluid_capture shows a grey backdrop where the app export shows black
description: Symptom: rendering Peter's waterTest graph (export-time save) headless through fluid_capture gives a grey background; his app exports of the same graph (~/Downloads/waterExportTestVert64ResVortex.mp4) are black. Graph and environment settings match the save. Root cause unknown; suspects: environment/background colour source differs between the headless capture path and the export path (clear colour, environment map default, tone map of the backdrop). Fix shape: find where each path sets the backdrop and make them one source. Matters because headless stills are the look oracle for water work.
close_reason: Not a bug: Peter removes the studio floor object for his exports; headless renders kept it.

title: Liquid Surface mesh relaxation: shared-vertex marching cubes plus an umbrella smoothing atom
description: GPU_FLUID_SURFACE_DESIGN.md section 11 row (Vertex welding, shared-vertex output, mesh smoothing) has its trigger met: Peter wants the bake look. Sized in P6f option 3: marching cubes emits one vertex per lattice edge plus an index buffer; a relaxation atom runs FLIP's TriangleMesh::smooth umbrella step (v += value x (neighbour mean - v)); normals recomputed; then de-index or draw indexed. Three to four atoms on the codegen path with value and fused-vs-unfused proofs. Offline on the dumped GPU mesh, 0.5 x 4 takes the Dam Break 8 s band from 8.0/6.1 deg to 4.4/4.7 (bake 8.3/4.9) and keeps sheet coverage. Build only if Peter wants more than the isotropic-blob look (BUG-4snj (Liquid Surface default look)) gives.
notes: Built on feat/water-look as one atom, node.relax_surface_mesh: an umbrella pass finding neighbours through the 4 cells around each vertex lattice edge, no index buffer or welding needed. Two passes in the Liquid Surface group, card param Mesh Relaxation (0..1, default 0 = bit-exact copy). Off-cost decision: BUG-j34u (Mesh relaxation off-cost). Fusion blocker: BUG-q7na (relax_surface_mesh cannot head a fused region). Awaiting a look review before landing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Staged GPU check of the water presets above res 64 on the BUG-bnp9 fix
description: Verification for BUG-bnp9 (GPU MPM water locks the Mac above resolution 64) on fix/mpm-res-lockup. The CPU sweep matter_extent_tests proves every lattice-sized buffer covers its dispatch at res 8..=512. Still owed: a real GPU run of Water Dam Break (Live GPU) with the Liquid Surface at res 80, then 96, then 128, one step at a time, stopping on any hitch, ideally a fresh build at each res and one live raise from 64. Nobody has run it above 64 yet. Note that scripts/gpu_proofs_gate.py includes matter_solver_perf, which builds a solver-only 128^3 scene (no Liquid Surface).

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: SWASH render smoke (branch test/swash-render-smoke, 03d4b9c41): the shared GPU Liquid Surface ran under SWASH particles at 64 through the full WaterDamBreakGpu render graph, 900 frames each on the Dam Break and a still pool, no GPU fault, no failed command buffer, mesh within capacity (peak 872k of 8.39M vertices) and inside the tank, GPU memory flat at 1.3 GB. CPU extent proofs now cover the rendered scenes at 64, 96 and 128 (fft_water_rendered_scenes_cover_every_dispatch). The 96 and 128 GPU runs were NOT done: the auto-mode permission classifier denied the 96 run in the worker seat. To run them: SWASH_SMOKE_DIR=<dir> cargo test --manifest-path <slot>/Cargo.toml -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs --lib swash_render_smoke_96 -- --nocapture --test-threads=1 (then _128). This is SWASH, not MPM: it says nothing yet about the matter solver above 64.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Correction to the description: matter_solver_perf is not in the default GPU gate. It sits behind the matter-perf-proofs feature (tests/gpu_proofs/main.rs gates the module; the test itself now builds Dam Break at 64 cubed), so scripts/gpu_proofs_gate.py never runs it. Found during seam P4.

title: Matter buoyancy reads 4.35% under Archimedes once the push-out pays the body
description: With D30 (GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md, grid_to_matter adds the push-out momentum to the body reaction words, BUG-n97i) matter_coupling_hydrostatic_force reads 600.5 N from the reaction (602.5 N from body rows) against rho0*g*V = 627.8 N, -4.35%, inside its 5% gate by 0.65 points; the neutral density-1 box sinks from 0.386 m to 0.050 m over 2 s. Before D30 it read -0.44% because the uncounted push-out momentum acted as a ghost force holding up part of the liquid above the box. The exchange itself is now closed (matter_coupling_energy_light_body residual <= 0.075% of momentum exchanged), and matter_coupling_floating_equilibrium improved (offset 0.328*dx -> 0.216*dx). Open question: is the 4% a boundary-layer discretization deficit (check convergence 32 -> 64, never above 64 per BUG-bnp9) or a top-face artefact (gravity presses the top particle layer into the box every substep and the push-out takes that load)? Verification task: run the hydrostatic scene at res 32 and 64 and at two box sizes; if the error shrinks with dx it is discretization and the gate stands; if not, look at the top-face push-out.

title: SWASH helper: surface-native preconditioner toward the ~12-pass ideal
description: Research item from Peter, 2026-09-30. The six-view helper (docs/FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md D4) gets 15-20 passes on drops/tower; the per-patch exact-inverse oracle (oracle_blocks.py) gets 11-12, flat with resolution. Closing that gap cuts about 30% of the pressure solve, since passes multiply the box-solve cost, which dominates each pass. Fewer views is NOT the lever: three unsigned views need twice the sheets per view, the same 24 planes of work. Direction: approximate the surface square-root operator directly on the collar, whatever its shape, e.g. a multilevel scheme on collar cells. The earlier surface-Laplacian attempt failed only because stair-stepped collar face graphs split into disconnected pieces; diagonal (26-neighbour) connectivity may fix that. Python experiment first. Revive after the P2 race vs MPM.

title: SWASH audio-spectral forcing: audio bands drive water wavelengths
description: Idea from Peter, 2026-09-30, during SWASH (docs/FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md) P1. Map audio spectrum bands onto water wave sizes: bass pumps long swells, mids the tank resonances, highs fine surface shimmer. The pressure solve works in the box cosine basis, but it describes pressure, not motion, so this needs a force-injection atom that adds velocity in chosen wavelength bands (a band-limited push through the existing cosine-transform atoms) before the projection. Revive after the P2 race vs MPM, win or lose.

title: Codegen: buffer atom with several outputs, one atomic
description: generate_standalone_buffer (crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/freeze/codegen/standalone.rs, about lines 478-700) handles one atomic output, or several outputs with no atomics, and errors with "Multi-output atomic is not a shape any atom needs yet". region.rs (about line 1569) makes any atom with an atomic output a Boundary. Now needed: the fix for the collider push-out momentum loss in coupled MPM (see the bug "Coupled MPM loses momentum at the collider push-out") wants grid_to_matter (Pointwise, points aliased to points_out) to also accumulate into the per-body reaction words, or a separate push-out atom with the same output shape. Work: support the shape in standalone codegen, decide the fusion kind for an aliased Pointwise output next to an atomic side output, and add the fused-vs-unfused proof.
close_reason: landed

title: Coupled MPM loses momentum at the collider push-out
description: Symptom: in matter_coupling_energy_light_body (feat/gpu-mpm-build-b), body momentum plus liquid momentum minus gravity drifts by -0.24 / -12.1 / -26.8 kg*m/s (y) at body/liquid mass ratios 0.1 / 1 / 10 over 8 ticks, against 1.3 / 6.4 / 9.8 kg*m/s exchanged. Body+liquid kinetic energy peaks at 1.12x the initial total at ratio 10; body energy alone stays within 1.01x, so the P2b gate passes. Root cause (measured): grid_to_matter_body.wgsl, the D29 push-out, removes the inward normal velocity of points inside a body, and nothing adds that momentum to the reaction sum. With the removal disabled the residual drops to -0.18 / -3.9 / -5.1, so it accounts for about 2/3. The remaining third is unexplained; one suspect is the test pairing body row n with liquid stats n-1. Fix shape: add m*v_n*normal from the push-out to the same per-body reaction words (the 16-word accumulator) that node.matter_body_reaction writes. Blocked on codegen: generate_standalone_buffer rejects a buffer atom with several outputs where one is atomic (standalone.rs, "Multi-output atomic"). Splitting the push-out into its own atom needs the same shape. Priority is low while MPM water is test-scene only (FFT_WATER_SOLVER_DESIGN.md).
close_reason: landed

title: Research: FFT pressure split for particle liquids (Dodd-Ferrante + APIC/MPM) - stability maths
description:
Research thread with Peter, 2026-09-30. No code; maths first.

Idea: particle liquid (APIC/MPM particles carry momentum + material) with pressure as ONE FFT/DCT solve per step via the Dodd-Ferrante constant-coefficient split (rho0 = min density, air simulated as a real light phase), solids as Brinkman drag masks. Nobody found combining particles with the split (CFD uses smooth interfaces; graphics solvers skip air).

Findings so far (frozen-density, pressure-only reduced model; scripts were throwaway):
- Guess error recurrence e+ = mu(2e - e_prev), mu = 1-1/r: stable (Cifani 2019), fades over ~2r steps.
- It rings: period ~2*pi*sqrt(r) steps (~200 at 1000:1); smooth motion at that rhythm gives pressure error ~sqrt(r) x pressure. Frame flicker is NOT amplified.
- Damped guess p~ = p + beta(p - p_prev), beta = 1 - 2/sqrt(r): no ringing, fades in ~sqrt(r) steps, worst error ~1x, slow motion ~10x worse.
- Waterbed: mean ln|H| over all rhythms = ln(1-1/r) for every beta (Jensen/Bode). No past-only predictor beats it; only exact info about the current frame helps (e.g. column-sum hydrostatic pressure).
- Precision: FP32 cancellation ~r*eps at 1000:1 (Astra). Fix: delta form, solve (1/rho0) lap delta = div u*/dt - div((1/rho) grad p~), u = u* - dt[(1/rho) grad p~ + (1/rho0) grad delta]. Optional float-float for the residual.
- Adaptive per-Fourier-wave predictor (LPC-style; Kolmogorov-Szego bound) is a candidate, stability unchecked.

Next: 2D planar-interface model including velocity update + interface advection (Astra: pressure error only partly becomes velocity error via the projection), then check whether ringing survives. Sources: Dodd & Ferrante JCP 2014; Cifani JCP 2019; Jain ACDI 2021.
notes:
Astra review 2026-09-30 (Codex session 01a0ef9e-27af-7183-bee9-050425a61494, verified ran): ringing confirmed at pressure level (peak mu/(1-mu)^1.5, 31.6 at r=1000) but it is a steady sinusoidal gain, and in uniform density the projection hides it from velocity entirely; only at the interface (grad(a0-a) x grad e) can it drive real velocity error, gain unknown -> 2D coupled model is the real test. Exact critical beta = (1-r^-0.5)/(1+r^-0.5) (0.939 at 1000); lighter modes still ring; beta<1 makes the guess first-order. Flicker pressure-error gain per unit P is ~1 (not amplified, not damped). Waterbed holds only for fixed stable LTI filters (mean log|H| = log mu + exterior zeros); adaptive/nonlinear predictors and real (non-flat) spectra can do much better, so the LPC idea is not ruled out. Delta form correct but not a full roundoff fix. Visual verdict: potentially lively, FLIP-equivalent detail unproven (dense air memory, air drag on splashes per MultiFLIP, diffuse interface limits thin sheets). Candidate memory fixes: shrink-wrap FFT box; wavelet or fast-multipole solve of the constant-coefficient split equation.
2D model result 2026-09-30 (scratch scripts, 32x32 MAC tank, periodic x FFT + DCT walls, float64, linearised momentum, semi-Lagrangian phi, exact sparse solve vs split, same everything else; validated: wave period 32+-1 half-steps vs 32 predicted, both solvers exact to 1e-11, split converges dt^2 at r=100). Raw split at interactive steps (16-64 steps per wave period) is ~100% wrong (vel/surface error 1-2x) at BOTH r=100 and 1000; stable, not blowing up. <5% needs ~400 steps/period at r=100, extrapolated ~1500 at r=1000 (MPM-level substeps). Ringing reaches velocity modestly: r=1000 vel error peaks 2.9 at 128 steps/period (ring 199) vs 1.3 at 64, 0.7 at 400. Critical beta flattens error to ~1 everywhere (waterbed confirmed coupled). Column-sum hydrostatic guess makes it WORSE (blows up 10-3000x at coarse steps): exact only for flat surfaces, injects wrong sideways pressure on sloped ones -> idea dead as stated. Open: cheap corrective solves (FFT-preconditioned Krylov, ~sqrt(r) iters), heavier fake air.
Ratio sweep (raw split, beta=1, 32 / 64 steps per wave swing): r=2 1.6%/0.4%, r=5 13%/3%, r=10 41%/10%, r=30 142%/43%. Only usable near r<=5 at show-speed steps -> liquid-liquid effects (oil on water, lava lamp, ink layers), not water in air. Damping the guess cannot fix it (waterbed).
FFT-preconditioned CG on the true variable-density equation (2D tank, random rhs): iterations to 1% / 0.01%: r=10 8/15, r=100 25/47, r=1000 82-86/136-158; SAME at N=32 and N=64 (resolution-independent, ~sqrt(r) scaling). Next lead: drop air entirely (free surface, p=0, ratio -> infinity) and solve the odd-shaped water domain with FFT on the box + surface-only correction: capacitance matrix method (Buzbee-Dorr-George-Golub 1971) / kernel-free boundary integral method (Ying & Henriquez JCP 2007); second-kind formulation should give bounded iterations independent of grid (literature claim, unverified). Surface points could come from the existing fluid mesher. Loses bubbles.
Free-surface (air dropped, p=0) naive test: GMRES + whole-box FFT/DCT helper, masked 5-point Laplacian. Passes to 1% / 0.01%: N=32 23/41, N=64 38/65, N=128 63/101 (~1.6x per doubling, ~N^0.7) -> NOT flat. Two separate drops changed nothing. The flat-count claim belongs to the second-kind boundary-integral formulation (KFBIM, Ying & Henriquez 2007), not this naive masked version. Next: derive/implement the second-kind version on the grid (consult Astra on formulation first).
Free surface over moving wave, tol 1e-3, passes per frame (plain / warm start / edge-band exact local fix / both): N=32 35/38/28/27, N=64 63/72/54/61, N=128 132/119/112/110. Count ~doubles per grid doubling; warm start ~useless (first-order p=0 boundary flips cells air<->water each frame, so the equation jumps exactly where the hard part is; ghost-fluid subcell boundary (Gibou/Enright 2002) would make it change smoothly); edge-band fix only 15-20% (FFT helper is wrong over the whole air region, not just the edge). Known graphics baseline to beat: multigrid-preconditioned CG with free surface (McAdams et al. 2010), roughly flat counts. Candidates: second-kind boundary integral (KFBIM) or accept multigrid as the core.
Astra consult 3 (Codex thread 01a0ef9e..., turn 01a0efce-c2c3-7153-8ece-318db4d99d33, verified ran). Diagnosis: box-FFT helper lets pressure extend harmonically into air; planar symbol of the preconditioned masked operator lambda(k) = 1/(1-g^2) ~ 1/(2|k|h), g+1/g = 2+(kh)^2 -> long surface wavelengths get O(1/h) eigenvalues; local band fix cannot reach them. Air-phase case stays h-independent because a_min L <= A_rho <= a_max L on the same domain (kappa <= r). Ranked: (1) second-kind double-layer surface solve evaluated with box FFTs (KFBI Ying-Henriquez 2007; Leathers-Guy arXiv 2203.12126 report mesh-independent counts); novelty = discrete flux-compatible version consistent with the particle/grid divergence incl. subcell surfaces. (2) exact capacitance solve on a one-cell air collar, S = J G J^T, planar symbol ~1/(2|k|), preconditioned by 2 sqrt(-Lap_surface) via tangent-plane FFT patches + component coarse modes + near-contact coupling (combination possibly new). (3) learned correction to the second-kind inverse, speculative. Decisive test for both: 2D rounded strip, FP32, N=32..256, fixed physical thickness then 4-cell sheets, subcell translations; FFT applications to 1e-3 true post-projection divergence. Kill if counts grow on fixed geometry or thin sheets need many tens.
Capacitance test (Astra option 2), 2D, flat periodic surfaces, one-cell air collar + constant, GMRES, box FFT/DCT pseudo-inverse; verified against sparse masked solve. tol 1e-6 passes (no surface FFT / with sqrt(-Lap_row+q0^2) surface FFT): water layer N=32..256: 11,14,16,18 / 8,8,8,7 (FLAT); 4-cell floating sheet: 15,20,25,31 / 9,11,16,22 (grows: paired close surfaces, needs near-contact coupling); fixed-thickness sheet at tol 1e-3 flat 5-6. True masked residual 1e-7..5e-6, max err vs reference <=2e-6. FP32 FFT at 256 sheet4 tol1e-3 same counts as f64. Scripts in session scratchpad (capacitance.py). Untested: curved/wavy surfaces (needs FFT along curve / tangent patches), drops, folds, 3D, timing. Next: wavy surface + separate drop.
Free-surface sloshing sim (air removed), capacitance + surface FFT helper (column-summed |k| scaling + local within-column term; the column-only helper was singular and falsely converged at 11% error). N=64: 9.2 passes/frame avg (8-11) to 1e-6, true residual <=2.4e-6, surfaces identical to exact at 4 decimals; old plain helper 32.3 to 1e-3. N=128: 11.3 avg (8-18), residual <=5.9e-6, surface gap 1e-4 (0.2% of wave); old helper 41.1. Slight growth on wavy surfaces -> the column-summed helper is crude for slopes; a proper along-the-curve surface FFT is the next refinement. Viewer: https://claude.ai/artifact/1nvDRAGrQTTVYbm8KTEA6H
3D capacitance (cap3d.py): box FFT x,z + DCT y, collar sources + constant, helper = per-(x,z)-column sum scaled by sqrt(-Lap_surf+q0^2) via 2D FFT + local within-column term; 8 frames of a 3D standing wave, tol 1e-6, true masked 7-point residual checked. Wave: N=32/64/96 -> 10.1/10.4/10.2 passes per frame (FLAT), residual <=1.1e-6. Wave + two floating drops: 17.5/22.0/25.1 (grows): column-summed helper lumps the drop and the main surface in one column. Next: per-component surface helper (drops as their own pieces), then GPU FFT timing on M4 Max.
3D sim demo (sim3d.py, 40^3, 160 steps, pool + falling drop, semi-Lagrangian velocity + phi, capacitance + surface FFT pressure every step to 1e-6): passes/step mean 12.0 (8-21; ~20 while the drop is airborne, ~10 after it lands), worst true residual 1.6e-6. Demo transport loses ~1% water (semi-Lagrangian phi), not the solver. Viewer section added to https://claude.ai/artifact/1nvDRAGrQTTVYbm8KTEA6H
Particle (PIC/FLIP 0.97) 3D demos, 40^3, ~206k particles, capacitance pressure every step: (a) flat still pool + drop: drop falls at true gravity (0.787 vs 0.790 predicted at step 10), plunges and pool rebounds, 15.2 passes/step avg (11-22), residual <=1.9e-6. Earlier grid-phi demo was wrong (drop fell at 1/3 g and smeared out: semi-Lagrangian averaging with air). (b) asymmetric: collapsing corner column + drop thrown sideways, 200 steps: 20.0 avg (12-26), residual <=4.3e-6; more separate pieces -> more passes (column-summed helper). Tank wraps in x,z (no side walls yet; DCT in x,z would add walls). GPU-drop-in notes: GPU MPM design (docs/GPU_MPM_SOLVER_DESIGN.md:117,125) records an earlier MAC projection prototype (mac_* primitives, water_mac_* proofs, 2.06 ms/projection with 96 SOR pairs on 32x8x32) - reusable for MAC div/grad; MPM grid is node-based, the tested projection is MAC.
GPU (MLX 0.32.3 Metal FFT, float32, scratch venv; surface GMRES + helper on CPU): wave 9 passes at every size 32..256^3. Measured per pass (incl. scatter/gather/sync): 64^3 0.77 ms, 96^3 1.58, 128^3 2.15, 192^3 5.58, 256^3 13.3; whole solve (Python + CPU Krylov overhead) 18.6 / 19.6 / 32 / 80 / 189 ms; float32 residual 3e-5..6e-4. Breakdown: pure FFT round trip 64^3 0.42 ms, 128^3 1.30, 256^3 4.69; y-mirror (DCT substitute) doubles 256^3 to 10.3; scatter ~0.2-0.4, gather+CPU copy ~0.15. Projection with real DCT + GPU-side Krylov: ~1.5 ms/pass at 128^3 -> ~13 ms at 9 passes (1e-6), ~7 ms at ~5 passes (1e-3); 256^3 ~5 ms/pass. Earlier 3-5 ms at 128^3 estimate was optimistic. Drop case 128^3: 22 passes. Lit search (agent): combination not found (~75% conf); closest: Ying-Henriquez KFBI 2007 / Leathers-Guy IBDL; Buzbee-Dorr-George-Golub 1971, OLeary-Widlund 1979 capacitance; Arioli-Loghin 2008 sqrt Steklov-Poincare preconditioner; Liu-Mitchell-Aanjaneya-Sifakis TOG 2016 Schur/FFT liquid (CPU). No killer paper; untested: thin sheets, splash crowns, droplet clouds.
128^3 full GPU step (sim3d_mlx.py, MLX, ~6M particles, PIC/FLIP 0.97, collapsing column + thrown drop, 400 steps, tol 1e-4): passes/step mean 29.9 (20-43), Python-driven step median 254 ms. Pass count rises with splash fragmentation at higher res (column-summed helper; per-piece helper is the fix). Viewer option added (zlib bitmask frames).

Research record: docs/FFT_CAPACITANCE_PRESSURE_FINDINGS.md. Scripts attached to viewer https://claude.ai/artifact/1nvDRAGrQTTVYbm8KTEA6H under scripts/. Next: per-piece surface helper (Python).

- Oracle (exact per-patch inverse): drops 12/12/11 passes at N=20/28/36 (flat) while helper grows 16/18/25. Growth = helper fault; inter-surface coupling = flat tax (~4 far-drop patterns, 10-12 close drop, rank constant with N).
- Coarse correction with per-piece mean+slopes or even the true coupling eigenvectors does not help the helper (makes it worse); oracle only 12->9.
- Next: per-surface helper that follows each surface (overlapping charts, separate opposing sheets), per Astra.

- 24 passes: 82 ms/frame, true residual max 3.1%.
- Still pool (20 cells deep): max particle speed < 0.5 mm/s after 2 s, true residual 4e-5. MPM fails this gate.
- MLX DCT costs ~2x a real transform; engine estimate ~6-7 ms/step.

- equal median error ~6e-3: FFT 24 passes 20.0 ms vs MG 8 iters 31.3 ms (1.57x)
- ~2.5e-4: FFT 32 30.8 ms vs MG 12 47.2 ms (1.53x); ~1e-1: FFT 16 11.6 vs MG 4 16.0 (1.4x)

Passes to 1e-6 at 32/64/96: drops 15.0/15.8/16.5 (column 17.5/22.0/25.1), tower 16.8/19.5/20.5 (column 21.2/29.1/32.0), wave 10.9/11.1 (column 10.1/10.4). Next: port to the MLX Dam Break and rerun the multigrid race.

At 31 ms: charts 1.1e-3 vs multigrid 7.6e-3. Astra consulted on helper cost, node-grid Q1-P0 seam, fair benchmark.

2026-09-30 node<->face transfer oracle (transfer_check.py, N=24, exact sparse face solve, MPM-style nodes with walls on nodes): divergence left relative to before: correction bridge 1.3e-1; replace bridge 9.7e-2 but keeps only 0.58 of node speed; correction bridge iterated 2/4/8 solves 7.0e-2/4.2e-2/2.4e-2. 2026-09-30 SWASH P0 on feat/fft-water (c0f772616..99f6423cb): engine 3D FFT + one-FFT cosine transform, box solve 0.39-0.47 ms at 64^3, 1.07-1.18 ms at 128^3 (quiet GPU). Rejected with numbers: MINRES in place of GMRES (1.5-2x more passes), direct per-axis cosine sum (1.3 ms at 64^3), naive workgroup FFT kernel (0.51 / 2.20 ms). title: Measure Blob V2 transient allocation events and detector-only retained bytes
description: The 1080p Blob V2 release proof records app tick/GPU timing, detector worker duration, readback age, fixed-lag wait, process malloc-zone retained bytes/blocks, and GPU allocated bytes. The native benchmark also records malloc-zone net live blocks. Neither path counts transient allocation events or isolates retained detector state from other app/OpenCV allocations. Add a bounded, nonintrusive allocation-event counter for the native detector and report detector-only retained bytes at default 320/8 and stress 1024/32 without changing the audio/render hot path.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible bounded benchmark reports median/p95/max detector call time, transient allocation-event count after warmup, and detector-only retained bytes for both default and stress cases; the numbers are not inferred from net live malloc-zone blocks.

title: p4a-demo-probe-indexed-quad-uv-anomaly
description: Demo-lane probe anomaly (k3-demo-artifact-backlog, 2026-09-17): in the P4a emissive coverage probe, the indexed quads SECOND triangle reports debug-query UV (0.162, 0.496) where the probe oracle expects centroid UV (0.333, 0.667); reverse-solved barycentrics place the sample off the ray aim. Entries 0 (indexed first tri) and 2 match the oracle exactly. Landed proofs are green: rt_dynamic_shading section 4 asserts indexed UV/normal with a scrambled index order at 2e-4, and the A4 emissive sections assert per-corner indexed UV fetch. Suspect the demo probes oracle (winding/order assumption), not the GPU path — but unverified. Fix shape: reproduce the probe against the P4b-landed code, diff the oracle winding against the fixture index buffer; if the GPU path is truly wrong, the failing case is tri 2 of the indexed quad in the emissive candidate table. Evidence: /tmp/manifold-rt-dynamic/23ee5ff39/DEMOS.md gap 3.
close_reason: Root-caused by reading, no repro needed. Real GPU bug, already fixed by P4b (f2df14b0e). Pre-P4b fetch_interpolated_uv in shadow_rays.msl ignored the index buffer (flat math v=primitive_id*3+i, git show 23ee5ff39:...shadow_rays.msl lines 769-777). Demo fixture tri 0 indices were (0,1,2) so flat math coincidentally matched the oracle; tri 1 read out-of-bounds vertices 4,5 producing uv=(0.162,0.496) instead of centroid (1/3,2/3). The flat small-triangle object matched because its tri 0 is flat-layout. P4b replaced the fetch with the shared rt_index_at helper (used by both debug_ray_query fetch and emissive gather, shadow_rays.msl lines 634-636 and 800-802) and landed rt_dynamic_shading section 4: scrambled-index quad (3,0,1) asserting indexed UV/normal via debug query at 2e-4 plus a flat-would-differ assert. Gate re-run at main 90756f831: rt_dynamic_shading PASS.

title: Layer-skin GPU proof can fail on a single wall-clock timing spike
description: During reversed-Z landing at d551750a9, the full GPU suite had one timing failure: mutual_skin_two_layers_render_300_frames steady max 27.46ms vs 20ms budget, avg 0.48ms. It passed in the earlier full run and unchanged isolated rerun: max 0.59ms, avg 0.33ms. All correctness checks passed. Investigate a robust proof policy for transient scheduler/GPU contention without hiding genuine steady-state regressions. No threshold change made.
notes: Reproduced 2026-10-01 on plain main d15d4bf17 (GPU idle apart from other agents queued): mutual_skin_two_layers_render_300_frames steady max 3388.88 ms, avg 12.06 ms over 290 frames; same ~3.15 s single-frame spike on the batch tree alone (3157 ms) and in the scoped landing gate (3146 ms). Not noise-sized: a consistent ~3 s stall in steady state, so a real stall (pipeline compile or GPU wait) not jitter. Logs: /tmp/land-skin-main.log, /tmp/land-batch-skin-alone.log. The sibling skin_tracks_source_content_and_missing_id_falls_back failed once in the gate with a black capture (0 vs 0) and passed alone.
close_reason: Two harness causes, no product bug. (1) Stall: render_scene compiles the cel MSAA pipeline on first draw (3729 ms measured), on the frame the async GLB parse lands (frame 44/105); the test only exempted frames 0-9. The app prewarms these pipelines at startup and pre-rolls loads. (2) Black capture in skin_tracks_source_content: the probe ran fixed frames without waiting for the background GLB parse, so the model was never drawn. Fix: both tests pre-roll on warmup_pending plus Complete frame status; the 20 ms wall-clock budget became per-frame Complete/no-reload value checks. gpu_scope now maps preset_runtime/ and layer_skin.rs to these lib proofs. Branch fix/layer-skin-tests.

title: Qualify inherited RT material parity boundaries
description: Static source audit during scene-modifier RT design found existing material limitations: shadow_rays.msl omits nonemissive KHR UV transforms (around552), ignores authored TANGENT.w (478), samples mask texture alpha nearest/repeat without material alpha factor (586); RtNormalSource normal matrix uses a documented nonuniform-scale approximation (params.rs325); raster shadow_depth.wgsl lacks base-color alpha-mask sampling. These are documented existing boundaries, not newly reproduced runtime regressions. Kept separate from current-frame modifier geometry implementation to avoid silently claiming raster/RT material parity. Reuse existing BUG-wytp, BUG-wfxe and BUG-1gqt history when designing focused follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded numeric reproductions establish each discrepancy; separately approved fixes use shared material/index/appearance helpers and preserve current modifier RT same-frame contract. No claim of visual qualification without observed render.
notes:
2026-09-26 BUG-5l4o implementation (0e30b43dd, landing pending) resolves the inherited transform/alpha/normal issues: UV0/UV1 with per-map transforms/addressing, authored tangent handedness, inverse-transpose normals, alpha factor times texture and vertex color, matching raster cutouts. Focused numeric GPU proofs pass. Remaining hybrid capability boundary is explicit in GLTF_MATERIAL_EXTENSIONS_DESIGN section 7: secondary hits omit coat/sheen/iridescence/SSS/full Phong-Cel and punctual specular; glass/Blend absent from acceleration; mip0 ray-hit sampling lacks ray cones; anisotropic env and secondary lighting remain approximations. Track full parity as later renderer work, never claim it from current geometry/material fixes.
Peter explicitly requested glass and secondary ray-tracing fixes on 2026-09-26. Active repair branch codex/material-render-polish: extend secondary material payload/shading and full punctual lighting, verify observed renders. Previous capability limits are unfinished work, not acceptance.
2026-09-26: glass/secondary-material repair landed and pushed at 6c68c9008 (branch tip 9e26a9837). Secondary hits now evaluate clearcoat, sheen, iridescence, mapped anisotropy/specular and full punctual-light/environment inputs. Closed glass front-surface visibility fixed; corrected Suzanne render inspected. Dark-light motion is byte-inert without changing stable caster slots; overflow/live toggles pass. Required landing gate 7 passed, 0 failed, including full GPU suite. Remaining hybrid limits stay open: glass/Blend outside RT acceleration, secondary SSS/full Phong-Cel, ray-hit mip selection, recursive specular/nested dielectric transport; see current material contract.

title: neighbor_smooth fused-tail numerical proof
description: Residual from BUG-x72p (scene-mirror-blocked-gather-input-fusion) landing: neighbor_smooth unfused dispatch is min(grid_size^2, capacity) — param-driven. Root cause: crates/manifold-core/src/flatten.rs:404 returns Ok(Producer::Unconnected) when a passthrough group input has no upstream wire, and flatten.rs:354 matches (Unconnected, Concrete(_)) as a no-op. title: Water dt-halving gate: trajectory divergence evidence needs Astra ruling
description: WATER_SIMULATION_DESIGN section 5 gate, S4 evidence. Default pool AND bounded impact fixture at dt/2 diverge from dt at trajectory level: t=2s mean position delta ~5.2e-2 m, max ~2.0e-1 m, density rel delta ~0.31, settling |v| ~0.35 m/s. Refinement probe t=0.5s: |dt-dt/2| 8.9e-3 m vs |dt/2-dt/4| 1.1e-2 m (ratio 0.79 — deltas do not shrink under refinement). Solver stable: zero fault bits over 960 substeps, interior density median ~995 / p95 ~1037 vs rest 1000, velocities bounded. Diagnosis: nearly undamped formulation sustains physical slosh whose phase diverges between resolutions; not tuned per lane contract. water_timestep_halving_stability (tests/gpu_proofs/water_solver.rs) records evidence, asserts hard invariants only; acceptance thresholds await Astra/Peter. Suspects if formulation changes: c0/EOS stiffness, grid-update dissipation, seed equilibration transient.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Slot-7 review/fix follow-up (2026-09-10): numerical acceptance remains open. Fresh Metal measurements after the integration/geometry fixes: at 0.5 s mean trajectory differences are 7.459 mm (dt vs dt/2) and 10.67 mm (dt/2 vs dt/4), refinement ratio 0.70. Pool 2 s max/mean position delta 147.5/41.93 mm, max relative density delta 0.2368, mean settling speed 0.2894 m/s. Impact results are comparable. The tests pass finite/bounded/no-fault invariants but do not enforce timestep agreement. Static comparison found transfer formulas consistent with the existing f64 reference; that does not establish convergence. No evidence yet establishes slosh phase as the sole cause. No formulation or acceptance tolerances were changed. Lead decision: keep this as a release blocker; do not land or claim complete physical validation on the strength of the green diagnostic tests. Next work needs a bounded numerical investigation and justified acceptance criterion, not cosmetic damping or relaxed thresholds.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text:
APIC replacement remains blocked; production MLS-MPM and rendering unchanged.

Reviewed independent f64 trilinear MAC/APIC and fractional pressure references pass their focused checks. Pressure now includes the pinned FLIP Fluids cell-volume correction for non-divergence-free solid velocity extensions. The coupled wave fixture revealed coarse-grid dispersion and tangential drag from zero-valued solid sampling ghosts. A static aligned-box free-slip reflection improves the h=0.03125 m result: period 1.45614 s vs theory 1.47462 s; later peak envelope 96.7%. Normalized waveform differences at 60→120 and 120→240 Hz are 2.42% and 3.45%. Both meet the original 10% agreement bound, but the additional monotonic-refinement acceptance test fails. It failed before and after the wall correction, so further physics experiments stopped at the two-failure limit. The earlier 5% retention claim was a phase-confounded sample, not a peak measurement.

MAC scatter/resolve/extrapolation drafts pass eight WGSL/ABI unit checks and renderer clippy (including the GPU-proof target). Native parity cannot run: Naga 28 SPIR-V translation panics in block.rs:3369 with 'Expression [97] is not cached' before dispatch. Removed module/startup/proof registrations to leave app runtime unchanged; drafts remain in slot-7. No new GPU pressure/advection integration, moving-object proof, full acceptance, performance claim or video.

Next diagnosis should compare the same wave fixture against the complete pinned upstream engine before further solver changes, and isolate the native shader-translation panic. Do not land main or represent this as an accepted solver. Contract and slot-7 WORKTREE_HANDOFF.md record scope and recovery commands.
